name: CoinGecko Onchain Token Price
description: Query the latest onchain DEX price plus optional market-cap, 24h volume, 24h price change, and total reserve for one (or comma-separated several) ERC-20/SPL token contract addresses on a given network, using CoinGecko's onchain (GeckoTerminal) data. First-party CoinGecko x402 endpoint.

usage.callShape: GET https://pro-api.coingecko.com/api/v3/x402/onchain/simple/networks/{network}/token_price/{contract_address}. {network} is a CoinGecko onchain network slug (e.g. base, eth, monad, solana). {contract_address} is a single token contract address path segment (multiple addresses may be comma-separated in the same segment). All other input is OPTIONAL boolean query params: include_market_cap, mcap_fdv_fallback, include_24hr_vol, include_24hr_price_change, include_total_reserve_in_usd, include_inactive_source. No request body. Pays $0.01 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453) or Solana.
usage.outputShape: data.id, data.type (="simple_token_price"), data.attributes.token_prices.<address>, data.attributes.market_cap_usd.<address>, data.attributes.h24_volume_usd.<address>, data.attributes.h24_price_change_percentage.<address>, data.attributes.total_reserve_in_usd.<address>, data.attributes.last_trade_timestamp.<address>. All attribute maps are keyed by the (lowercased) contract address; market_cap/volume/etc keys only appear when their include_* query flag was set.
quirks: Per-address values can be null OR empty-string OR "0.0" for thinly-traded / untracked tokens — this is a valid 200 response, NOT an error. Verified live: address 0x00c9c681d803d27d9c2e1e8612de073db0c5c390 on Base returned token_prices=null, market_cap_usd=null, h24_price_change_percentage="", h24_volume_usd="0.0", total_reserve_in_usd="65.156...". Callers MUST handle null/empty.
Numeric values are returned as STRINGS, not numbers (e.g. "2289.33"), and total_reserve_in_usd can have very high precision.
All input is path segments + optional query flags; there is NO request body and no query param is required.

Response attribute keys are keyed by the contract address (lowercased); the market_cap_usd / h24_volume_usd / h24_price_change_percentage / total_reserve_in_usd / last_trade_timestamp maps only appear if the matching include_* flag is passed.

The default Base example address (0x00c9c681...) is essentially price-less; use a liquid token (e.g. WETH 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 on base, or WETH 0xc02aaa39... on eth) for a meaningful demo.
Second backend URL ends in literal ':address' — that is an unresolved path template, not a real address; substitute a real contract address before calling.
usage.guide: Query the latest onchain DEX price plus optional market-cap, 24h volume, 24h price change, and total reserve for one (or comma-separated several) ERC-20/SPL token contract addresses on a given network, using CoinGecko's onchain (GeckoTerminal) data. First-party CoinGecko x402 endpoint. GET https://pro-api.coingecko.com/api/v3/x402/onchain/simple/networks/{network}/token_price/{contract_address}. {network} is a CoinGecko onchain network slug (e.g. base, eth, monad, solana). {contract_address} is a single token contract address path segment (multiple addresses may be comma-separated in the same segment). All other input is OPTIONAL boolean query params: include_market_cap, mcap_fdv_fallback, include_24hr_vol, include_24hr_price_change, include_total_reserve_in_usd, include_inactive_source. No request body. Pays $0.01 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453) or Solana. Output: data.id, data.type (="simple_token_price"), data.attributes.token_prices.<address>, data.attributes.market_cap_usd.<address>, data.attributes.h24_volume_usd.<address>, data.attributes.h24_price_change_percentage.<address>, data.attributes.total_reserve_in_usd.<address>, data.attributes.last_trade_timestamp.<address>. All attribute maps are keyed by the (lowercased) contract address; market_cap/volume/etc keys only appear when their include_* query flag was set.

name: CoinMarketCap Quotes
description: CoinMarketCap real-time price quotes and market data for one or more cryptocurrencies by symbol, slug or CMC ID. Pay-per-call x402.

id.description: One or more comma-separated CoinMarketCap cryptocurrency IDs. Example: "1,1027".

slug.description: One or more comma-separated cryptocurrency slugs. Example: "bitcoin,ethereum".

symbol.description: One or more comma-separated cryptocurrency symbols. Example: "BTC,ETH".

convert.description: Optionally calculate market quotes in up to 120 currencies by passing a comma-separated list. Default: "USD".

convert_id.description: Optionally calculate market quotes by CoinMarketCap ID instead of symbol.

aux.description: Comma-separated list of supplemental data fields: num_market_pairs, cmc_rank, date_added, tags, platform, max_supply, circulating_supply, total_supply, is_active, is_fiat.

skip_invalid.description: Pass true to relax request validation and skip any invalid IDs/symbols.

usage.callShape: GET https://pro-api.coinmarketcap.com/x402/v3/cryptocurrency/quotes/latest?symbol=BTC (or ?slug=bitcoin or ?id=1). Params go in the URL query string; no JSON body. Pays $0.01 USDC via x402 on Base.
usage.outputShape: body.data[] is an array of matching coins; price at body.data[i].quote[0].price (USD), with body.data[i].quote[0].percent_change_24h, .market_cap, .volume_24h. Coin identity at body.data[i].id/name/symbol/slug/cmc_rank. body.status.credit_count = credits used.
quirks: Params are query-string on a GET, not a JSON body.

Querying by symbol returns ALL tokens sharing that ticker (symbol=BTC returned 14 entries; real Bitcoin is the one with id=1 / slug=bitcoin / cmc_rank=1). For a precise single-token result query by slug (e.g. slug=bitcoin) or by CMC id (e.g. id=1) instead.
Must supply at least one of id / slug / symbol or the call has no target.
txHash not surfaced by the payment layer (confirmed=false) but the call did settle and return 200 with live data.
Pricing defaults to USD; pass convert=EUR,JPY etc. for other quote currencies (each adds a quote object under data[].quote).
usage.guide: Call GET https://pro-api.coinmarketcap.com/x402/v3/cryptocurrency/quotes/latest with the coin selector as a URL query param: prefer slug (e.g. ?slug=bitcoin) or id (e.g. ?id=1) for an unambiguous single result, since ?symbol=BTC returns every token using that ticker. The wallet auto-pays $0.01 USDC via x402 on Base; no API key needed. Read the price from body.data[0].quote[0].price (USD) and 24h change from body.data[0].quote[0].percent_change_24h. To match a coin from a symbol result, pick the entry with the matching slug/id (real Bitcoin = id 1, slug bitcoin, cmc_rank 1). Add convert=EUR (etc.) to get other fiat quotes.

name: Alchemy Token Prices
description: Alchemy Prices API — current USD price(s) for one or more tokens by ticker symbol (ETH, BTC, USDC, …). Pay-per-call x402 on Base.

usage.callShape: GET https://x402.alchemy.com/prices/v1/tokens/by-symbol?symbols=ETH (comma-separate multiple symbols, e.g. ?symbols=ETH,BTC,USDC)
usage.outputShape: body.data[] is an array of {symbol, prices[]}; each price is {currency, value, lastUpdatedAt}. USD price = body.data[0].prices[0].value (string).
quirks: URL requires a ?symbols= query param even though inputSchema is null — a bare GET would return no useful data; pass one or more tickers comma-separated (e.g. ?symbols=ETH or ?symbols=ETH,BTC,USDC)
Prices come back as STRINGS, not numbers (value:"1684.84")
Each token's prices is an array keyed by currency (currently just usd)
Pay confirmed:false in result but on-chain payment went through and 200 returned with live data — settlement is fine
usage.guide: Call GET https://x402.alchemy.com/prices/v1/tokens/by-symbol with a ?symbols= query string listing one or more ticker symbols (comma-separated for multiple, e.g. ?symbols=ETH,BTC). Pay via x402 USDC on Base ($0.001/call). Read prices from body.data[]: match by .symbol, then take .prices[0].value (a USD price string) and .prices[0].lastUpdatedAt for freshness. No auth or API key needed; payment is the only gate.

name: Dome Price Oracle
description: Fetch historical or most-recent crypto price for a currency pair from a chosen oracle source (Binance or Chainlink). With no start_time/end_time, returns only the single most recent price (limit auto-forced to 1). Supply a start_time+end_time range to get a time series (up to 100 points/page).

usage.callShape: GET https://x402.orth.sh/dome/crypto-prices/{binance|chainlink}?currency=<pair> (required: currency; optional: start_time, end_time [both Unix ms], limit [max 100], pagination_key). No body. x402 v1 on Base USDC, $0.01.
usage.outputShape: prices[].symbol, prices[].value (number USD), prices[].timestamp (Unix ms), total (int)
quirks: CURRENCY FORMAT DIFFERS PER BACKEND. binance: lowercase alphanumeric, NO separator (btcusdt, ethusdt, solusdt, xrpusdt). chainlink: slash-separated lowercase (btc/usd, eth/usd, sol/usd). Using the wrong format for the source will 4xx.
currency is REQUIRED; omitting it 4xx
With no start_time/end_time, limit is forced to 1 — you get ONLY the single most recent price regardless of any limit you pass
Provide BOTH start_time and end_time (Unix milliseconds) to get a historical series; default/max limit 100 per page
timestamp values are Unix MILLISECONDS
More results paginate via pagination_key (base64) returned in the response
x402 v1 endpoint (no v2 accepts array) — agentcash/MCP fetch rejects it with parse_payment_required; pay via qa-pay or a v1-capable x402 client
Both sources return identical output shape; chainlink value carries full float precision (e.g. 61730.81628466482), binance is rounded (e.g. 61792.59)
usage.guide: Fetch historical or most-recent crypto price for a currency pair from a chosen oracle source (Binance or Chainlink). With no start_time/end_time, returns only the single most recent price (limit auto-forced to 1). Supply a start_time+end_time range to get a time series (up to 100 points/page). GET https://x402.orth.sh/dome/crypto-prices/{binance|chainlink}?currency=<pair> (required: currency; optional: start_time, end_time [both Unix ms], limit [max 100], pagination_key). No body. x402 v1 on Base USDC, $0.01. Output: prices[].symbol, prices[].value (number USD), prices[].timestamp (Unix ms), total (int)

name: Solana RPC
description: Solana JSON-RPC passthrough — make any Solana RPC method call, pay-per-request over x402 (no node or API key).

usage.callShape: POST https://blockrun.ai/api/v1/solana/rpc with JSON body {jsonrpc:"2.0", id:1, method:"<solanaRpcMethod>", params:[...]}
usage.outputShape: body.result (standard Solana JSON-RPC response shape: {jsonrpc, id, result}); UNVERIFIED — no successful paid call completed
quirks: Price is sub-cent: $0.0005 (500 atomic USDC, 6 decimals) on Base eip155:8453. The qa-pay primitive's payment was rejected by BlockRun's facilitator with invalidReason='amount_too_low' and NOTHING was paid (paid:false, costUsd:0, no txHash). The $0.0005 amount is below what the current pay tooling settles as valid.

Endpoint itself is alive: returns a well-formed x402 v2 402 with a correct accepts array (scheme=exact, network=eip155:8453, amount=500, asset=USDC 0x833589..., payTo=0xe9030014F5DAe217d0A152f02A043567b16c1aBf).
It is a Solana JSON-RPC passthrough to public mainnet-beta. Body must include jsonrpc, id, method (params optional). Billed $0.0005 per call or per element of a JSON-RPC batch.
Did NOT retry after the amount_too_low rejection — re-paying would hit the same sub-cent floor and risk loss with no upside.
usage.guide: POST a standard Solana JSON-RPC body {jsonrpc:"2.0", id:1, method:"getSlot"} (or any Solana RPC method, with optional params array) to https://blockrun.ai/api/v1/solana/rpc. The result comes back at body.result in standard JSON-RPC form. Payment is x402 USDC on Base at $0.0005/call (per element for batches). CAUTION: with the current QA pay tooling the payment was rejected as amount_too_low (sub-cent price below the settlement floor) and the call could not be completed — verify with a pay client that can settle 500-atomic-unit ($0.0005) amounts before relying on it.

name: Allium Explorer SQL Query
description: Run an arbitrary SQL query against Allium's multichain blockchain data warehouse (Explorer). Async 3-step flow: submit SQL, poll free status, then pay to fetch result rows. Supports crosschain tables (e.g. crosschain.metrics.overview, ethereum.blocks, etc.).

usage.callShape: STEP 1 (paid $0.01): POST /api/v1/explorer/queries/run-async with JSON body {"parameters":{"sql":"<SQL>"}} -> returns {"run_id":"..."}. STEP 2 (FREE): GET /api/v1/explorer/query-runs/{run_id}/status -> returns a bare JSON string, poll until it equals "success" (goes "queued"/"running"->"success"). STEP 3 (paid $0.22): GET (or POST) /api/v1/explorer/query-runs/{run_id}/results -> returns the rows.
usage.outputShape: run-async: {run_id}. status: bare JSON string e.g. "success". results: {sql, data:[{<row cols>}], meta:{columns:[{name,data_type}], row_count, run_id}, queried_at}
quirks: Async 3-step flow. run-async ONLY submits and returns {run_id} — it does NOT return rows.
Body shape is {"parameters":{"sql":"..."}} — SQL goes inside parameters.sql, NOT at top level.
Status endpoint GET /query-runs/{run_id}/status is FREE/unprotected and returns a BARE JSON STRING. Terminal success value is "success" (NOT "succeeded" as prior docs claimed). Poll until "success".
Results cost $0.22 USDC (220000 micro-units), NOT ~$0.01. A FULL query therefore costs ~$0.23 total ($0.01 submit + $0.22 results) — prior docs under-stated this ~10x.
Results endpoint accepts BOTH GET and POST at /query-runs/{run_id}/results (both $0.22). Submit uses /queries/run-async but status+results use /query-runs/{run_id}/... (different path prefix).
The service auto-appends 'LIMIT 10000' to your SQL (observed: 'SELECT 1 AS x' became 'SELECT 1 AS x LIMIT 10000').
Accepts USDC on Base (eip155:8453), Solana, X Layer (eip155:196), and Tempo (mpp).
qa-pay txHash came back null on the submit step (paid:true, confirmed:false) but the run_id was valid and results were retrievable — settlement is fine, just no hash surfaced on that flow.

usage.callShape: POST /api/v1/developer/wallet/transactions with a JSON ARRAY body: [{"chain":"ethereum","address":"0x..."}]. Returns rows synchronously (no polling).

inputExample._note: The ACTUAL request body is the array under 'body' sent as the JSON root: [{"chain":"ethereum","address":"0x..."}]. The _root_is_array/_note keys are documentation-only and must NOT be sent.

usage.outputShape: {items:[{id, type, address, chain, hash, index, within_block_order_key, block_timestamp, block_number, block_hash, fee:{raw_amount,amount_str,amount}, fee_currency, labels:[], from_address, to_address, asset_transfers:[{transfer_type, operation, transaction_hash, log_index, from_address, to_address, asset:{type,address,name,symbol,decimals,token_id}, amount:{raw_amount,amount_str,amount}}], activities:[]}]}

A bare object {chain,address} returns HTTP 422 'Input should be a valid list'. The probe/openapi inputSchema describes a single object and is WRONG — the bazaar example body [{...}] is correct.
Supports multiple addresses in one call (array can have >1 entry).
chain values are lowercase strings: ethereum, solana, base, etc.
Output addresses are lowercased in the response.
Synchronous (no run_id / no polling) — unlike the Explorer SQL op.
$0.03 per call. Accepts USDC on Base, Solana, X Layer, and Tempo (mpp).

description: Fetch the receipt of a mined Ethereum transaction (eth_getTransactionReceipt): execution status, gas used, effective gas price, and emitted event logs. Mainnet or Sepolia. Keyless pay-per-call.

usage.callShape: GET https://skills.onesource.io/api/chain/receipt/{hash}?network=ethereum (hash = 0x-prefixed 64-hex tx hash in the URL path; network optional query, default ethereum, enum ethereum|sepolia; no request body; x402 USDC on Base or MPP on Tempo)
usage.outputShape: data.result.status (0x1=success/0x0=fail), data.result.gasUsed, data.result.cumulativeGasUsed, data.result.effectiveGasPrice, data.result.from, data.result.to, data.result.contractAddress, data.result.blockNumber, data.result.blockHash, data.result.transactionHash, data.result.transactionIndex, data.result.logs[], data.result.logsBloom; meta.endpoint, meta.request_id
quirks: Output is nested under data.result (NOT data directly).
All numeric fields are hex strings (e.g. status '0x1', gasUsed '0x5208', blockNumber '0xb443') - decode hex client-side.
hash path param is regex-validated ^0x[a-fA-F0-9]{64}$; malformed hashes 400 before any RPC call.
network query param defaults to ethereum; only ethereum|sepolia accepted.
Live RPC pass-through: an unknown/unmined hash returns null result rather than an error.
meta block in real responses only contained endpoint + request_id (no cost_usdc/payment_* despite OpenAPI advertising them).

name: OneSource Onchain Transaction Details
description: Fetch full Ethereum transaction details by hash (eth_getTransactionByHash): from, to, value, gas/gasPrice, nonce, input calldata, signature, and block placement. Returns BOTH the transaction AND its receipt in one call. Mainnet or Sepolia. Keyless pay-per-call.

usage.callShape: GET https://skills.onesource.io/api/chain/tx/{hash}?network=ethereum (hash = 0x-prefixed 64-hex tx hash in the URL path; network optional query, default ethereum, enum ethereum|sepolia; no request body; x402 USDC on Base or MPP on Tempo)
usage.outputShape: data.transaction.{from,to,value,nonce,gas,gasPrice,input,type,hash,blockNumber,blockHash,transactionIndex,r,s,v}, data.receipt.{status,gasUsed,cumulativeGasUsed,effectiveGasPrice,from,to,contractAddress,blockNumber,blockHash,transactionHash,transactionIndex,logs[],logsBloom}; meta.endpoint, meta.request_id
quirks: Returns BOTH data.transaction AND data.receipt objects in a single call (unlike the receipt-only endpoint which uses data.result).
Output nesting key is data.transaction (NOT data.result) plus data.receipt - different shape from the /receipt endpoint.
All numeric fields are hex strings (value '0x7a69', gas '0x5208', blockNumber '0xb443') - decode hex client-side.
hash path param is regex-validated ^0x[a-fA-F0-9]{64}$; malformed hashes 400 before any RPC call.
network query param defaults to ethereum; only ethereum|sepolia accepted.
Pricier ($0.008) than /receipt ($0.005) because it bundles tx + receipt.
meta block in real responses only contained endpoint + request_id (no cost_usdc/payment_* despite OpenAPI advertising them).
GET x402 endpoint - verify via agentcash fetch (qa-pay can stall on GET x402).
usage.guide: Fetch full Ethereum transaction details by hash (eth_getTransactionByHash): from, to, value, gas/gasPrice, nonce, input calldata, signature, and block placement. name: btcnode.uk Bitcoin Status
description: Live Bitcoin blockchain status from a synced full node — block height, chain-tip hash, mining difficulty, peer count and more. Pay-per-call x402.

usage.callShape: GET https://btcnode.uk/api/info (no body, no params)
usage.outputShape: body.chain, body.blocks, body.difficulty, body.connections, body.success
usage.guide: Make a plain GET to https://btcnode.uk/api/info with no body or query params; pay the x402 quote (~$0.001 USDC, exact scheme on Base/eip155:8453). The response is a flat JSON object with live full-node status: body.chain (e.g. "main"), body.blocks (current block height), body.difficulty (string), body.connections (peer count), and body.success (true). It is a synchronous call — read the result directly from the response body.

name: GraphAdvocate
description: Converts plain-English queries into working GraphQL/REST calls across 15,500+ blockchain subgraphs on 8 chains (Uniswap, Aave and more). Pay-per-call x402.

usage.callShape: POST https://graphadvocate.com/route with JSON body {"request": "<plain-English blockchain data question>"}

inputExample.request: What is the latest price of USDC on Uniswap v3 on Base?

usage.outputShape: body.recommendation (recommended service), body.reason, body.query_ready.args (ready-to-run GraphQL + subgraph_id), body.execution_result.data.data (LIVE executed query results — e.g. token, bundle.ethPriceUSD, tokenHourDatas[].priceUSD), body.alternatives[], body.get_started (free API key URL). The actual answer to your question is usually pre-executed inside body.execution_result.data.data.
quirks: The request field MUST be named 'request' (not 'query', 'text', or 'prompt'). Wrong field name still returns HTTP 200 but with {error:'Missing request text', hint:'POST {request: your query} or A2A format'} — and YOU STILL PAY for that failed call. Always send {"request": "..."}.
x402 paid even on the bad-field-name response (200 + error body), so the field name is money-critical.

The response is a recommendation engine: it picks the best subgraph/API for your plain-English question AND pre-executes the GraphQL for you. Read body.execution_result.data.data for the live answer; body.query_ready/curl_example are for if you want to re-run it yourself.
Response includes a body.promoted_skills array advertising other paid GraphAdvocate endpoints (polymarket/hyperliquid scoring) — ignore unless relevant.
qa-pay reported confirmed:false / txHash:null (settlement not captured on-chain in this harness), but status 200 and live data confirm the call succeeded.
usage.guide: POST to https://graphadvocate.com/route with JSON body {"request": "<your plain-English blockchain data question>"} — payment is x402 USDC ($0.01) on Base, no API key needed. CRITICAL: the field must be named "request"; using "query" or any other name returns a 200 hint-error AND still charges you. Read the live answer from body.execution_result.data.data, which contains the pre-executed GraphQL result; body.recommendation/query_ready/curl_example tell you which subgraph it used and how to re-run it yourself with a free thegraph.com API key.

name: Dexter Solana Analytics
description: Solana token/wallet trade summary — volumes, top counterparties and sample trades. Pay-per-request over x402 (USDC on Solana).

usage.callShape: GET https://x402.dexter.cash/onchain/activity (no body, no query params per registry spec)
usage.outputShape: Expected token/wallet trade summary (volumes, top counterparties, sample trades) but server returned error: body.ok=false, body.error="internal_error"
quirks: Endpoint took payment ($0.05 USDC on Base) then returned HTTP 500 with {"ok":false,"error":"internal_error"} — server-side failure, charge-then-error.
Registry inputSchema is null and no query-param documentation exists; the bare GET that is advertised as payable does not actually produce data.
Payment accepted on both Solana and Base (eip155:8453); qa-pay settled on Base. Failure is not network-specific (server-side 500).
usage.guide: Do not use this endpoint as-is: GET https://x402.dexter.cash/onchain/activity accepts the x402 payment ($0.05 USDC, Base or Solana) but then returns HTTP 500 {ok:false,error:"internal_error"} with no usable data. The registry exposes no input schema or query parameters, so there is nothing to adjust to make it work. Treat as broken/dead until the provider fixes the server; calling it only loses money.

name: OKLink Explorer
description: OKLink onchain data, token information and crypto prices across 40+ L1/L2 and 200+ blockchain networks, via the QuestFlow x402 agent gateway.

usage.callShape: POST https://api.questflow.ai/x402/agent/qrn:agent:687df7c0b234010b7d331c25 with JSON body {input: string}

inputExample.input: What is the current price of Bitcoin?

usage.outputShape: body.response (string). On a working call this would hold the agent's natural-language answer; currently always returns the error string "X402 Service is currently unavailable."
quirks: CHARGE-THEN-ERROR: gateway returns HTTP 201 and charges ~$0.10/call on Base, but backend returns {"response":"X402 Service is currently unavailable."} — money is lost with no useful result.
Persistent across 2 paid attempts (2026-06-08); backend OKLink agent appears dead, not transient.
No txHash returned by gateway (confirmed:false); settlement not on-chain-verifiable from response.
Do NOT call this endpoint until provider confirms it is back up — every call burns USDC for an error string.
usage.guide: Do not use this endpoint as-is. It is a QuestFlow x402 agent gateway for OKLink blockchain data; in theory you POST {"input":"<your question>"} and read the answer from body.response. In practice (tested 2026-06-08) it returns HTTP 201 and charges ~$0.10 per call but the backend replies {"response":"X402 Service is currently unavailable."} every time, so you pay and get nothing. Treat as broken and skip until the provider restores the backend.

name: Quicknode RPC
description: API-keyless JSON-RPC + REST access to 79+ blockchain networks (EVM + Solana + Aptos) via x402. Credit-based drawdown ($10 USDC prepaid = 1M credits). Requires a one-time SIWE auth to obtain a bearer token before RPC calls.

usage.callShape: POST https://x402.quicknode.com/{network} with JSON-RPC body {jsonrpc,id,method,params} — but only AFTER a one-time SIWE auth handshake to obtain a bearer token, which is then sent on RPC calls
usage.outputShape: body.result (JSON-RPC result), e.g. hex block number — UNVERIFIED (auth wall reached before any RPC executed)
quirks: Price is $10.00 — exceeds the $6 QA hard cap, so it could not be paid in this run. The $10 is a prepaid credit drawdown ($10 USDC = 1M credits), not per-call.
Registry probe reported 402, but live POST calls return HTTP 401 {"error":"invalid_signature","message":"Signature verification failed"} — the real gate is SIWE auth, not a plain x402 paywall.
Requires a one-time SIWE (Sign-In-With-Ethereum) handshake to mint a bearer token BEFORE any RPC call; the bearer token must accompany RPC requests. Plain x402 payment alone does NOT unlock it.
qa-pay --siwx flag did NOT satisfy QuickNode's SIWE flow — still 401 invalid_signature. QuickNode uses its own bespoke auth handshake, not the generic SIWX poller.
{network} path segment must be a real network slug (e.g. ethereum-mainnet, solana-mainnet); supports 79+ EVM/Solana/Aptos networks.
usage.guide: Untested in this run — blocked by two issues. First, the $10.00 price exceeds the $6 QA cap so no payment was made. Second, the endpoint is NOT a plain x402 paywall: live POST calls return HTTP 401 invalid_signature because QuickNode requires a one-time SIWE auth handshake to obtain a bearer token before any JSON-RPC call. To use it, an agent must (1) complete QuickNode's SIWE sign-in to get a bearer token (this also does the $10 prepaid credit drawdown), then (2) POST JSON-RPC bodies like {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"eth_blockNumber","params":[]} to https://x402.quicknode.com/{network} carrying that bearer token, and read the result from body.result. The generic --siwx path does not work here.

If retried in future, the intended usage is GET .../analyze/{token_address} substituting a real ERC-20 address (no body), reading body.risk_score and body.flags[].

usage.outputShape: Synchronous JSON object (verified from paid 200): pair (e.g. 'SOL/USD'), base ('SOL'), quote ('USD'), price (number, e.g. 73.72), source (e.g. 'Yahoo Finance (live)'), as_of (ISO 8601 UTC timestamp), note (human-readable '1 SOL = X USD.'), plus a marketing _hint field to ignore.
quirks: Zero-parameter GET — no input required; just call the fixed path to get the current SOL/USD price.
Optional ?format= query param exists (per openapi 'response format hint') but was not needed for a valid call.
Price source is 'Yahoo Finance (live)' (confirmed in the paid response), not an onchain/DEX oracle — this is a symbol-pair spot quote, distinct from onchain-contract price lookups.
Response includes a marketing _hint field that can be ignored.

This is one endpoint in a large x402node family of per-symbol /crypto/price/<sym>/usd/<sym>-usd and /crypto/convert/<sym>/usd/<sym>-usd paths (e.g. AVAX, BTC, ETH); each pair is its own fixed-path endpoint.
usage.guide: Fetch the live SOL/USD spot price with a single zero-argument GET to https://api.x402node.dev/crypto/price/sol/usd/sol-usd. No input, no API key — pay per call over x402 (USDC on Base or Solana; this run cost $0.004). Read body.price for the current price (a number of USD per 1 SOL), body.as_of for the quote timestamp, and body.source for provenance ('Yahoo Finance (live)'). body.note gives a ready-to-read '1 SOL = X USD.' string. Ignore the _hint field.

name: x402node Stablecoin Info
description: Deep profile of any stablecoin by symbol — peg type/mechanism (fiat-backed, crypto-backed, or algorithmic), live price vs. one dollar, circulating supply and per-chain breakdown, audit status with audit links, and mint/redeem rules — for stablecoin risk intelligence, sourced from DefiLlama.

query.symbol: Stablecoin symbol, e.g. USDT, USDC, DAI, FRAX (recommended; provider default USDT)
query.name: ENS name e.g. vitalik.eth (optional, per OpenAPI)

outputSchema.fields: symbol, name, pegType, pegMechanism, price, totalCirculating, chainCount, topChains[], audited, auditLinks[], mintRedeem, note, source

usage.callShape: GET https://api.x402node.dev/market/stablecoin-info?symbol=<SYMBOL> (x402 Base USDC ~$0.006, no API key, no body). Pass the stablecoin ticker as the `symbol` query param (e.g. USDC, USDT, DAI, FRAX). Also accepts x402 on Solana per the 402/OpenAPI accepts.
usage.outputShape: Synchronous JSON object (live paid 200 for symbol=USDC): symbol, name, pegType (e.g. peggedUSD), pegMechanism (fiat-backed | crypto-backed | algorithmic), price (float, USD), totalCirculating (number), chainCount (number), topChains[] (per-chain supply), audited (bool), auditLinks[] (URLs), mintRedeem (string), note (string), source (e.g. defillama). Also returns a promotional _hint field unrelated to the data.
quirks: The `symbol` query param is optional per OpenAPI (defaults to USDT) but you should always pass it for a meaningful result.

For symbol=USDC the paid response returned totalCirculating:0, chainCount:0 and topChains:[] even though the endpoint advertises circulating-supply-by-chain — supply figures may be missing/zero for some symbols; the peg/price/audit/mechanism fields were populated correctly.
Response includes a promotional `_hint` field (x402node cross-promo); ignore it.
Data is aggregated from DefiLlama (source field), so coverage/freshness follows DefiLlama.
Price is fixed at $0.006 (OpenAPI x-payment-info mode:fixed), not dynamic — no re-quote needed.
Sibling endpoint /stablecoin/peg-check ($0.008) is a lighter depeg-only check; this one is the full profile.
usage.guide: To get a full risk profile of a stablecoin, issue a GET to https://api.x402node.dev/market/stablecoin-info with a `symbol` query param set to the stablecoin ticker (e.g. symbol=USDC, USDT, DAI, FRAX) and pay the x402 quote (~$0.006 USDC on Base, no API key, no body; Solana also accepted). On a 200 read the flat JSON object: pegType and pegMechanism tell you whether it is fiat-backed, crypto-backed, or algorithmic (higher depeg risk); price is its live USD value; audited + auditLinks[] give attestation status; mintRedeem describes redemption; totalCirculating/chainCount/topChains[] give supply-by-chain when available; source names the upstream (DefiLlama). Synchronous, no polling. Ignore the _hint field.

name: x402node Stablecoin Peg Check
description: Check a stablecoin's peg health — current price vs $1, deviation in basis points, an on-peg/off-peg status flag, peg mechanism, and market cap (DefiLlama-sourced).

symbol.description: Stablecoin symbol, e.g. USDT, USDC, DAI, USDe (default USDT)
Stablecoin ticker or DefiLlama id, e.g. USDT, USDC, DAI (default USDT)

address.description: Contract address (alternative to symbol)

chain.description: Chain for the address

usage.callShape: GET https://api.x402node.dev/stablecoin/peg-check?symbol=<SYMBOL> (x402 payment, $0.008 USDC on Base; symbol optional, defaults to USDT). Result returned inline in the 200 JSON body — no polling.
usage.outputShape: body.symbol, body.name, body.price (USD, ~1.0), body.depegBps (deviation from $1 in basis points, signed), body.status ('on-peg' | off-peg flag), body.pegMechanism (e.g. 'fiat-backed'), body.mcap (circulating market cap USD), body.note, body.source ('defillama-stablecoins')
quirks: The 'symbol' input is an OPTIONAL query parameter; omitting it defaults to USDT. It is NOT a path or body param.
Payment is gated before validation — a 402 pre-flight on the first request is normal x402 behavior.
price is a full-precision float (e.g. 0.9998416707182998); use depegBps for the human-readable deviation and status for the flag.
Data is sourced from DefiLlama stablecoins ('source':'defillama-stablecoins'); coverage matches DefiLlama's tracked stablecoins.
Response includes a promotional '_hint' string that is not data.
usage.guide: Call GET https://api.x402node.dev/stablecoin/peg-check with an optional 'symbol' query parameter (e.g. ?symbol=USDC; omit for USDT). Pay the x402 quote ($0.008 USDC on Base, asset USDC 0x8335...2913, payTo 0x4466...125e; Solana USDC also accepted). The result comes back synchronously in the top-level JSON body: read price (USD), depegBps (signed deviation from $1), status ('on-peg'/off-peg flag), pegMechanism, and mcap. Use this to monitor depeg/exit risk on held stablecoins. Data is DefiLlama-sourced and live.

name: Xona Token Search
description: Search crypto assets by name, symbol, or mint/contract address and get back canonical assets plus per-token market stats (price, liquidity, 24h/30d volume, market cap, FDV, price change, supply) via Xona's Tokens API, gated by an x402 micro-payment on Base.

q.description: Search query string (name, symbol, or mint/contract address)

limit.description: Max results 1-50 (default 20)

results.description: Matching assets; each has assetId, name, symbol, category, imageUrl, stats{price,liquidity,volume24hUSD,volume30dUSD,marketCap,fdv,priceChange24hPercent,priceChange1hPercent,totalSupply,circulatingSupply}, and primaryVariant{variantId,mint,kind,trustTier,tags,symbol,name,market{...},liquidityTier}.

usage.callShape: POST https://api.xona-agent.com/base-main/tokens-api/search with a JSON body {"q": <query>, "limit"?: 1-50 (default 20), "category"?: <asset category>}. Only q is required. Pays $0.01 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453). Result is returned inline in the 200 (synchronous, no poll).
usage.outputShape: { success:true, data:{ query, category, primaryVariantStrategy, results:[ { assetId, name, symbol, category, imageUrl, stats:{ price, liquidity, volume24hUSD, volume30dUSD, marketCap, fdv, priceChange24hPercent, priceChange1hPercent, totalSupply, circulatingSupply }, primaryVariant:{ variantId, mint, kind, trustTier, tags[], symbol, name, market:{ source, metricsSource, price, liquidity, volume1hUSD, volume24hUSD, trade1h, trade24h, uniqueWallet1h, uniqueWallet24h, marketCap, fdv, holder, totalSupply, circulatingSupply, priceChange24hPercent, priceChange1hPercent, decimals, logoURI, lastTradeAt, asOf, lastFetchedAt }, executionQuality, liquidityTier } } ] } }
quirks: The empty-body bazaar schema in the live 402 is a placeholder; the real input is {q, limit?, category?} (q required), taken from the provider's own /x402-resources listing and confirmed by a paid 200.

Despite the 'Base/EVM' label and Base (eip155:8453) payment rail, the returned token data is cross-chain and market stats are sourced from Birdeye — the verified q="USDC" result surfaced a Solana USDC mint (EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v) under primaryVariant, not a Base contract. Treat mint/asset chain as data-dependent, not always Base.
Numeric market stats are returned as JSON numbers (floats), not strings. Some fields (asOf, executionQuality) can be null on a valid 200.
There is also a Solana-rail sibling at /tokens-api/search (paid $0.01 USDC on solana-mainnet); this entry is the Base-rail (/base-main/) variant.
usage.guide: Search crypto assets by name, symbol, or mint/contract address and get canonical assets plus per-token market stats via Xona's Tokens API. POST https://api.xona-agent.com/base-main/tokens-api/search with JSON body {"q": <query string>, "limit"?: 1-50 (default 20), "category"?: <asset category>}; only q is required. Pays $0.01 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453); result returns inline in the 200 (synchronous). Response: data.results[] where each result has assetId/name/symbol/category/imageUrl, a stats object (price, liquidity, volume24hUSD, volume30dUSD, marketCap, fdv, priceChange24h/1hPercent, totalSupply, circulatingSupply), and a primaryVariant object (mint, kind, trustTier, tags, and a Birdeye-sourced market{} block with 1h/24h trade + wallet counts, decimals, logoURI, timestamps). Note the token data is cross-chain even though payment is on Base.

name: ChainRay Chain Overview
description: Single-call aggregated snapshot of one blockchain: current/predicted gas, chain- and protocol-health scores, on-chain and market TVL with top protocols, stablecoin peg + supply, and the latest block — bundling several ChainRay endpoints into one x402-paid response with a verifiable proof.

chain.description: Target blockchain (default base). One of 46 supported: base, ethereum, arbitrum, optimism, polygon, bsc, avalanche, zksync, linea, scroll, blast, mantle, gnosis, polygon-zkevm, mode, sei, celo, manta, taiko, fantom, cronos, opbnb, zora, worldchain, metis, fraxtal, kava, zetachain, filecoin, core-dao, aurora, moonbeam, klaytn, bob, canto, solana, sui, aptos, ton, xrp, tron, doge, cardano, near, cosmos, bitcoin.

usage.callShape: GET https://chainray.online/chain-overview?chain=<evm-or-l1-chain> -- x402 USDC on Base (eip155:8453). The chain query param is OPTIONAL and defaults to base; omit it for Base. No request body, no path params. Returns HTTP 402 with x402 payment requirements on the first call, then HTTP 200 with the aggregated overview once an EIP-3009 USDC authorization is signed.
usage.outputShape: JSON object: chain, type ('chain-overview'), aggregated (bool); gas.{chain,current.{baseFee,fast,standard,slow,unit},trend,trendChangePercent,prediction1h,network.{avgUtilization,latestBlockNumber,blocksAnalyzed},history[]}; health.{healthScore,grade,gas,tvl.{onChain.{totalTvl,totalTvlFormatted,protocols[]},market.{chainTvl,topProtocols[]}},stablecoins.{stablecoins[].{token,address,priceUsd,deviation,status,poolFee},alertCount,alerts[]},sectionsAvailable}; protocols.{overallHealth,healthScore,maxScore,description,metrics,marketBreakdown[],protocols[]}; stablecoinSupply.{onChain.{stablecoins[],aggregated[],chainsScanned[]},globalMarket.{topStablecoins[],source}}; latestBlock.{number,hash,parentHash,timestamp,timestampISO,gasUsed,gasLimit,baseFeePerGas,transactionCount,miner,size,fetchedAt}; equivalentEndpoints[] (the individual endpoints this bundles), savings (e.g. '$0.037 saved vs querying individually'), timestamp; _proof.{blockNumber,blockHash,blockTimestamp,chain,chainName,proofVersion,proofTimestamp,dataHash}.
quirks: One aggregated call replaces ~5 individual endpoints (/gas-tracker, /chain-health, /protocol-health, /stablecoin-supply, /block-info); the response's savings field quantifies the discount and equivalentEndpoints lists them.

chain is optional (defaults to base); 46 chains supported including non-EVM L1s (solana, sui, aptos, ton, xrp, tron, doge, cardano, near, cosmos, bitcoin) though some sub-sections (e.g. on-chain protocol TVL via Aave/Compound reads) are EVM-oriented and may be sparse for non-EVM chains.
Some fields can be null or sparse (e.g. gas.history[].block came back null, protocols.protocols[] empty on Base) — read defensively.
Carries a verifiable _proof object (Chain Proof v3: dataHash + block anchoring) like all ChainRay endpoints.
Synchronous: the full overview is inline in the 200 body; no polling.
usage.guide: Aggregated one-call snapshot of a single chain from ChainRay: current + predicted gas, chain-health and protocol-health scores, on-chain and DeFi-market TVL with top protocols, stablecoin peg status + supply, and the latest block. GET https://chainray.online/chain-overview?chain=<chain> -- x402 USDC on Base (eip155:8453), $0.01 per call. The chain param is optional and defaults to base; supply one of the 46 supported chains (base, ethereum, arbitrum, optimism, polygon, bsc, avalanche, solana, sui, aptos, bitcoin, ...) to switch. No body, no path params, no API key. Prefer this over calling gas/health/tvl/stablecoin/block endpoints separately when you want a full chain state readout — the response's savings field shows the discount. Output is a nested JSON object (gas, health, protocols, stablecoinSupply, latestBlock, plus equivalentEndpoints/savings and a _proof bundle); some sub-sections may be null/sparse depending on chain.

name: ChainRay Flash Loan Monitor
description: Scans recent blocks on an EVM chain for Aave V3 flash-loan events, returning the count and details of flash loans detected with a verifiable Chain Proof.

backends.inputSchema: query param: chain=<evm-chain> (default base). EVM chains only (35-chain enum: base, ethereum, arbitrum, optimism, polygon, bsc, avalanche, zksync, linea, scroll, blast, mantle, gnosis, ...).
backends.outputSchema: chain, protocol, blocksScanned, totalFlashLoans, flashLoans[], timestamp, _proof.{blockNumber,blockHash,blockTimestamp,chain,chainName,proofVersion,proofTimestamp,dataHash}

usage.callShape: GET https://chainray.online/flashloan-monitor?chain=<evm-chain> -- x402 USDC on Base. chain query param defaults to base; EVM chains only.
usage.outputShape: chain, protocol, blocksScanned, totalFlashLoans, flashLoans[], timestamp, _proof.{blockNumber,blockHash,blockTimestamp,chain,chainName,proofVersion,proofTimestamp,dataHash}
quirks: chain is a query param (NOT path); default base. EVM-only enum of ~35 chains.
Currently monitors the Aave V3 protocol; protocol field in the response names it.
Scans a fixed recent window (blocksScanned=200); totalFlashLoans/flashLoans[] can legitimately be 0/empty when no flash loans occurred in that window (observed on the paid call).
Every response includes a _proof object with a dataHash (verifiable via /verify-proof).
usage.guide: Scans the most recent ~200 blocks on an EVM chain for Aave V3 flash-loan events. GET https://chainray.online/flashloan-monitor?chain=<evm-chain> -- x402 USDC on Base, $0.01. chain query param defaults to base; EVM chains only (35-chain enum). No other input. Output: chain, protocol (e.g. 'Aave V3'), blocksScanned, totalFlashLoans, flashLoans[] (empty when none in window), timestamp, and a _proof bundle (blockNumber, blockHash, blockTimestamp, chain, chainName, proofVersion, proofTimestamp, dataHash) verifiable via /verify-proof.

name: ChainRay Gas History
description: Sampled base-fee (gas) history time-series for an EVM chain over the last ~6 hours: per-sample block base fee, gas used/limit, utilization and tx count, plus min/max/avg/current stats.

backends.inputSchema: queryParams: chain=<evm-chain> (optional, default base). EVM chains only (46-chain enum incl. base, ethereum, arbitrum, optimism, polygon, bsc, avalanche, zksync, linea, scroll, ...).
backends.outputSchema: chain, chainName, period, sampleInterval, dataPoints, failedSamples, stats.{min,max,avg,current,unit}, samples[].{index,blockNumber,timestamp,time,baseFeeGwei,gasUsed,gasLimit,utilization,txCount}, note, timestamp, _proof.{blockNumber,blockHash,blockTimestamp,chain,chainName,proofVersion,proofTimestamp,dataHash}

usage.callShape: GET https://chainray.online/gas-history?chain=<evm-chain> -- x402 USDC on Base. chain query param is optional and defaults to base. EVM chains only (46-chain enum). No other params.
usage.outputShape: chain, chainName, period, sampleInterval, dataPoints, failedSamples, stats.{min,max,avg,current,unit}, samples[].{index,blockNumber,timestamp,time,baseFeeGwei,gasUsed,gasLimit,utilization,txCount}, note, timestamp, _proof.{blockNumber,blockHash,blockTimestamp,chain,chainName,proofVersion,proofTimestamp,dataHash}

Returns SAMPLED data (~every 300 blocks / ~10min over a ~6h window, ~36 data points), not per-block values -- see body.note.
stats values (min/max/avg/current) and baseFeeGwei are in gwei; stats returned as strings.
Every response includes a _proof object with a dataHash (verifiable via ChainRay proof verification).
usage.guide: Returns a sampled base-fee (gas) history time-series for an EVM chain over the last ~6 hours. GET https://chainray.online/gas-history?chain=<evm-chain> -- x402 USDC on Base ($0.001). chain query param defaults to base; EVM chains only (46-chain enum: base, ethereum, arbitrum, optimism, polygon, bsc, avalanche, zksync, linea, scroll, blast, mantle, gnosis, ...). No other input. Output: chain, chainName, period (e.g. '360 minutes (6.0h)'), sampleInterval (e.g. 'Every 300 blocks (~10min)'), dataPoints, failedSamples, stats.{min,max,avg,current,unit=gwei}, samples[] (each: index, blockNumber, timestamp, time ISO, baseFeeGwei, gasUsed, gasLimit, utilization %, txCount) newest-first, note (data is sampled not per-block), timestamp, _proof.{blockNumber,blockHash,blockTimestamp,chain,chainName,proofVersion,proofTimestamp,dataHash}.

name: ChainRay Gas Predict
description: Short-horizon (5-20 block, ~10-40s) gas fee forecast for an EVM chain: current baseFee plus low/mid/high prediction, trend direction, 5/20-block moving-average stats, volatility, and a transact-timing recommendation, computed from the last 20 real blocks (no external APIs).

backends.inputSchema: queryParams: chain=<evm-chain> (optional, default base; EVM-only enum of 35 chains: base, ethereum, arbitrum, optimism, polygon, bsc, avalanche, zksync, linea, scroll, blast, mantle, gnosis, polygon-zkevm, mode, sei, celo, manta, taiko, fantom, cronos, opbnb, zora, worldchain, metis, fraxtal, kava, zetachain, filecoin, core-dao, aurora, moonbeam, klaytn, bob, canto)
backends.outputSchema: chain, current.{baseFee,unit}, forecast.{horizon,low,mid,high,unit,note}, trend.{direction,changePercent}, stats.{sampledBlocks,avg5Block,avg20Block,min,max,volatility}, recommendation, dataSource, methodology, timestamp, _proof.{blockNumber,blockHash,blockTimestamp,chain,chainName,proofVersion,proofTimestamp,dataHash,analysisHash}

usage.callShape: GET https://chainray.online/gas-predict?chain=<evm-chain> -- x402 USDC on Base. chain query param is optional and defaults to base. EVM chains only (35 supported).
usage.outputShape: chain, current.{baseFee,unit}, forecast.{horizon,low,mid,high,unit,note}, trend.{direction,changePercent}, stats.{sampledBlocks,avg5Block,avg20Block,min,max,volatility}, recommendation, dataSource, methodology, timestamp, _proof.{blockNumber,blockHash,blockTimestamp,chain,chainName,proofVersion,proofTimestamp,dataHash,analysisHash}
quirks: chain is a query param (NOT a path segment); default base. EVM-only enum of 35 chains (a subset of ChainRay's 46 -- non-EVM chains like solana/sui/bitcoin are rejected).
Fixed price $0.005 (openapi x-payment-info mode=fixed); not dynamic.
Forecast horizon is very short: 5-20 blocks (~10-40s). Gas values are in Gwei.
Every response includes a _proof object (Chain Proof v3) with dataHash + analysisHash, verifiable via ChainRay's proof verification.
Purely statistical (moving average + coefficient of variation over last 20 blocks); no LLM/speculative model.
usage.guide: Short-horizon gas fee forecast for an EVM chain. GET https://chainray.online/gas-predict?chain=<evm-chain> -- x402 USDC on Base, $0.005. chain query param defaults to base; EVM chains only (35 supported: base, ethereum, arbitrum, optimism, polygon, bsc, avalanche, zksync, linea, scroll, blast, mantle, gnosis, and more). No other input. Read forecast.{low,mid,high} (Gwei) for the 5-20 block (~10-40s) window, trend.direction (RISING/STABLE/FALLING) + trend.changePercent for direction, stats.{avg5Block,avg20Block,volatility} for context, and recommendation for a plain-English transact-timing hint. current.baseFee is the latest observed baseFee. body._proof carries a verifiable Chain Proof v3 bundle (dataHash, analysisHash).

usage.outputShape: chain, current.{baseFee,fast,standard,slow,unit}, trend, trendChangePercent, prediction1h.{estimatedBaseFee,confidence,note}, network.{avgUtilization,latestBlockNumber,blocksAnalyzed}, history[].{block,baseFeeGwei,utilization}, timestamp, _proof.{blockNumber,blockHash,blockTimestamp,chain,chainName,proofVersion,proofTimestamp,dataHash}

usage.guide: Current gas/fee snapshot for a given chain: current base/fast/standard/slow fees (gwei), stable/rising/falling trend, a 1-hour linear base-fee prediction, network utilization, and a short recent base-fee/utilization history. GET https://chainray.online/gas-tracker[?chain=<chain>] -- x402 USDC on Base ($0.001). chain query param is optional and defaults to base; 46 chains supported (EVM + non-EVM). No body. usage.guide: Lists known on-chain DAO/governance contracts for a given EVM chain. usage.guide: Monitors major stablecoins on an EVM chain for depeg events. GET https://chainray.online/stablecoin-monitor?chain=<evm-chain> -- x402 USDC on Base. chain query param is optional and defaults to base; EVM chains only (~35 supported). Output: chain, stablecoins[].{token,address,priceUsd,deviation,status,poolFee} (status = PEGGED|DEPEGGED, deviation/poolFee are percent strings), alertCount, alerts[] (subset of stablecoins flagged DEPEGGED), timestamp, _proof.{blockNumber,blockHash,blockTimestamp,chain,chainName,proofVersion,proofTimestamp,dataHash}.

name: ChainRay Whale Alerts
description: Recent large-transfer (whale) feed for an EVM chain over a lookback window: each alert carries tx hash, from/to (with known-address labels like whale/smart_money/exchange), token, amount and USD value, plus an on-chain intel and verifiable proof bundle.

chain.description: Target blockchain (46-chain enum: base, ethereum, arbitrum, optimism, polygon, bsc, avalanche, zksync, linea, scroll, blast, mantle, gnosis, solana, sui, aptos, ton, xrp, tron, bitcoin, etc).

minAmount.description: Minimum transfer USD value to count as a whale alert.

usage.callShape: GET https://chainray.online/whale-alerts?chain=<evm-or-chain>[&hours=<int>][&minAmount=<usd-int>] -- x402 USDC on Base. All params optional (chain defaults to base, hours to 6, minAmount to 50000). Result returned inline in the 200; no polling.
usage.outputShape: chain, scannedBlocks, periodHours, minAmountUsd, ethPrice, totalAlerts, alerts[]{txHash,blockNumber,from,to,token,amount,usdValue,direction,fromLabel,toLabel}, timestamp, _intel.{knownAddresses,details.{<addr>:{labels[],lastSeen,seenCount}}}, _proof.{blockNumber,blockHash,blockTimestamp,chain,chainName,proofVersion,proofTimestamp,dataHash}
quirks: All inputs are query params (NOT path/body); every param optional with defaults chain=base, hours=6, minAmount=50000.
chain accepts a 46-chain enum spanning EVM and non-EVM (solana, sui, aptos, ton, xrp, tron, bitcoin, etc).
fromLabel/toLabel are null unless the address is known; richer labels (whale, smart_money, exchange) are in _intel.details keyed by lowercased address with labels[]/lastSeen/seenCount.
Every response carries a _proof object with a dataHash (verifiable via /verify-proof).
alerts can be large (the base sample returned 709 alerts, ~16 KB body) and reflect a live scan over scannedBlocks.
usage.guide: Get a feed of recent large ('whale') transfers on a chain. GET https://chainray.online/whale-alerts?chain=<chain>[&hours=<int>][&minAmount=<usd-int>] -- pay per call via x402 (USDC on Base, ~$0.005). All params optional: chain defaults to base (46-chain enum incl. ethereum/arbitrum/polygon/solana/etc), hours is the lookback window (default 6), minAmount is the USD floor for a transfer to count (default 50000). Read totalAlerts and iterate alerts[] for {txHash, from, to, token, amount, usdValue, direction}; cross-reference _intel.details (keyed by lowercased address) for whale/smart_money/exchange labels. body._proof carries a verifiable proof bundle. Verified 2026-07-29 with {chain:'base'} -> HTTP 200, 709 alerts, $0.005 charged.

name: x402node Block Info
description: Return the latest block on any of 7 EVM chains with block height, block age, transaction count, gas utilization percent, base fee and a low/moderate/high congestion rating, so an agent can check chain liveness and network busyness before submitting a transaction.

chain.description: EVM chain: ethereum, base (default), arbitrum, optimism, polygon, bsc, avalanche. Optional; defaults to base.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.x402node.dev/chain/block-info with an optional ?chain= query param (ethereum, base (default), arbitrum, optimism, polygon, bsc, avalanche). No body. Pay the fixed $0.004 x402 quote (USDC on Base or Solana, no API key) and retry with the payment header.
usage.outputShape: Synchronous flat JSON (from the paid 200): { chain:'base', blockNumber:49297806, timestamp:1785384959 (unix sec), ageSec:1, txCount:190, gasUsedPct:9.9, baseFeeGwei:0.005, congestion:'low'|'moderate'|'high', note: human-readable string, source:'rpc', _hint: promo string }.
quirks: Zero required params: chain defaults to base when omitted. Supports 7 EVM chains (ethereum, base, arbitrum, optimism, polygon, bsc, avalanche).
congestion is a derived rating (low/moderate/high); gasUsedPct is the raw gas utilization percent (higher = busier network).
Fixed price ($0.004 in OpenAPI x-payment-info, matching the 4000-atomic live 402 accept) - not a dynamic quote.
Live 402 advertised BOTH a Base and a Solana USDC accept (both amount 4000); both are recorded. Paid via Base.
Distinct from x402node's /chain/block (raw block lookup by number) - this endpoint adds gas utilization + congestion rating across 7 chains.
Response includes a promotional _hint field that can be ignored.
usage.guide: Check how busy an EVM chain is before submitting a transaction. Issue a plain GET to https://api.x402node.dev/chain/block-info, optionally passing ?chain=<ethereum|base|arbitrum|optimism|polygon|bsc|avalanche> (defaults to base), and pay the ~$0.004 x402 quote (USDC on Base or Solana, no API key). On the 200, read the flat JSON: `congestion` is a low/moderate/high rating, `gasUsedPct` is the raw gas utilization, `baseFeeGwei` is the current base fee, `ageSec` is how old the latest block is, and `blockNumber` is the head height. Synchronous - no polling.

name: x402node Chain Block
description: Returns block details (number, hash, timestamp, transaction count, sample transaction hashes, gas used/limit, base fee, miner) for a given EVM chain — latest block by default or a specific block by number.

chain.description: ethereum, base (default), arbitrum, optimism, polygon

usage.callShape: GET https://api.x402node.dev/chain/block?chain=<evm-chain>[&number=<block-number>] — x402 USDC on Base (or Solana), fixed $0.004/call. Both params optional: chain defaults to base; omit number for the latest block. Result is returned synchronously in the 200 body.
usage.outputShape: body.chain, body.number, body.hash, body.timestamp (ISO), body.txCount, body.sampleTxHashes[] (array of tx hash strings), body.gasUsed (string), body.gasLimit (string), body.baseFeeGwei (number), body.miner (address). Read fields directly off the top-level JSON body.
quirks: Both query params are optional: chain defaults to base, number defaults to the latest block.
Only five EVM chains supported here: ethereum, base, arbitrum, optimism, polygon (the sibling /chain/block-info supports 7).
Numeric on-chain fields gasUsed and gasLimit are returned as strings; number, txCount and baseFeeGwei are numbers.
Fixed price $0.004 USDC (4000 atomic units), not 'Varies'. Accepts payment on Base OR Solana — either network works.
Response includes a documentation-only _hint field; ignore it.
usage.guide: Fetch block metadata for an EVM chain with a single paid x402 GET. Call GET https://api.x402node.dev/chain/block — the wallet pays $0.004 USDC on Base (Solana also accepted) automatically via the 402 flow. Add ?chain=<ethereum|base|arbitrum|optimism|polygon> to pick the chain (defaults to base) and ?number=<block> to fetch a specific block (omit for latest). Read the answer from the top-level body: body.number and body.hash identify the block, body.timestamp is the block time (ISO), body.txCount and body.sampleTxHashes give transaction info, and body.gasUsed/body.gasLimit/body.baseFeeGwei/body.miner give gas and producer details.

name: x402node Universal Crypto Price
description: Universal live crypto spot price for ANY coin by symbol (BTC, ETH, SOL, WIF, or localized names), with an optional quote currency (USD/CNY/EUR), amount conversion, and locale-aware output, returned as a synchronous JSON quote (symbol, vs, price, pair, source, timestamp).

symbol.description: Coin symbol or localized name (e.g. BTC, ETH, SOL, WIF). Required in practice.

vs.description: Quote currency, e.g. USD/CNY/EUR. Optional; defaults per locale.

amount.description: Optional amount to convert into the quote currency.

lang.description: Optional localization hint for the human-readable note (zh/ja/ko).

usage.callShape: GET https://api.x402node.dev/crypto/price?symbol=<COIN>&vs=<CURRENCY> (x402 Base or Solana USDC, no body). symbol is the coin to price; vs, amount, and lang are optional query params. Pay the fixed $0.01 x402 quote and retry with the payment header.
usage.outputShape: Synchronous JSON object (verified from the paid 200): { symbol:'BTC', vs:'USD', price:64051.46 (number in the quote currency), pair:'BTC/USD', source:'Yahoo Finance (live)', as_of: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp, note:'1 BTC = 64051.46 USD.' (human-readable), _hint: provider promo string to ignore }.
quirks: Universal query-param endpoint: pass ?symbol=<COIN> (BTC/ETH/SOL/WIF or localized names); vs/amount/lang are optional. Distinct from the per-symbol fixed-path /crypto/price/<sym>/usd/<sym>-usd endpoints (those are $0.004 zero-param quotes).
Fixed price ($0.01 in OpenAPI x-payment-info, matching the 10000-atomic live 402 accept) — not a dynamic quote.
Price source is 'Yahoo Finance (live)', a symbol-pair spot quote — not an onchain/DEX oracle.
The live 402 advertised BOTH a Base and a Solana USDC accept (both recorded here); the paid call settled on Base.
Response includes a marketing _hint field that can be ignored.
usage.guide: Fetch a live crypto spot price for any coin. Issue a GET to https://api.x402node.dev/crypto/price with ?symbol=<COIN> (e.g. BTC) and optionally &vs=<CURRENCY> (e.g. USD), no body, and pay the x402 quote (~$0.01 USDC on Base or Solana, no API key). On the 200 read the flat JSON: `price` is the spot value as a number in the quote currency, `pair` is the pair label, `as_of` is the ISO-8601 timestamp, and `source` names the upstream feed (Yahoo Finance). Synchronous — no polling.

name: ToolOracle XRPL RLUSD Integrity
description: Cross-verifies Ripple USD (RLUSD) stablecoin integrity across three sources in one call — DeFiLlama peg price and market cap, XRPL on-chain circulating supply via gateway_balances on the issuer account, and live XRPL DEX orderbook liquidity — returning per-source results plus an integrity summary and anomaly flags (e.g. SUPPLY_MISMATCH).

inputSchema.note: No parameters — the RLUSD token/issuer is fixed server-side. Send an empty JSON body {} with Content-Type: application/json.

usage.callShape: POST https://tooloracle.io/v2/xrpl_rlusd_integrity with an empty JSON body {} and Content-Type: application/json. Pay $0.03 USDC via x402 on Base. Result is inline in the 200 (synchronous, no poll).
usage.outputShape: Flat JSON (NOT a JSON-RPC envelope). Read data.sources.defillama.{price,mcap}, data.sources.xrpl_onchain.{circulating,issuer}, data.sources.xrpl_dex.{active_offers,dex_liquidity}, data.flags[] ({type,severity,detail}), and data.integrity.{sources_checked,sources_ok,flags_count,status,confidence}. A content hash is at meta.content_hash.
quirks: Takes NO input parameters — the RLUSD token/issuer is fixed server-side; send an empty JSON body {}.
Response is a flat JSON object (unlike the sibling MiCA Compliance Pre-flight, which is a JSON-RPC envelope) — the real result is directly under data, no double JSON.parse needed.
Backend fronted at tooloracle.io but served by FeedOracle (did:web:feedoracle.io); auth is anonymous despite x402 payment.
meta.credits_consumed was 0 on the paid call; the x402 $0.03 charge is the real cost. Paid on Base, tx confirmed (0xa07af3ffe443f5453d594ba28451f8d048f3b1199934b2a27115632c0d87ceb3).
data.integrity.status is a live judgement (observed 'MONITOR' with a MEDIUM SUPPLY_MISMATCH flag comparing DeFiLlama mcap vs XRPL on-chain supply) — values vary per call with market conditions.
usage.guide: POST to https://tooloracle.io/v2/xrpl_rlusd_integrity with an empty JSON body {} (Content-Type: application/json). Pay $0.03 USDC via x402 on Base — no API key, no sign-in. The 200 returns synchronously: read data.sources for the three per-source checks (DeFiLlama peg price/mcap, XRPL on-chain circulating supply, XRPL DEX liquidity), data.flags[] for anomalies like SUPPLY_MISMATCH, and data.integrity for the roll-up (sources_checked/sources_ok, status, confidence). No parameters are needed; the check is fixed to RLUSD.

name: ChainRay Agent Discovery
description: Discovers registered A2A (agent-to-agent) agents in ChainRay's on-chain agent registry, filterable by capability, chain, or keyword, with a verifiable Chain Proof.

chain.description: Blockchain network to filter by, e.g. base, ethereum, polygon (optional)

usage.callShape: GET https://chainray.online/agent-card/discover[?chain=<evm-chain>][&cap=<capability>] -- x402 USDC on Base. All query params optional; returns registered A2A agents filtered by capability/chain/keyword. Omit all params to list the full registry.
usage.outputShape: oracleType, totalMatched, returned, filters.{capability,chain,keyword}, agents[], registrySize, standard, timestamp, _proof.{blockNumber,blockHash,blockTimestamp,chain,chainName,proofVersion,proofTimestamp,dataHash}
quirks: chain and cap are query params (NOT path); all optional. Omit for the whole registry.
The A2A registry can be empty: a successful paid call may return agents:[] with totalMatched:0 and registrySize:0 (observed at index time on chain=base) -- it is a live registry, not static data.
Every response carries a verifiable _proof object with a dataHash (Chain Proof v3).
llms.txt lists this endpoint at $0.02, but the live 402 header/body and openapi.json both quote $0.005 (maxAmountRequired 5000 = 0.005 USDC, 6dp) -- the live 402 is authoritative.
usage.guide: Discovers registered A2A (agent-to-agent) agents in ChainRay's on-chain agent registry. GET https://chainray.online/agent-card/discover with optional query params chain=<evm-chain> and cap=<capability keyword>; omit all to list the whole registry. Plain x402-paid GET (USDC on Base, no API key). Read matches off body.agents[] (each an A2A agent card); body.registrySize/totalMatched/returned describe the result set; body._proof.dataHash is a verifiable proof of the response. Sibling ops on the same host: POST /agent-card/register ($0.05) to add an agent and GET /agent-card/{agentId} ($0.001) to look one up.

name: ChainRay DeFi Compare
description: Side-by-side DeFi lending-market comparison for a chain: live Aave V3 supply/borrow APYs and utilization (direct on-chain contract reads), Compound V3 Comet market rates, and top yield pools by TVL from DeFi Llama.

inputSchema.chain: string (optional query param; enum of 46 chains, default base)

backends.outputSchema: chain, comparison, protocolCount, protocols[], note, timestamp, _proof

usage.callShape: GET https://chainray.online/defi-compare?chain=<evm-chain> -- x402 USDC on Base. All params optional; chain query param defaults to base.
usage.outputShape: chain, comparison, protocolCount, protocols[]: for Aave V3 -> onChain.{protocol,protocolType,source,summary.{marketsAvailable,bestSupplyAPY},markets[].{asset,address,supplyAPY,borrowAPY,totalSupply,totalBorrow,utilization,lastUpdated},errors[]} + topYieldPools.{pools[].{project,symbol,chain,apy,apyBase,apyReward,tvl,tvlFormatted,change1d,change7d,stablecoin},source,note} + timestamp; for Compound V3 -> {protocol,market,chain,chainName,cometAddress,supplyAPY,borrowAPY,utilization,totalSupply,totalBorrow,dataSource}. note, timestamp, _proof.{blockNumber,blockHash,blockTimestamp,chain,chainName,proofVersion,proofTimestamp,dataHash}
quirks: chain is a query param (NOT path); default base. Enum of 46 chains, though live DeFi coverage is strongest on major EVM chains.
protocols[] is heterogeneous: the Aave V3 element nests on-chain markets plus DeFi-Llama topYieldPools, while the Compound V3 element is a flat market object -- shapes differ per protocol.
Some on-chain reads can fail per-asset and surface under protocols[].onChain.errors[] (e.g. a bad/legacy token address) without failing the whole call.
Carries a _proof object (Chain Proof v3 dataHash) like all ChainRay endpoints; verifiable via /verify-proof.
Fixed $0.01 price per openapi.json x-payment-info and llms.txt; not dynamic.
usage.guide: Side-by-side DeFi lending-market comparison for a chain: live Aave V3 supply/borrow APYs and utilization (direct on-chain contract reads), Compound V3 Comet market rates, and top yield pools by TVL from DeFi Llama. GET https://chainray.online/defi-compare?chain=<evm-chain> -- x402 USDC on Base. All params optional; chain query param defaults to base (enum of 46 chains). Output: chain, comparison, protocolCount, protocols[] (heterogeneous per protocol -- Aave V3 nests onChain.markets[] {asset,supplyAPY,borrowAPY,utilization,totalSupply,totalBorrow} plus topYieldPools from DeFi Llama; Compound V3 is a flat Comet market object), note, timestamp, _proof.{dataHash,...}. Use to compare lending yields across Aave/Compound and scout the highest-TVL yield pools on a chain.

name: ChainRay DeFi Yields
description: Best DeFi yield opportunities for a chain in one x402-paid call: live on-chain lending-market APYs (Aave V3 supply/borrow rates, TVL, utilization) plus the top TVL-ranked yield pools aggregated from DeFi Llama (project, symbol, APY base/reward, TVL, 1d/7d change, stablecoin flag), with a verifiable proof.

chain.description: Blockchain network (e.g., base, ethereum, polygon). Optional; defaults to base.

usage.callShape: GET https://chainray.online/defi-yields?chain=<evm-chain> -- x402 USDC on Base (eip155:8453), $0.01 per call. The chain query param is OPTIONAL and defaults to base; omit it for Base. No request body, no path params, no API key. Returns HTTP 402 with x402 payment requirements on the first call, then HTTP 200 with the yields payload once an EIP-3009 USDC authorization is signed.
usage.outputShape: JSON object: chain; onChain.{protocol,protocolType,source,summary.{marketsAvailable,bestSupplyAPY},markets[].{asset,address,supplyAPY,borrowAPY,totalSupply,totalBorrow,utilization,lastUpdated},errors[].{asset,address,error}}; topYieldPools.{pools[].{project,symbol,chain,apy,apyBase,apyReward,tvl,tvlFormatted,change1d,change7d,stablecoin},source,note}; timestamp; _proof.{blockNumber,blockHash,blockTimestamp,chain,chainName,proofVersion,proofTimestamp,dataHash}.
quirks: chain is optional and defaults to base; supply another supported EVM chain (ethereum, polygon, arbitrum, optimism, etc.) to switch.
onChain is currently Aave V3 lending markets read directly from contracts; some markets can appear under onChain.errors[] (e.g. a bad/legacy token address) while the rest still return.
topYieldPools is aggregated from DeFi Llama (17K+ pools) and sorted by TVL; apy is base+reward, with apyBase/apyReward broken out (either can be null).
Carries a verifiable _proof object (Chain Proof v3: dataHash + block anchoring) like all ChainRay endpoints.
Synchronous: the full result is inline in the 200 body; no polling.
usage.guide: Get the best DeFi yield opportunities for a chain in one ChainRay call. GET https://chainray.online/defi-yields?chain=<chain> -- x402 USDC on Base (eip155:8453), $0.01 per call. The chain param is optional and defaults to base; supply a supported EVM chain (base, ethereum, polygon, arbitrum, optimism, ...) to switch. No body, no path params, no API key. Returns two blocks: onChain (live Aave V3 lending markets read from contracts -- supplyAPY/borrowAPY, totalSupply/totalBorrow, utilization per asset, plus a summary with bestSupplyAPY) and topYieldPools (DeFi Llama pools sorted by TVL -- project, symbol, apy/apyBase/apyReward, tvl, 1d/7d change, stablecoin flag). Also returns a timestamp and a verifiable _proof bundle.

name: ChainRay Gas Optimization
description: Analyzes the last ~50 blocks of an EVM chain to recommend the cheapest window to transact: current base fee vs average with a verdict, per-window gas/utilization history, cheapest vs most-expensive window, potential savings, an estimated wait time, and plain-language recommendations.

chain.description: Target EVM chain (default base). EVM-only: one of base, ethereum, arbitrum, optimism, polygon, bsc, avalanche, zksync, linea, scroll, blast, mantle, gnosis, polygon-zkevm, mode, sei, celo, manta, taiko, fantom, cronos, opbnb, zora, worldchain, metis, fraxtal, kava, zetachain, filecoin, core-dao, aurora, moonbeam, klaytn, bob, canto.

usage.callShape: GET https://chainray.online/gas-optimization[?chain=<evm-chain>] -- x402 USDC on Base. chain query param is optional and defaults to base; EVM chains only (35-chain enum). No body, no path params.
usage.outputShape: chain, current.{baseFee,unit,vsAverage,verdict}, stats.{mean,min,max,volatility,avgUtilization,sampledBlocks}, windows[].{blocksAgo,avgGas,avgUtilization,relativeToMean}, optimization.{cheapestWindow,mostExpensiveWindow,potentialSavings,estimatedWaitTime}, recommendations[] (string advice), timestamp, _proof.{blockNumber,blockHash,blockTimestamp,chain,chainName,proofVersion,proofTimestamp,dataHash}
quirks: chain is a query param (NOT a path segment) and is optional -- defaults to base.
EVM chains only (35 supported); unlike gas-tracker it does not accept non-EVM chains like solana/bitcoin.

Analyzes ~50 recent blocks and bins them into ~5-block windows; on a very cheap/idle chain like Base every window can read the same sub-0.01 gwei value, so cheapestWindow==mostExpensiveWindow and potentialSavings '0%' -- expect more spread on busier chains like ethereum/polygon.
Fees are reported in gwei (current.unit); recommendations[] is human-readable advice (emoji-prefixed).
Every response carries a _proof object (Chain Proof v3 dataHash) verifiable via ChainRay's /verify-proof.
usage.guide: Recommends the cheapest window to transact on an EVM chain by analyzing ~50 recent blocks. GET https://chainray.online/gas-optimization[?chain=<evm-chain>] -- x402 USDC on Base ($0.005). chain query param is optional and defaults to base; EVM chains only (35-chain enum: base, ethereum, arbitrum, optimism, polygon, bsc, avalanche, zksync, linea, scroll, blast, mantle, gnosis, ...). No body, no path params, no API key. Use this (rather than gas-tracker) when you want binned gas history plus an actionable cheapest-window + potential-savings + wait-time recommendation. Output: chain, current.{baseFee,unit,vsAverage,verdict}, stats.{mean,min,max,volatility,avgUtilization,sampledBlocks}, windows[].{blocksAgo,avgGas,avgUtilization,relativeToMean}, optimization.{cheapestWindow,mostExpensiveWindow,potentialSavings,estimatedWaitTime}, recommendations[], timestamp, _proof.{...,dataHash}.

name: ChainRay Liquidation Alerts
description: Scans recent blocks on an EVM chain for Aave V3 lending-protocol liquidation events, returning a count, per-liquidation detail, and an overall risk level with a verifiable proof bundle.

chain.description: Target EVM chain (35-chain enum: base, ethereum, arbitrum, optimism, polygon, bsc, avalanche, zksync, linea, scroll, blast, mantle, gnosis, polygon-zkevm, mode, sei, celo, manta, taiko, fantom, cronos, opbnb, zora, worldchain, metis, fraxtal, kava, zetachain, filecoin, core-dao, aurora, moonbeam, klaytn, bob, canto). EVM chains only.

usage.callShape: GET https://chainray.online/liquidation-alerts[?chain=<evm-chain>] -- x402 USDC on Base. chain query param is optional and defaults to base; EVM chains only (35-chain enum). No body, no path params. Result returned inline in the 200; no polling.
usage.outputShape: chain, protocol (e.g. 'Aave V3'), blocksScanned, totalLiquidations, riskLevel (LOW|...), liquidations[] (empty when none in window; otherwise per-liquidation objects), note, timestamp, _proof.{blockNumber,blockHash,blockTimestamp,chain,chainName,proofVersion,proofTimestamp,dataHash}
quirks: Only input is the optional chain query param (NOT path/body); defaults to base. EVM chains only (35-chain enum), unlike some sibling endpoints that also accept non-EVM chains.
Currently monitors Aave V3 liquidations over a fixed recent window (blocksScanned=500 observed).
liquidations[] is empty when no liquidations occurred in the scanned window; riskLevel summarizes stress (LOW observed on base with 0 liquidations).
Every response carries a _proof object with a dataHash (Chain Proof v3, verifiable via /verify-proof).
usage.guide: Monitor recent lending-protocol (Aave V3) liquidation events on an EVM chain. GET https://chainray.online/liquidation-alerts[?chain=<evm-chain>] -- pay per call via x402 (USDC on Base, $0.01). chain query param is optional and defaults to base; EVM chains only (35-chain enum: base, ethereum, arbitrum, optimism, polygon, bsc, avalanche, zksync, linea, scroll, blast, mantle, gnosis, and more). No body or path params. Read totalLiquidations and riskLevel for a quick stress read, iterate liquidations[] for per-event detail (empty when none in the scanned window), and note carries a plain-English interpretation. body._proof carries a verifiable Chain Proof v3 bundle (dataHash). Verified 2026-07-30 with {chain:'base'} -> HTTP 200, totalLiquidations=0, riskLevel=LOW, $0.01 charged.

name: ChainRay Gas Average Oracle
description: Multi-chain gas price aggregate oracle: in one call, returns current gas prices (fast/standard/slow, Gwei) with trend for a comma-separated list of EVM chains and recommends the cheapest chain to transact on.

backends.inputSchema: queryParams: chains=<comma-separated evm-chain list> (optional, default 'base,ethereum,arbitrum,optimism,polygon'). EVM chains only.
backends.outputSchema: oracleType ('gas-aggregate'), chainsQueried, chainsResponded, feeds[].{chain,gasPrice,fast,standard,slow,unit,trend,error}, recommendation.{cheapestChain,standardGas,unit}, timestamp, _proof.{blockNumber,blockHash,blockTimestamp,chain,chainName,proofVersion,proofTimestamp,dataHash}

usage.callShape: GET https://chainray.online/oracle/gas-avg?chains=<comma-separated evm-chain list> -- x402 USDC on Base. chains query param is optional and defaults to 'base,ethereum,arbitrum,optimism,polygon'.
usage.outputShape: oracleType ('gas-aggregate'), chainsQueried, chainsResponded, feeds[].{chain,gasPrice,fast,standard,slow,unit,trend,error}, recommendation.{cheapestChain,standardGas,unit}, timestamp, _proof.{blockNumber,blockHash,blockTimestamp,chain,chainName,proofVersion,proofTimestamp,dataHash}
quirks: Multi-chain: the 'chains' query param is a COMMA-SEPARATED list (plural), not a single 'chain'; it defaults to 'base,ethereum,arbitrum,optimism,polygon' when omitted. (The 402 bazaar hint shows a singular 'chain:base' example but the actual param is 'chains'; openapi.json confirms 'chains'.)

Fixed price $0.005 (openapi x-payment-info mode=fixed); not dynamic. Note: llms.txt lists it as $0.02 but that is stale -- openapi.json, the 402 (maxAmountRequired 5000 = $0.005), and the live paid call all agree on $0.005.
Gas values are in Gwei. A chain that fails to respond comes back with gasPrice/fast/standard/slow=null and error (e.g. optimism was null in the verified run) rather than being dropped.
recommendation.cheapestChain picks the lowest standard gas among the responded chains.
Every response includes a _proof object (Chain Proof v3) with dataHash, verifiable via ChainRay's proof verification.
usage.guide: Multi-chain gas price aggregate. GET https://chainray.online/oracle/gas-avg?chains=<comma-separated evm-chain list> -- x402 USDC on Base, $0.005. chains is optional and defaults to 'base,ethereum,arbitrum,optimism,polygon'. In a single call you get feeds[] with per-chain gasPrice + fast/standard/slow (Gwei) and trend, and recommendation.cheapestChain naming the cheapest chain to transact on right now. Use this to decide WHERE (which chain) to transact; use ChainRay Gas Predict for a short-horizon forecast on ONE chain, ChainRay Gas Tracker for a single chain's current price, and ChainRay Gas History for a single chain's history. A non-responding chain returns null fields + an error string instead of being omitted. body._proof carries a verifiable Chain Proof v3 bundle (dataHash).

name: ChainRay Protocol TVL

name: CoinStats Exchange Price
description: CoinStats historical price of a crypto trading pair on a specific exchange (Binance, Coinbase, Kraken, etc.) at a given Unix timestamp, returned as a single conversion price. First-party CoinStats x402 endpoint (x402.coinstats.app); no API key.

exchange.description: Input/filter query param (name from the provider's own example; added during baked-query remediation so it stays discoverable).

from.description: Input/filter query param (name from the provider's own example; added during baked-query remediation so it stays discoverable).

to.description: Input/filter query param (name from the provider's own example; added during baked-query remediation so it stays discoverable).

timestamp.description: Input/filter query param (name from the provider's own example; added during baked-query remediation so it stays discoverable).

backends.outputSchema: JSON object: { price: number } — the price of the `from` currency expressed in the `to` currency on that exchange at that timestamp.

usage.callShape: GET https://x402.coinstats.app/coins/price/exchange with four REQUIRED query params: exchange, from, to, timestamp. No request body, no path params. First call returns HTTP 402 with x402 payment requirements; after signing an EIP-3009 USDC authorization it returns HTTP 200 with the price inline. Pays $0.001 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453).
usage.outputShape: Flat JSON object with a single field: price (number). Verified live: {"price":13.717421124828531} for exchange=Binance, from=BTC, to=ETH, timestamp=1636315200 (Nov 7 2021) — i.e. ~13.72 ETH per BTC at that time.
quirks: All four query params are required; from/to are currency SYMBOLS (BTC, ETH, USD, USDT), not coin-ids. The bazaar-extension example in the live 402 (from=bitcoin, to=usd) is a mis-generated placeholder — its example output 15.7349 is copied from the openapi and does not correspond to a bitcoin/usd price; the openapi symbol form is the real call.
timestamp is Unix seconds and selects a HISTORICAL price; there is no 'latest' shortcut on this operation.
Response is a single scalar wrapped in JSON ({price}); no metadata about which exchange/pair was resolved is echoed back.
Synchronous: the price is in the 200 body inline; no polling.
The x402/Bazaar wrapper also advertises a POST method variant, but GET is the canonical OpenAPI operation (get-coin-exchange-price) and is what was paid/verified.
usage.guide: CoinStats historical price of a trading pair on a specific exchange at a Unix timestamp. First-party CoinStats x402 endpoint; no API key.
