GET https://x402.coinstats.app/coins/price/exchange with four required query params: exchange (e.g. Binance), from (base symbol, e.g. BTC), to (target symbol, e.g. ETH), timestamp (Unix seconds, e.g. 1636315200). Pays $0.001 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453). Returns a flat JSON object {price:number} — the from-in-to conversion price on that exchange at that time (verified live: {"price":13.717421124828531}). Use it to look up a historical cross/exchange rate for a specific venue rather than a global average.

name: x402stock Spot
description: Live on-chain spot prices for every tradable pair on the Hyperliquid DEX (HYPE, PURR, wrapped BTC/ETH/SOL, and hundreds more) quoted against USDC/USDT0/USDE/USDH in one call: mark price, mid price, previous-day price, 24h USD and base volume, circulating and total supply, and market cap — sorted by 24h volume.

billing.description: amount is the price and is charged in full when you pay; a failed delivery is credited back in full. (Exact entries appear only on fixed-price requests - ceiling-priced requests are offered the reserve-and-pay-actual entry instead.)

usage.callShape: GET https://agents.x402stock.xyz/api/v1/spot — no query params, no path params, no request body. x402 USDC on Base (eip155:8453), fixed $0.02 per call (not dynamic).
usage.outputShape: JSON object: source ('x402stock'), as_of (ISO-8601 timestamp), venue ('hyperliquid'), market ('spot'), count (number of pairs), pairs[] — each { pair (e.g. 'HYPE/USDC'), id (Hyperliquid market id, e.g. '@107' or the pair symbol for the canonical listing), base_token, quote_token, canonical, mark_price, mid_price, prev_day_price, day_volume_usd, day_volume_base, circulating_supply, total_supply, market_cap_usd } — sorted descending by day_volume_usd.
quirks: Zero parameters — GET the bare URL, nothing else. For ONE token instead of the full list, the host separately exposes /api/v1/spot/{token} ($0.01) — a different, non-covered operation.

Verified live call returned 319 pairs. quote_token varies per pair (USDC, USDT0, USDE, or USDH) — the same base_token (e.g. HYPE, UBTC) can appear multiple times, once per quote currency it trades against.

mark_price/mid_price/prev_day_price/day_volume_usd/day_volume_base/circulating_supply/total_supply/market_cap_usd are all nullable per the schema; mid_price was observed null on a zero-volume pair (HYPE/USDH) in the verified response.

canonical:true was observed on exactly 1 of the 319 pairs (PURR/USDC) — Hyperliquid's own flagship native spot listing (id equals the pair symbol); the other 318 use canonical:false with a numeric Hyperliquid spot index as id (e.g. '@107').
Spot only — for perpetual-futures data (funding rate, open interest) use the separate /api/v1/perps family; for major-coin fiat quotes use /api/v1/crypto.

The live 402 also advertised an alternate MPP/Tempo payment rail (protocols.mpp, method 'tempo') alongside x402 in the same challenge; only the x402 USDC-on-Base accept was used and is recorded here — MPP/Tempo is a different protocol and out of scope for this registry.
usage.guide: Get every live Hyperliquid on-chain spot price in one call. GET https://agents.x402stock.xyz/api/v1/spot with no params and no body; pay the fixed $0.02 x402 USDC quote on Base and read the JSON. `pairs[]` is the full list (as_of/venue:'hyperliquid'/market:'spot'/count alongside it), each entry carrying `pair` (e.g. 'HYPE/USDC'), `base_token`/`quote_token`, `mark_price`/`mid_price`, `prev_day_price`, `day_volume_usd`/`day_volume_base`, `circulating_supply`/`total_supply`, `market_cap_usd`, and a `canonical` flag — sorted by 24h USD volume descending. Verified 2026-07-30: paid $0.02, got 319 pairs (top by volume: HYPE/USDC at mark_price 53.631). To price a single token instead of the whole market, use the separate /api/v1/spot/{token} operation.

name: SignalFuse Arena Strategy Signal
description: Directional crypto trading signal from a chosen SignalFuse arena strategy (VWAP reversion, EMA-5 breakout, RSI-7 extremes, or RSI reversion swing) for BTC/ETH/SOL/DOGE, returning long/short with a confidence score plus take-profit, stop-loss, hold-time and reasoning as synchronous JSON.

symbol.description: Crypto asset ticker (path parameter).

reason.description: Present when signal is null (e.g. no_signal, no_context)

usage.callShape: GET https://api.signalfuse.co/v1/arena/{strategy_id}/{symbol} — strategy_id + symbol are path params
usage.outputShape: Synchronous JSON. When a signal is active (per the 402 outputSchema example): { strategy_id:'vwap_reversion', strategy_name:'VWAP Reversion', symbol:'BTC', signal:'long'|'short', score:0.82 (0-1 confidence), tp_pct:0.015 (take-profit), sl_pct:0.008 (stop-loss), hold_time_sec:300, reasoning:'Bollinger band squeeze with volume expansion' }. When no signal is active (OBSERVED on the paid 200): { strategy_id:'vwap_reversion', symbol:'BTC', signal:null, reason:'no_signal' } — signal is null and a `reason` field explains why.
quirks: signal can be null: the paid 200 returned {signal:null, reason:'no_signal'} because no active setup existed at call time — still a valid, charged response (the paid strategy fields tp_pct/sl_pct/hold_time_sec/reasoning are only present when signal is non-null).
Fixed price ($0.001 = 1000 atomic USDC from the live 402 accept), not a dynamic quote; the 402 body says price 'varies' but the accepts amount is fixed at 1000.
strategy_id and symbol are PATH params (not query/body); vary them within the enums to hit other strategies/assets on the same endpoint.
Per the OpenAPI description, payment for each strategy goes to that strategy's own wallet, so payTo may differ across strategy_id values (this proposal's accept/payTo is captured for vwap_reversion).

Alternative access advertised in the 402 body (not used here): a 5-free-credit trial token via POST /v1/credits/trial {wallet} + x-credit-token header, or the browser playground at signalfuse.co/play (25 free calls/day).
Free (unpaid) companion endpoints exist but are not required for this call: GET /v1/arena/leaderboard (strategy standings), GET /v1/regime/preview, GET /v1/health.
usage.guide: Get a directional crypto trading signal from a SignalFuse arena strategy. Issue a GET to https://api.signalfuse.co/v1/arena/{strategy_id}/{symbol} choosing strategy_id (e.g. vwap_reversion) and symbol (e.g. BTC) from the enums, with no body, and pay the x402 quote (~$0.001 USDC on Base, no API key). On the 200, read the JSON: when `signal` is 'long' or 'short' you also get `score` (0-1 confidence), `tp_pct`/`sl_pct` (take-profit / stop-loss), `hold_time_sec`, and `reasoning`; when there is no active setup, `signal` is null and `reason` (e.g. 'no_signal') explains why — this null case still costs the fee. Synchronous, no polling.

name: SignalFuse Batch Signals
description: Returns fused directional trading signals (long/short/neutral, 0-100 strength, confidence, macro regime, and social/macro/market component scores) for multiple crypto assets in a single call — all 10 supported assets by default, or a comma-separated subset. Combines ModernFinBERT social sentiment, macro-regime classification, and market structure.

symbols.description: Comma-separated crypto symbols, e.g. BTC,ETH,SOL. Optional query param — omit for all 10 assets (BTC,ETH,SOL,DOGE,PEPE,WIF,BONK,ARB,OP,AVAX).

signals.description: Map of symbol to signal object

usage.callShape: GET https://api.signalfuse.co/v1/signal/batch (x402, $0.075 USDC on Base eip155:8453). Optional ?symbols=BTC,ETH,SOL query param; omit it to receive all 10 assets. Synchronous — the full signals payload is returned inline in the 200.
usage.outputShape: { signals: { <SYMBOL>: { symbol, signal: long|short|neutral, signal_strength (0-100 int), confidence (0-1), regime, components: { social:{score,label}, macro:{score,label}, market:{score,label} }, updated_at, data_age_seconds, stale } , ... }, count, related:[{path,price,why}] }. Observed with count:10 covering BTC,ETH,SOL,DOGE,PEPE,WIF,BONK,ARB,OP,AVAX.
quirks: At probe time every asset returned stale:true with large data_age_seconds (e.g. BTC ~125k s, ETH ~4.4M s) — signals can be stale; check per-asset data_age_seconds/stale before acting.
Component sub-scores are frequently 0/neutral (macro was 0 for all assets at probe time) and confidence can be 0 even when a signal is returned (e.g. BTC).
'symbols' query param is optional; omitting it returns all 10 supported assets (BTC,ETH,SOL,DOGE,PEPE,WIF,BONK,ARB,OP,AVAX).
Response includes a 'related' array pointing to /v1/regime ($0.001) for context on interpreting the signals.
Provider also offers a free credit-token path (POST /v1/credits/trial -> x-credit-token header) and a browser playground; the registry backend uses the x402 pay path.
usage.guide: Call GET https://api.signalfuse.co/v1/signal/batch to get fused directional trading signals for crypto assets in one x402-paid call ($0.075 USDC on Base). Omit query params to receive all 10 supported assets, or pass ?symbols=BTC,ETH,SOL for a subset. Each asset returns signal (long/short/neutral), signal_strength (0-100), confidence (0-1), macro regime, and social/macro/market component scores. Synchronous: the full payload is inline in the 200 (no polling). IMPORTANT: inspect each asset's data_age_seconds/stale field — data was stale for all assets at index time — and note confidence/component scores may be 0. For single-asset signals use GET /v1/signal/{symbol} ($0.010).

name: OttoAI Hyperliquid Market Data
description: Live Hyperliquid perpetuals market data for any tradable asset symbol: mark/oracle price, hourly and annualized funding rate, open interest, 24h volume, max leverage, size specs, and a top-of-book order book snapshot.

asset.description: Asset ticker symbol, e.g. BTC, ETH, SOL

market.description: symbol, assetId, maxLeverage, sizeDecimals, currentPrice, markPrice, oraclePrice, onlyIsolated, assetType, description, tradingUrl, fundingRateHourlyPct, fundingRateAnnualizedPct, openInterest, openInterestUsd, volume24hUsd, prevDayPrice, change24hPct, premiumPct, impactPrices{bid,ask}, orderBook{bestBid,bestAsk,mid,spread,spreadPct,bids[],asks[]}

usage.callShape: GET https://x402.ottoai.services/hyperliquid-market?asset={SYMBOL}. Single required query param 'asset' = the perpetual's ticker symbol (BTC, ETH, SOL, etc.). No request body. Pays $0.001 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453) or Polygon (eip155:137), USDC EIP-3009 or Permit2. Result returns inline in the 200 body (synchronous, no poll).
usage.outputShape: { status: 'success'|'failed', market: { symbol, assetId, maxLeverage, sizeDecimals, currentPrice, markPrice, oraclePrice, onlyIsolated, assetType, description, tradingUrl, butler_recommendations, fundingRateHourlyPct, fundingRateAnnualizedPct, openInterest, openInterestUsd, volume24hUsd, prevDayPrice, change24hPct, premiumPct, impactPrices:{bid,ask}, orderBook:{bestBid,bestAsk,mid,spread,spreadPct,bids:[{price,size,orders}],asks:[{price,size,orders}]} }, powered_by }. Price/size values are strings; funding/OI/volume values are numbers.
quirks: The 'asset' input is a QUERY param (?asset=BTC), NOT a path segment — the URL path is fixed at /hyperliquid-market for every symbol. Do not template the path per-asset.

Prices (currentPrice, markPrice, oraclePrice, prevDayPrice, order-book price/size) are returned as STRINGS; funding rates, openInterest, openInterestUsd, volume24hUsd, change24hPct, premiumPct are numbers. Callers must coerce.

fundingRate is reported in TWO fields: fundingRateHourlyPct (per-hour %) and fundingRateAnnualizedPct; both can be negative (shorts pay longs). Verified BTC live: hourly -0.000325%, annualized -2.8478%.
Response includes a promotional 'market.butler_recommendations' string and a top-level 'powered_by' tag ('[Powered by $OTTO AI | @useOttoAI]') — marketing text, not data.

Endpoint advertises SIWX (sign-in-with-x) eligibility for ~1hr free access on subsequent requests per the provider's openapi guidance, but each fresh call in this indexing was a paid x402 402->200; treat it as pay-per-call.
Also settleable on Polygon (eip155:137) USDC and via Permit2 for either chain, in addition to Base USDC.
usage.guide: Fetch live Hyperliquid perpetuals market data for a single asset symbol. GET https://x402.ottoai.services/hyperliquid-market?asset={SYMBOL} with the required query param 'asset' (e.g. BTC, ETH, SOL). No request body. Pays $0.001 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453) or Polygon (eip155:137). Synchronous — the JSON result is inline in the 200 body. Returns market.currentPrice / markPrice / oraclePrice, fundingRateHourlyPct + fundingRateAnnualizedPct, openInterest + openInterestUsd, volume24hUsd, maxLeverage, sizeDecimals, change24hPct, premiumPct, impactPrices, and a top-of-book orderBook (bestBid/bestAsk/mid/spread + top 5 bids/asks). Use it to read funding rates, open interest, and live perp pricing before sizing a Hyperliquid position.

name: OttoAI Stablecoin Watch
description: Live stablecoin peg-and-supply monitor: per-coin peg deviation (bps), circulating supply with 1d/7d/30d flow, market dominance and chain spread for the top USD stablecoins, plus a market-wide risk-on/risk-off narrative and downside depeg alerts for any coin trading >0.5% below peg. Sourced from DefiLlama, refreshed hourly.

inputSchema.description: No input. Plain GET; the 402 advertises an empty queryParams object and no body.

usage.callShape: GET https://x402.ottoai.services/stablecoin-watch — no query params, no body. Pay x402, retry, read JSON result inline at 200.
usage.outputShape: {status:'success', data:{totalCirculatingUsd, stablecoinCount, marketChange{d1Pct,d7Pct,d30Pct}, narrative, analysisStatus, generatedAt, topStablecoins[{name,symbol,priceUsd,pegDeviationBps,pegMechanism,circulatingUsd,dominancePct,change1dPct,change7dPct,change30dPct,chains[]}], depegAlerts[{name,symbol,priceUsd,circulatingUsd,pegDeviationBps}]}, meta{generatedAt,validUntil,stalenessSec,degraded,sourceHealth,inputSnapshotId}}. Observed: stablecoinCount=327, totalCirculatingUsd=306824326639, marketChange d30Pct=-1.096 (supply contracting), 4 depegAlerts led by apxUSD at -1304.4bps; topStablecoins returned the top 30 by dominance.
quirks: No input of any kind — plain GET. The x402 402 header advertises an empty queryParams object and no body.

Data is a snapshot sourced from DefiLlama, refreshed hourly: meta.validUntil / meta.stalenessSec / meta.degraded / meta.sourceHealth report freshness — the paid response was ~49 min into a 60-min window (stalenessSec 2944, degraded=false).

topStablecoins returns only the top ~30 by dominance, but stablecoinCount (327) reflects the full universe DefiLlama tracks; depegAlerts covers any tracked coin >0.5% below peg regardless of top-30 membership.

priceUsd and change*Pct can be null for some coins (e.g. USDX, M); a couple of yield-bearing 'stablecoins' (USYC, USDY) report priceUsd >1.13 with large positive pegDeviationBps — these are NAV-accruing tokens, not depegs.

Price is $0.001 (accepts amount '1000' atomic USDC = 6 decimals). Payable in USDC on Base or Polygon (EIP-3009 or Permit2) or Solana. x402 settles but the runtime reports confirmed=false with no txHash (common on this facilitator).
Provider offers a $0.001 money-back feedback endpoint (POST /feedback) and docs at docs.useotto.xyz; part of Otto AI's 81-endpoint x402 swarm.
usage.guide: Get a live stablecoin peg-and-supply dashboard in one paid call. GET https://x402.ottoai.services/stablecoin-watch with no params or body; pay $0.001 x402 (USDC on Base/Polygon via EIP-3009 or Permit2, or USDC on Solana) and read the JSON inline at 200 (synchronous, no polling). Returns market-wide totals and 1d/7d/30d supply flow, a risk-on/risk-off narrative, the top ~30 USD stablecoins with peg deviation (bps), price, dominance, per-coin flow and chain spread, and a depegAlerts list for any tracked coin >0.5% below peg. Data is DefiLlama-sourced and hourly — check meta.stalenessSec / meta.validUntil before acting.

name: OttoAI Yield Markets
description: Returns live DeFi yield-farming markets (supply APY, TVL, and vault/aToken addresses per token) across Aave V3 and Morpho on Base, Ethereum, Polygon, Arbitrum, Avalanche, and BSC, filterable by protocol, chain, or token symbol.

usage.callShape: GET https://x402.ottoai.services/yield-markets. No request body and no required params. Optional query filters (all default to 'ALL' when omitted): protocol (AAVE|MORPHO), chainId (numeric EVM chain id, e.g. 1, 8453, 137), tokenSymbol (e.g. USDC). Pays $0.001 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453) or Polygon (eip155:137); each network offers a plain-transfer and a permit2 accept variant.
usage.outputShape: { status: 'success'|'failed', count: <int>, filters: { protocol, chainId, tokenSymbol }, markets: [{ protocol ('AAVE'|'MORPHO'), tokenSymbol, tokenName, tokenAddress, supplyApy (number, in %), totalLiquidityUsd (number), chainId, chainName, ...AAVE-only: aTokenSymbol, aTokenAddress; ...MORPHO-only: vaultAddress, vaultSymbol, vaultName, vaultUrl }], powered_by }. Verified live: 182 markets returned across Ethereum, Base, Polygon, Arbitrum, Avalanche, BSC for Aave V3 and Morpho.
quirks: The OpenAPI 200 schema advertises a generic { status, data } shape, but the real response returns markets under a top-level 'markets' array (plus 'count', 'filters', 'powered_by') — code against the actual shape, not the openapi.json schema.
supplyApy is expressed as a percentage number (e.g. 49.27 means 49.27%), not a fraction.
AAVE rows carry aTokenSymbol/aTokenAddress; MORPHO rows carry vaultAddress/vaultSymbol/vaultName/vaultUrl. Consumers must branch on 'protocol' since these key sets are mutually exclusive.

Optional filters (protocol, chainId, tokenSymbol) are described in the 402 description but are NOT declared in openapi.json parameters; the returned 'filters' object echoes back what was applied (defaults 'ALL').
usage.guide: Compare DeFi lending/vault yields before deploying idle capital. GET https://x402.ottoai.services/yield-markets for all live Aave V3 + Morpho markets, or narrow with optional query filters protocol=AAVE|MORPHO, chainId=<evm-chain-id>, tokenSymbol=<SYMBOL>. Response is a JSON array of markets, each with supply APY (as a percent), TVL in USD, chain, token, and the vault (Morpho) or aToken (Aave) address. Costs $0.001 USDC per call via x402 on Base or Polygon; no API key or auth. Verified live returning 182 markets.

name: Greeneris Bitcoin Fees
description: Recommended Bitcoin transaction fee rates in sat/vB (fastest, half-hour, hour, economy, minimum) from mempool.space's live mempool, with an optional difficulty-retarget estimate (progress %, change %, remaining blocks/time).

include.description: Add the current difficulty retarget estimate (optional)

fees_sat_per_vb.description: Recommended fee rates in sat/vB: {fastest, half_hour, hour, economy, minimum}

difficulty_adjustment.description: Present only when ?include=difficulty: {progress_percent, difficulty_change_percent, estimated_retarget_date_ms, remaining_blocks, remaining_time_ms}

fee_estimates_sat_vb.description: Recommended fee rates keyed by horizon (fastest, half_hour, hour, economy, minimum); each is { sat_vb: integer, target: human-readable confirmation window }

congestion.description: Live mempool snapshot: { mempool_tx_count, mempool_vsize, mempool_total_fee_sat, estimated_backlog_blocks }

sources.description: { errors, partial, providers[] } — data provenance and degradation flags

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/btc/fees — no required input. Optional query param ?include=difficulty adds the difficulty retarget estimate. No body. x402 USDC on Base, no API key.
usage.outputShape: { ok:true, data:{ fees_sat_per_vb:{fastest,half_hour,hour,economy,minimum}, difficulty_adjustment?:{progress_percent,difficulty_change_percent,estimated_retarget_date_ms,remaining_blocks,remaining_time_ms}, source } } — all fee rates in sat/vB.
quirks: Response wraps the payload in { ok, data:{...} }; the fee rates live under data.fees_sat_per_vb.
No required input — calling with no query returns just fees_sat_per_vb + source.
difficulty_adjustment is only included when ?include=difficulty is passed.
Fee rates are in sat/vB (fastest/half_hour/hour/economy/minimum) sourced from mempool.space's live mempool snapshot; served with a 60s cache.
Bitcoin mainnet only. On the live 402 the service self-identifies as 'eu-verify' (shared Greeneris backend), but this route returns Bitcoin fee data as documented.
usage.guide: Get recommended Bitcoin transaction fee rates from the live mempool. GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/btc/fees with an optional ?include=difficulty to also get the difficulty retarget estimate. No body, no API key — pay $0.001 USDC on Base via x402. Output: { ok, data:{ fees_sat_per_vb:{fastest,half_hour,hour,economy,minimum}, difficulty_adjustment?:{...}, source } }, fee rates in sat/vB from mempool.space.

name: Greeneris Ethereum Gas
description: Live Ethereum mainnet gas pricing from PublicNode RPC: next-block base fee, 25/50/75th-percentile priority tips over the last 5 blocks (slow/std/fast), and a ready-to-sign max_fee recommendation — all in decimal gwei.

base_fee_gwei.description: Next-block base fee in decimal gwei

priority_fee_gwei.description: 25/50/75th-percentile priority tips over last 5 blocks: {slow, std, fast}

recommended.description: {speed, max_priority_fee_gwei, max_fee_gwei} — max_fee = 2*base + tip, ready to sign

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/eth/gas — no required input. Optional query param ?speed=slow|std|fast (default std) selects which priority-fee percentile (25/50/75th) drives the recommendation. No body. x402 USDC on Base, no API key.
usage.outputShape: { ok:true, data:{ base_fee_gwei, priority_fee_gwei:{slow,std,fast}, recommended:{speed, max_priority_fee_gwei, max_fee_gwei}, legacy_gas_price_gwei, blocks_sampled, source } } — all fee values in decimal gwei.
quirks: Response wraps the payload in { ok, data:{...} }; the fee fields live under data (the Bazaar output example omitted this ok/data envelope, but the OpenAPI example and the live 200 include it).
No required input — calling with no query uses speed=std for the recommendation.
?speed only changes which percentile is echoed in data.recommended; the full slow/std/fast priority_fee_gwei breakdown is always returned regardless of speed.
All values are decimal gwei (no hex parsing); max_fee = 2*base_fee + tip. Ethereum mainnet only.
Sourced from PublicNode RPC (eth_gasPrice + eth_feeHistory over the last 5 blocks); served with a 30s cache.
usage.guide: Get live Ethereum mainnet gas pricing (EIP-1559) with a ready-to-sign recommendation. GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/eth/gas with an optional ?speed=slow|std|fast (default std) to choose the 25/50/75th priority-fee percentile for the recommendation. No body, no API key — pay $0.002 USDC on Base via x402. Output: { ok, data:{ base_fee_gwei, priority_fee_gwei:{slow,std,fast}, recommended:{speed, max_priority_fee_gwei, max_fee_gwei}, legacy_gas_price_gwei, blocks_sampled, source } }, all in decimal gwei; max_fee = 2*base + tip.

name: Greeneris Pyth Oracle Prices
description: Real-time Pyth Network (Hermes) oracle crypto prices vs USD — aggregate price, confidence interval, EMA price and publish_time per asset — for 1-8 of a fixed set of major tickers, returned as normalized JSON.

symbols.description: Comma-separated tickers, 1-8 of: btc, eth, sol, bnb, xrp, ada, avax, doge, link, dot, usdc, usdt (query param, optional, default 'btc,eth').

prices.description: Map of ticker -> { price, conf, ema_price, publish_time }

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/oracle/pyth?symbols=btc,eth — single optional query param 'symbols' (comma-separated, 1-8 tickers; defaults to btc,eth). No body. x402 v2 USDC on Base, no API key; the payment is the auth.
usage.outputShape: { ok: boolean, data: { pair: 'USD', prices: { <ticker>: { price: number, conf: number, ema_price: number, publish_time: number (Unix seconds) }, ... }, source: string } } — e.g. { ok: true, data: { pair: 'USD', prices: { btc: { price: 64798.3475, conf: 19.50199679, ema_price: 64784.819, publish_time: 1785434494 }, eth: { price: 1919.28685419, conf: 0.56314581, ema_price: 1918.93558, publish_time: 1785434494 } }, source: 'Pyth Network via Hermes (permissionless oracle, sub-second updates)' } }
quirks: 'symbols' is an OPTIONAL query param (not path/body); omitting it returns btc,eth by default.
Ticker set is FIXED — 1-8 of: btc, eth, sol, bnb, xrp, ada, avax, doge, link, dot, usdc, usdt. Tickers are lowercase and priced vs USD (data.pair = 'USD').
Each asset carries a confidence interval (conf) and EMA price alongside the aggregate price — Pyth-specific fields useful for detecting oracle/spot divergence against a CEX.
publish_time is Unix SECONDS.
Result payload is wrapped in { ok, data } — the prices live under data.prices.
Server-side 30s cache — this is a permissionless oracle read, not a per-call live Hermes stream.
Sibling ops on the same host (e.g. /v1/fx/latest, /v1/stables/peg) are separate services, not variants of this one; only /v1/oracle/pyth exists under /oracle.
usage.guide: Real-time Pyth Network (Hermes) oracle crypto prices vs USD. GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/oracle/pyth with an optional query param symbols (comma-separated, 1-8 of btc,eth,sol,bnb,xrp,ada,avax,doge,link,dot,usdc,usdt; default btc,eth). No body, no API key — pay $0.005 USDC on Base via x402 v2. Response: { ok: true, data: { pair: 'USD', prices: { <ticker>: { price, conf, ema_price, publish_time } }, source } }; conf is the confidence/uncertainty band and ema_price the exponential moving average — cross-check against CEX spot to detect oracle/spot divergence. publish_time is Unix seconds; 30s server cache.

name: Greeneris Kalshi Prediction Markets
description: Live open markets from Kalshi, the CFTC-regulated US event exchange, most-traded first: ticker, title, yes bid/ask, mid-quote implied probability, 24h volume, open interest and close time, as normalized JSON.

series.description: Kalshi series_ticker filter (query param, optional), e.g. KXBTC, KXFED, KXCPIYOY

limit.description: Number of markets to return (query param, optional, default 10)

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/predict/kalshi?series=KXFED&limit=5 — both query params optional (series = Kalshi series_ticker filter e.g. KXBTC/KXFED/KXCPIYOY; limit = 1-25, default 10). No body. x402 USDC on Base, no API key; the payment is the auth.
usage.outputShape: { ok: boolean, data: { series, count, markets: [{ ticker, title, subtitle, yes_bid, yes_ask, implied_prob, last_price, volume_24h, open_interest, close_time }], source } } — e.g. { ok: true, data: { series: 'KXFED', count: 5, markets: [{ ticker: 'KXFED-27MAR-T3.50', title: 'Will the upper bound of the federal funds rate be above 3.50% following the Fed's Mar 17, 2027 meeting?', subtitle: '3.50%', yes_bid: 0.33, yes_ask: 0.62, implied_prob: 0.475, last_price: 0.56, volume_24h: 249.92, open_interest: 1135.01, close_time: '2027-03-17T17:55:00Z' }], source: 'Kalshi Trade API v2 ...' } }
quirks: Both params are optional query params (not path/body); calling with no params returns the 10 most-traded markets across all series.
Prices are in USD 0-1 (Kalshi contract convention): yes_bid/yes_ask/last_price and implied_prob are all fractions where 1.00 = $1 payout / 100% probability.
Result payload is wrapped in { ok, data } — the markets live under data.markets.
Data is sourced live from the public Kalshi Trade API v2 (CFTC-regulated event exchange) with a ~5min cache — not a real-time tick feed.

Distinct sibling ops on the same host: /v1/predict/polymarket is a separate service (different venue/dataset/schema), not a variant of this one. The provider suggests cross-referencing it for venue spreads.
usage.guide: Live Kalshi prediction-market quotes as normalized JSON. GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/predict/kalshi with optional query params series (Kalshi series_ticker filter, e.g. KXBTC/KXFED/KXCPIYOY) and limit (1-25, default 10). No body, no API key — pay $0.01 USDC on Base via x402. Response: { ok: true, data: { series, count, markets: [{ ticker, title, subtitle, yes_bid, yes_ask, implied_prob, last_price, volume_24h, open_interest, close_time }], source } }. Prices/probabilities are 0-1 fractions; markets are returned most-traded first; ~5min cache. Use /v1/predict/polymarket for the Polymarket venue.

name: Greeneris Polymarket Prediction Markets
description: Top open Polymarket prediction markets for a topic tag, ranked by 24h volume: event title, slug, end date, and per-market Yes/No outcome probabilities (0-1) with USD volume, sourced from the public Polymarket Gamma API (live on-chain odds).

tag.description: Polymarket tag slug, e.g. crypto, politics, economy, fed (query param, optional)

limit.description: Number of events to return (query param, optional)

probabilities.description: Map of outcome label (e.g. Yes/No) -> probability (0-1)

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/predict/polymarket?tag=crypto&limit=3 — both query params optional (tag defaults to crypto, limit defaults to 5). No body. x402 USDC on Base, no API key; the payment is the auth.
usage.outputShape: { ok: boolean, data: { tag: string, events: [ { title, slug, end_date (ISO), volume_24h_usd (number), markets: [ { question, probabilities: { <outcome>: number 0-1 }, volume_24h_usd } ] } ], source: string } } — e.g. { ok: true, data: { tag: 'crypto', events: [ { title: 'What price will Bitcoin hit in July?', slug: 'what-price-will-bitcoin-hit-in-july-2026', end_date: '2026-08-01T04:00:00Z', volume_24h_usd: 1360093.6, markets: [ { question: 'Will Bitcoin reach $67,500 in July?', probabilities: { Yes: 0.0255, No: 0.9745 }, volume_24h_usd: 267406.47 } ] } ], source: 'Polymarket Gamma API (live on-chain prediction-market odds)' } }
quirks: tag and limit are optional query params (not path/body); calling with no params returns top crypto events (limit 5).
tag is any Polymarket tag slug (crypto, politics, economy, fed, ...); an unknown/empty tag simply yields no events.
limit is clamped to 1..10.
Result payload is wrapped in { ok, data } — events live under data.events, each event's per-outcome odds under markets[].probabilities.
Probabilities are on-chain Polymarket Gamma odds (0-1); events are ranked by 24h USD volume. 5-minute cache.
Sibling op /v1/predict/kalshi is a separate service (Kalshi exchange dataset), not a variant of this one.
usage.guide: Live Polymarket prediction-market odds as normalized JSON. GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/predict/polymarket with optional query params tag (Polymarket tag slug, default crypto) and limit (1-10 events, default 5). No body, no API key — pay $0.01 USDC on Base via x402. Response: { ok: true, data: { tag, events: [ { title, slug, end_date, volume_24h_usd, markets: [ { question, probabilities: { Yes, No, ... }, volume_24h_usd } ] } ], source } }. Events are ranked by 24h volume; probabilities are on-chain Gamma odds (0-1). 5-minute cache. Use /v1/predict/kalshi for Kalshi-exchange markets.

name: Greeneris Stablecoin Depeg Monitor
description: Depeg-risk monitor for USD stablecoins (USDT, USDC, DAI, FDUSD, TUSD, USDe, PYUSD): DeFiLlama market-aggregate price per coin converted to a deviation from $1.00 in basis points, with a depeg_alert flag (fires beyond 50 bps) and the worst deviation across the set.

symbols.description: Comma-separated stablecoins from USDT, USDC, DAI, FDUSD, TUSD, USDE, PYUSD (max 8), query param, optional

pegs.description: Map of <SYMBOL> -> { price: number, deviation_bps: number, depeg_alert: boolean }

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/stables/peg?symbols=USDT,USDC,DAI — single optional query param `symbols` (comma-separated tickers, max 8; defaults to USDT,USDC,DAI when omitted). No body. x402 USDC on Base, no API key; the payment is the auth.
usage.outputShape: { ok: boolean, data: { pegs: { <SYMBOL>: { price: number, deviation_bps: number, depeg_alert: boolean } }, peg: string, max_abs_deviation_bps: number, any_depeg_alert: boolean, source: string } } — e.g. { ok: true, data: { pegs: { USDT: { price: 0.998878, deviation_bps: -11.22, depeg_alert: false }, USDC: { price: 0.999749, deviation_bps: -2.51, depeg_alert: false } }, peg: 'USD', max_abs_deviation_bps: 11.22, any_depeg_alert: false, source: 'DeFiLlama market-aggregate stablecoin prices (peggedUSD, live)' } }
quirks: `symbols` is an optional query param (not path/body); calling with no params monitors USDT,USDC,DAI by default.
Supported tickers only: USDT, USDC, DAI, FDUSD, TUSD, USDE, PYUSD (max 8 per call).
Result payload is wrapped in { ok, data } — the per-coin pegs live under data.pegs.
This is a derived risk signal (deviation in bps vs $1.00), not a raw price feed; depeg_alert fires beyond 50 bps. Served with a 60s cache.
Sibling op /v1/stables/supply (circulating supply + mint/burn flows) is a separate service, not a variant of this one.
usage.guide: Stablecoin depeg-risk monitor. GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/stables/peg with optional query param `symbols` (comma-separated tickers from USDT, USDC, DAI, FDUSD, TUSD, USDE, PYUSD, max 8; defaults to USDT,USDC,DAI). No body, no API key — pay $0.02 USDC on Base via x402. Response: { ok: true, data: { pegs: { <SYMBOL>: { price, deviation_bps, depeg_alert } }, peg, max_abs_deviation_bps, any_depeg_alert, source } }. Deviation is bps from $1.00 (DeFiLlama market-aggregate prices); depeg_alert fires beyond 50 bps; 60s cache. Use /v1/stables/supply for circulating supply and mint/burn flows.

name: Greeneris Stablecoin Supply
description: Circulating supply per stablecoin from DeFiLlama with computed net flows (delta_24h/delta_7d/delta_30d = net mint minus burn), peg type, peg mechanism and current price.

backends.inputSchema: Query params (GET, no body): symbol (string, optional) — stablecoin ticker e.g. USDT to get one asset; top (integer 1-50, default 10, optional) — number of largest stablecoins by supply to return. Provide symbol OR top; omit both to get the default top 10.
backends.outputSchema: ok (bool), data.count (int), data.stablecoins[] {name, symbol, peg_type, peg_mechanism, price, circulating, delta_24h, delta_7d, delta_30d}, data.source (string)

backends.inputSchema: Query params (GET, no body): symbol (string, optional) — stablecoin ticker (e.g. DAI, USDT, USDC) or a DefiLlama id; address (string, optional) — contract address as an alternative to symbol; chain (string, optional) — chain to prefer for the on-chain cross-check. Provide symbol OR address.
backends.outputSchema: symbol, name, llama_id (string), supply { circulating_total (number, all chains), per_chain { <ChainName>: number }, chain_count (int) }, onchain_verification { available (bool), chain, network, address, onchain_total_supply (number), onchain_total_supply_raw (string), defillama_chain_circulating (number), divergence_flag (bool), relative_diff (number), attribution (string) }, divergence_flag (bool), provenance { source, dataset }, attribution (string[]), disclaimer (string).

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/stables/supply with optional query params. ?symbol=USDT returns one stablecoin; ?top=10 (1-50, default 10) returns the largest by supply. No request body. No API key. Pays $0.005 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453). Served with a 30min cache.
usage.outputShape: ok=true; data.count (number of stablecoins returned); data.stablecoins[] each = {name, symbol, peg_type (e.g. peggedUSD), peg_mechanism (e.g. fiat-backed), price, circulating (units in circulation), delta_24h, delta_7d, delta_30d (net mint minus burn over each window)}; data.source ("DeFiLlama (stablecoins.llama.fi)").
quirks: Two mutually-informative query modes: ?symbol=<ticker> for a single stablecoin, or ?top=<n> (1-50, default 10) for the n largest by supply. With no params it returns the default top 10.
delta_24h/delta_7d/delta_30d are NET FLOWS (net mint minus burn) in the same units as circulating, and can be negative (verified: USDT delta_24h was -627805601.23 at index time).
price is the current DeFiLlama-reported price and may be slightly off $1.00 (verified USDT price 0.99887... ).
Data is served with a 30-minute cache; source is DeFiLlama (stablecoins.llama.fi).
402 resource labels the service internally as 'eu-verify' (the parent Greeneris API title); this specific route is the stablecoin-supply operation.
usage.guide: Circulating supply per stablecoin from DeFiLlama with computed net flows and peg metadata. GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/stables/supply — optional query params: symbol (ticker, e.g. USDT, for one asset) or top (1-50, default 10, largest by supply); no body, no API key. Pays $0.005 USDC via x402 on Base. Output: ok=true; data.count; data.stablecoins[] {name, symbol, peg_type, peg_mechanism, price, circulating, delta_24h, delta_7d, delta_30d}; data.source ("DeFiLlama (stablecoins.llama.fi)"). delta_* fields are net mint-minus-burn flows and can be negative; served with a 30min cache.

name: Greeneris Crypto Implied Volatility (DVOL)
description: Deribit DVOL index (30-day annualized implied volatility from the options order book) for BTC or ETH, delivered as a risk signal with current level, 24h change, and min/max/percentile over a lookback window.

asset.description: Underlying asset (query param, optional)

window.description: Lookback window for percentile and range (query param, optional)

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/vol/dvol?asset=BTC&window=30d — both query params optional (asset defaults to BTC, window defaults to 30d). No body. x402 USDC on Base, no API key; the payment is the auth.
usage.outputShape: { ok: boolean, data: { asset, dvol (number, IV %), change_24h (number), window, window_percentile (number), window_min (number), window_max (number), as_of (ISO timestamp), source } } — e.g. { ok: true, data: { asset: 'BTC', dvol: 35.56, change_24h: -2.69, window: '30d', window_percentile: 0.4, window_min: 35.36, window_max: 44.66, as_of: '2026-07-30T17:00:00+00:00', source: 'Deribit DVOL implied volatility index (public API, 30-day annualized IV)' } }
quirks: asset and window are optional query params (not path/body); enums are asset=BTC|ETH and window=7d|30d|90d.
Result payload is wrapped in { ok, data } — the volatility fields live under data.
Values derive from Deribit public volatility-index candles (30-day annualized IV) with a 5-minute cache — not a per-tick live feed.
window_percentile ranks the current dvol within the lookback window (0 = at the low, 100 = at the high).
usage.guide: Deribit DVOL crypto implied-volatility index as normalized JSON. GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/vol/dvol with optional query params asset (BTC|ETH, default BTC) and window (7d|30d|90d, default 30d). No body, no API key — pay $0.02 USDC on Base via x402. Response: { ok: true, data: { asset, dvol, change_24h, window, window_percentile, window_min, window_max, as_of, source } }. dvol is the 30-day annualized implied volatility level; window_percentile/min/max frame it against the lookback range. 5-minute cache.

name: Arkham Cluster Summary
description: Return summary statistics for an Arkham address cluster (a group of onchain addresses attributed to the same actor) by its cluster ID: total number of addresses, all-time USD volume, current USD balance, and first/last transaction timestamps.

id.description: The ID of the Arkham cluster to summarize (a 72-hex-char cluster identifier).

outputSchema.description: Cluster summary statistics: clusterId, numAddresses (int), volumeUsd (number), balanceUsd (number), firstTx (ISO timestamp), lastTx (ISO timestamp).

usage.callShape: POST application/json body {"id": "<arkham-cluster-id>"} to https://api.arkm.com/x402/cluster/summary; result returned inline in the 200 response body (synchronous).
usage.outputShape: JSON object with cluster-level aggregates: clusterId (string, the queried cluster id), numAddresses (integer, e.g. 1911969), volumeUsd (number, all-time USD volume, e.g. 1831352221536.44), balanceUsd (number, current USD balance, e.g. 405289757.85), firstTx (ISO 8601 timestamp of first transaction), lastTx (ISO 8601 timestamp of most recent transaction).
usage.quirks: Requires an Arkham cluster ID (a 72-char hex string), not a wallet address or entity slug — clusters group addresses attributed to the same actor. Distinct from the sibling ops /tag/summary and /intelligence/entity-summary. Static $0.20 (not a dynamic ceiling) — the live 402 description says '$0.20 per call' and quotes 200000 base units on both Base and Solana USDC; an empty body returns the same 402 (no dynamic re-quote needed).
usage.needs: An Arkham cluster ID (72-hex-char string), e.g. "00000002aae817c1a0d2ec3c91ede74c64c92c83658decdad52b591451948d75a9ca".
usage.guide: Call POST https://api.arkm.com/x402/cluster/summary with a JSON body {"id": "<cluster-id>"}. Pay the x402 402 with USDC on Base (or Solana). The cluster summary object (numAddresses, volumeUsd, balanceUsd, firstTx, lastTx) comes back inline in the 200 response — no polling.

name: Arkham Address History
description: Get the historical daily USD portfolio value of a blockchain address over time, broken down per chain, using Arkham's onchain intelligence.

address.description: The blockchain address to query historical portfolio data for. EVM addresses are lowercased at ingress; Solana addresses are preserved.

chains.description: Optional. Chains to filter by, as a single comma-separated value (e.g. 'ethereum,bsc'). If omitted, returns data across all supported chains.

outputSchema.description: Map keyed by chain slug (e.g. ethereum, bsc, arbitrum_one). Each value is an array of daily portfolio-value points.

usd.description: Total USD value held on that chain on that day

usage.callShape: POST https://api.arkm.com/x402/history/address with JSON body {"address":"<blockchain address>"} and optional {"chains":"ethereum,bsc"}. No API key, no signup. Pays $0.20 USDC via x402 (HTTP 402) on Base (eip155:8453) or Solana; the result time series is returned inline in the 200 body.
usage.outputShape: JSON object keyed by chain slug (e.g. ethereum, bsc, arbitrum_one, polygon, ...). Each value is an array of daily points {time (ISO 8601 UTC day), usd (number = total USD portfolio value held on that chain that day)}. Verified live for 0x28C6c06298d514Db089934071355E5743bf21d60 (Binance hot wallet): ~568KB response spanning many chains from 2023 onward.
quirks: Fixed $0.20 per call (openapi x-payment-info mode:fixed) — this is NOT a dynamic worst-case ceiling; it is the real price.
Output is a per-chain map, not a flat array — iterate object keys (chain slugs) then the daily {time,usd} arrays under each. Response can be large (hundreds of KB) for active, long-lived addresses.
'usd' is the total USD portfolio VALUE snapshot for that day, not a flow/volume; it can be very large for exchange hot wallets.
By-ADDRESS lookup; the sibling POST /x402/history/entity is the by-ENTITY equivalent (input field 'entity', $0.40) and is a separate service.
Address fields are canonicalized at ingress: EVM addresses are lowercased, Solana addresses preserved.
400 = missing/invalid body, 404 = address not found upstream; neither is charged (only successful upstream requests settle payment).
usage.guide: Get the historical daily USD portfolio value of a blockchain address over time, per chain, via Arkham's onchain intelligence. POST https://api.arkm.com/x402/history/address with JSON body {"address":"<address>"} (optionally {"chains":"ethereum,bsc"} to filter). No API key; pays a fixed $0.20 USDC via x402 on Base or Solana. Response (inline in the 200) is a JSON object keyed by chain slug (ethereum, bsc, arbitrum_one, ...); each value is an array of daily points {time (ISO 8601 UTC), usd (total USD value on that chain that day)}. Iterate object keys, not a flat array; responses can be hundreds of KB for active wallets. This is the by-address variant; use /x402/history/entity for a by-entity ($0.40) lookup.

name: Arkham Address Intelligence
description: Look up Arkham's onchain intelligence for a single blockchain address: the attributed entity (name, type, and social/Crunchbase/LinkedIn links), the human-readable address label, chain, and contract/user-address flags.

address.description: The blockchain address to query. EVM addresses are lowercased at ingress; Solana addresses preserved.

chain.description: Optional. Blockchain network to query (e.g. ethereum). Only one network is used; if omitted, the address's chain is auto-detected.

arkhamEntity.description: Attributed entity: name, id, type (e.g. cex), note, service, website, twitter, crunchbase, linkedin

arkhamLabel.description: Human-readable address label: name, address, chainType

usage.callShape: POST https://api.arkm.com/x402/intelligence/address with JSON body {"address": "<blockchain address>"}. Optional "chain" field (e.g. "ethereum") pins the network; if omitted the chain is auto-detected. Any extra body field becomes an Arkham query parameter. Pays a fixed $0.20 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453) or Solana. Synchronous JSON result returned inline in the 200.
usage.outputShape: Top-level object: address, chain, arkhamEntity{name,id,type,note,service,website,twitter,crunchbase,linkedin}, arkhamLabel{name,address,chainType}, isUserAddress (bool), contract (bool). Live verified: 0x28C6c0...1d60 -> {chain:"ethereum", arkhamEntity.name:"Binance", arkhamEntity.type:"cex", arkhamLabel.name:"Hot Wallet", arkhamLabel.chainType:"evm", isUserAddress:false, contract:false}.
quirks: Fixed $0.20 per call (Arkham x-payment-info mode:fixed and the live 402 both quote 200000 base-unit USDC = $0.20); not a dynamic empty-body ceiling.
An address with no Arkham attribution still returns 200; arkhamEntity/arkhamLabel fields may be absent or empty rather than an error.
Distinct from the pricier siblings /intelligence/address-enriched ($0.40), /intelligence/address-all ($0.40, all chains), and batch variants ($50-$200) — this base op is single-address, single-chain.
EVM addresses are canonicalized (lowercased) at ingress; Solana addresses are preserved as-is.
usage.guide: Look up Arkham's onchain intelligence for a single blockchain address. POST https://api.arkm.com/x402/intelligence/address with JSON body {"address": "<address>"} (optional "chain" to pin the network; auto-detected otherwise). Pays a fixed $0.20 USDC via x402 on Base or Solana — no API key. Returns synchronously: the attributed entity (arkhamEntity: name, type such as cex, and social/Crunchbase/LinkedIn links), a human-readable address label (arkhamLabel: name, chainType), the chain, and isUserAddress/contract flags. Use for pre-trade wallet due diligence and counterparty identification. Example: {"address":"0x28C6c06298d514Db089934071355E5743bf21d60"} resolves to Binance's Hot Wallet.

name: Arkham Contract Intelligence
description: Look up Arkham's onchain intelligence for a deployed smart contract: its deployer (attributed entity + label), internal deployer, proxy status and implementation/proxy address, deployment block timestamp and transaction hash, bytecode, and function sighashes.

chain.description: Blockchain network where the contract is deployed (e.g. ethereum). Required.

address.description: The contract address to query. Required. EVM addresses are lowercased at ingress; Solana addresses preserved. Any extra body field becomes an Arkham query parameter.

functionSighashes.description: Array of function selector sighashes, or null.

proxyAddress.description: Implementation/proxy address when isProxy is true.

deployer.description: Deployer address with arkhamEntity{name,id,type,note,service,website,twitter,crunchbase,linkedin}, arkhamLabel{name,address,chainType}, chain, contract, isUserAddress.

internalDeployer.description: Internal (factory) deployer, same shape as deployer.

usage.callShape: POST https://api.arkm.com/x402/intelligence/contract with JSON body {"chain": "<network>", "address": "<contract address>"} (both required). Any extra body field becomes an Arkham query parameter. Pays a fixed $0.20 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453) or Solana. Synchronous JSON result returned inline in the 200.
usage.outputShape: Top-level object: address, blockTimestamp, bytecode, functionSighashes (array|null), isProxy (bool), proxyAddress, transactionHash, deployer{address, chain, arkhamEntity{name,id,type,note,service,website,twitter,crunchbase,linkedin}, arkhamLabel{name,address,chainType}, contract, isUserAddress}, internalDeployer{same shape}. Live verified: {chain:"ethereum", address:"0xA0b8...eB48" (USDC)} -> {isProxy:true, proxyAddress:"0xa2327a938...cbDCF", blockTimestamp:"2018-08-03T19:28:24Z", deployer.arkhamEntity.name:"Circle", deployer.arkhamEntity.type:"stablecoin", deployer.arkhamLabel.name:"Deployer", transactionHash:"0xe7e0fe39...75895"}.
quirks: Fixed $0.20 per call (402 resource description says '$0.20 per call'; openapi x-guidance says '$0.20 per Arkham credit'; live 402 quotes 200000 base-unit USDC = $0.20); not a dynamic empty-body ceiling.
Both chain AND address are required — unlike /intelligence/address where chain is optional/auto-detected. An empty or invalid body returns 400 (not charged).
isProxy/proxyAddress distinguish proxy contracts from direct deployments; deployer vs internalDeployer separates the EOA/factory that submitted the deploy tx from the internal creator.
EVM addresses are canonicalized (lowercased) at ingress; Solana addresses are preserved as-is. Failed upstream Arkham requests are not charged.
Rate limit ~20 req/sec per payer wallet on this endpoint.
usage.guide: Look up Arkham's onchain intelligence for a deployed smart contract. POST https://api.arkm.com/x402/intelligence/contract with JSON body {"chain":"<network>","address":"<contract address>"} (both required). Pays a fixed $0.20 USDC via x402 on Base or Solana — no API key. Returns synchronously: the deployer (deployer.arkhamEntity: name, type, and social/Crunchbase/LinkedIn links; arkhamLabel: name, chainType), the internalDeployer (factory/internal creator), proxy status (isProxy) and proxyAddress, deployment blockTimestamp and transactionHash, bytecode, and functionSighashes. Use for contract due diligence, deployer/factory attribution, and proxy-vs-direct detection before interacting with a contract. Example: {"chain":"ethereum","address":"0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48"} (USDC) resolves to deployer Circle, isProxy true.

name: Arkham Entity Predictions
description: Given an Arkham entity ID (e.g. "binance"), return the addresses Arkham predicts belong to that entity, each with its current USD balance — from Arkham's onchain intelligence attribution engine.

entity.description: The Arkham entity ID to retrieve address predictions for (e.g. "binance").

usage.callShape: POST https://api.arkm.com/x402/intelligence/entity-predictions  body={"entity":"binance"}
usage.outputShape: Array of objects, each {address:string, entityID:string, usdBalance:number} — one per predicted address attributed to the entity, sorted by USD balance descending.
quirks: Pure x402, no API key. Base USDC (eip155:8453) or Solana USDC accepted.
Fixed price $0.20 per call (200000 raw / 6 decimals) — the 402 description states "$0.20 per call"; not a dynamic worst-case ceiling.
Synchronous: full result array returned inline in the 200 body, no poll.
'entity' must be an Arkham entity ID (slug like "binance"), not a raw address — discover IDs via Arkham search/entity endpoints.
Verified: {"entity":"binance"} returned ~large array of attributed addresses with usdBalance (top address ~$927M).
usage.guide: Get the addresses Arkham predicts belong to an entity, each with its USD balance. POST https://api.arkm.com/x402/intelligence/entity-predictions with body={"entity":"<arkham-entity-id>"} (e.g. "binance"). Returns an array of {address, entityID, usdBalance} inline in the 200 (synchronous). Pure x402 — pay $0.20 USDC on Base or Solana, no API key.

name: Arkham Entity Summary
description: Get Arkham's onchain summary statistics for a labeled entity (e.g. an exchange, fund, or protocol): the number of addresses attributed to it, lifetime USD transfer volume, current USD balance, and the timestamps of its first and last observed transactions.

entity.description: The entity ID to retrieve summary statistics for (Arkham entity slug, e.g. 'binance').

numAddresses.description: Number of onchain addresses attributed to this entity.

volumeUsd.description: Lifetime USD transfer volume attributed to the entity.

balanceUsd.description: Current total USD balance held across the entity's addresses.

firstTx.description: Timestamp of the entity's first observed transaction (ISO 8601).

lastTx.description: Timestamp of the entity's most recent observed transaction (ISO 8601).

usage.callShape: POST https://api.arkm.com/x402/intelligence/entity-summary with JSON body { entity } — pay per call via x402 (USDC on Base or Solana). Result is returned inline in the 200; no polling.
usage.outputShape: Flat JSON object: { entityId (echoed slug), numAddresses (count of attributed addresses), volumeUsd (lifetime USD transfer volume), balanceUsd (current total USD balance), firstTx (ISO timestamp of first tx), lastTx (ISO timestamp of most recent tx) }. Verified run for 'binance' returned numAddresses 65002477, volumeUsd 49350159716067.305, balanceUsd 167698023165.0905, firstTx 2017-06-19T06:17:43Z, lastTx 2026-07-29T23:59:59Z.
quirks: The `entity` input is an Arkham entity slug/id (e.g. 'binance'), not a wallet address — use Arkham's search/entity endpoints or a known slug to obtain it.
Flat $0.20 per call: the 402 description states '$0.20 per call' and both the empty-body and real-body probes quote amount 200000 (=$0.20), so this is not a dynamic worst-case ceiling.
Pure x402, no API key required. Pay via USDC on Base (eip155:8453) or Solana; result is synchronous inline in the 200.
usage.guide: Look up Arkham's onchain summary stats for a labeled entity. POST https://api.arkm.com/x402/intelligence/entity-summary with JSON body {"entity":"<arkham entity slug, e.g. binance>"}; pay per call via x402 ($0.20 USDC on Base or Solana, no API key). The 200 returns a flat object with numAddresses, volumeUsd (lifetime transfer volume), balanceUsd (current holdings), and firstTx/lastTx timestamps. Result is synchronous; no polling. Verified 2026-07-30 with {entity:'binance'} -> HTTP 200, $0.20 charged (tx 0x2d7cb7d131966009227d0989d294a93262675581f7ec6ecf110109ff0dc0181a).

name: Arkham Entity Types
description: Lists the full set of supported Arkham entity-type labels (e.g. cex, dex, defi, bridge, stablecoin, nft-marketplace, hacker, scam) used to classify onchain entities across Arkham's crypto-intelligence dataset.

inputSchema.description: Empty JSON body {} — this endpoint takes no input parameters.

outputSchema.description: Flat array of entity-type label strings.

usage.callShape: POST https://api.arkm.com/x402/intelligence/entity-types with an empty JSON body {} (Content-Type: application/json). No input parameters. Pays a fixed $0.20 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453) or Solana. Result is returned inline (synchronous).
usage.outputShape: Top-level JSON array of entity-type label strings, e.g. ["gaming","derivatives","misc","nft-marketplace","hacker","dex","defi","bridge","stablecoin","cex","scam","nft", ...]. No wrapping object; ~51 labels in the live response.
quirks: Fixed price: the 402 quotes $0.20 on an empty body and the body IS empty by design (input schema requires {} with additionalProperties:false), so $0.20 is the real per-call price, not a worst-case ceiling.
GET returns 405 — POST only.
Response is a bare JSON array of strings (no {data:...} envelope).
Pure x402: the icon/serviceName in the 402 resource block are cosmetic; no API key is ever required.
This is a reference/lookup endpoint — the returned labels are the vocabulary used by other Arkham intelligence endpoints (entity, entity-summary) to type onchain entities.
usage.guide: Use this to enumerate the entity-type taxonomy Arkham uses to classify onchain entities before calling other Arkham intelligence endpoints. Call it with POST https://api.arkm.com/x402/intelligence/entity-types and an empty JSON body {}; no parameters are accepted. It costs a flat $0.20 USDC per call over x402 (Base USDC or Solana USDC), returns synchronously, and the body is a flat JSON array of label strings (cex, dex, defi, bridge, stablecoin, nft-marketplace, hacker, scam, dao, oracle, etc.). Verified live 2026-07-30: paid $0.20, HTTP 200, 51 labels returned.

name: Arkham Entity Intelligence
description: Look up Arkham's onchain intelligence for a known entity (e.g. exchange, protocol, fund) by its Arkham entity ID, returning its profile, classification/type, linked social + web + Crunchbase/LinkedIn references, and its populated Arkham tags.

entity.description: The Arkham entity ID to query (e.g. "binance").

outputSchema.description: Arkham entity intelligence object: name, id, type (e.g. cex), website, twitter, crunchbase, linkedin, note, customized, service, and populatedTags[] (id/label/rank/tagParams).

usage.callShape: POST application/json body {"entity": "<arkham-entity-id>"} to https://api.arkm.com/x402/intelligence/entity; result returned inline in the 200 response body (synchronous).
usage.outputShape: JSON object with the entity's profile: name, id, type (classification e.g. "cex"), website, twitter, crunchbase, linkedin, note, customized (bool), service, and populatedTags[] (each {id, label, rank, excludeEntities, disablePage, tagParams}). Rich object (~200KB for large entities like Binance due to a long populatedTags list).
usage.quirks: Requires an Arkham entity ID (a slug like "binance"), not a wallet address — use /x402/balances/address or /x402/intelligence/address for address-based lookups, and /x402/search to resolve a name into an entity ID. Distinct from the sibling ops /intelligence/entity-summary, /intelligence/entity-types, /intelligence/entity-predictions, /balances/entity, and /counterparties/entity. Static $0.20 (not dynamic) — the live 402 quotes 200000 base units on both Base and Solana USDC.
usage.guide: Call POST https://api.arkm.com/x402/intelligence/entity with a JSON body {"entity": "<id>"}. Pay the x402 402 with USDC on Base (or Solana). The full entity-intelligence object comes back inline in the 200 response — no polling.

name: Arkham Token Intelligence
description: Look up Arkham token intelligence for a single token by CoinGecko pricing ID (or by chain + contract address), returning identity, symbol, TradingView ticker, current price, and 24h-ago price.

inputSchema.description: Identify the token either by CoinGecko pricing ID (id) OR by chain + address.

id.description: The CoinGecko pricing ID of the token (e.g. 'usd-coin').

chain.description: Blockchain network where the token is deployed (used with address).

address.description: The token contract address to query (used with chain).

identifier.description: Echoes how the token was identified, e.g. { pricingID }.

usage.callShape: POST https://api.arkm.com/x402/intelligence/token with a JSON body identifying ONE token, either by CoinGecko pricing ID ({"id":"usd-coin"}) OR by chain + contract address ({"chain":"...","address":"0x..."}). No auth/API key; pays a flat $0.20 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453) or Solana. Result is returned inline (synchronous).
usage.outputShape: identifier (object echoing the lookup key, e.g. { pricingID }), name, symbol, tvTicker (TradingView ticker string), price (number, current USD price), price24hAgo (number, USD price 24h ago). Verified live for id=usd-coin: {"identifier":{"pricingID":"usd-coin"},"name":"USDC","symbol":"usdc","tvTicker":"BINANCE:USDCUSDT","price":0.999686,"price24hAgo":0.999831}.
quirks: Flat $0.20 per call — the empty-body 402 and the real-body 402 both quote 200000 (0.20 USDC), so this is a fixed price, NOT a worst-case ceiling.
Identify the token with EITHER 'id' (CoinGecko pricing ID) OR the pair 'chain'+'address'. The documented example uses the pricing-ID form {"id":"usd-coin"}.
Distinct sibling operations on the same host (do not conflate): /intelligence/address, /intelligence/entity, /intelligence/entity-summary, and /token/market — different lookups, each its own service.
Also accepts payment in USDC on Solana (solana:5eykt4UsFv8P8NJdTREpY1vzqKqZKvdp) with the same 0.20 amount.
usage.guide: Look up Arkham token intelligence for a single token. POST https://api.arkm.com/x402/intelligence/token with a JSON body identifying the token by CoinGecko pricing ID ({"id":"usd-coin"}) or by chain + contract address ({"chain":"ethereum","address":"0x..."}). No API key; pays a flat $0.20 USDC via x402 on Base or Solana, result returned inline. Response: { identifier, name, symbol, tvTicker, price, price24hAgo } — current and 24h-ago USD price plus the token's TradingView ticker.

name: Arkham Address Loan Positions
description: Return open lending/borrowing positions (supplied and borrowed balances, USD values, and per-chain totals) for a blockchain address across DeFi protocols (Aave, Compound, etc.) and multiple chains, using Arkham's onchain intelligence.

address.description: The blockchain address (EVM 0x... or other) to query loan positions for. Also accepts an array of addresses.

chains.description: Optional single comma-separated value to filter chains (e.g. 'ethereum,arbitrum_one'). If omitted, returns positions across all supported chains.

outputSchema.description: addresses{chain{address{arkhamLabel,chain,contract,isUserAddress}}}, totalPositions{chain->usdTotal}, balances{chain->[{name,symbol,id,balance,balanceExact,usd,price,price24hAgo,protocol,type:'supplied'|'borrowed',underlyingAssetAddress,market,quoteTime}]}

usage.callShape: POST https://api.arkm.com/x402/loans/address  body={"address":"0x..."}  (optional "chains":"ethereum,arbitrum_one")
usage.outputShape: JSON object: addresses{chain{addr{arkhamLabel,chain,contract,isUserAddress}}}; totalPositions{chain->usd number}; balances{chain->array of position rows [{name,symbol,id,balance,balanceExact,usd,price,price24hAgo,protocol(e.g. AAVE_V3/COMPOUND_V3),type:'supplied'|'borrowed',underlyingAssetAddress,market,quoteTime}]}. Empty chains return [].
quirks: Stateless x402 POST; JSON body. Arkham path parameters are supplied as body fields.
'address' is required; 'chains' is an optional comma-separated filter string.
Fixed $0.20 per call (openapi x-payment-info mode:fixed); not a dynamic ceiling.
x402 USDC accepted on Base (eip155:8453) or Solana; $0.20 observed on Base.
Returns positions across ~11 chains (ethereum, arbitrum_one, base, polygon, optimism, avalanche, bsc, flare, hyperevm, hypercore, robinhood); each balance row has type 'supplied' or 'borrowed'.
usage.guide: Get open DeFi lending/borrowing positions for a wallet address from Arkham. POST https://api.arkm.com/x402/loans/address with body {"address":"0x..."} (optionally {"chains":"ethereum,arbitrum_one"} to filter). Response: balances{chain->[position rows]} where each row's 'type' is 'supplied' or 'borrowed' with usd value and protocol (AAVE_V3, COMPOUND_V3, ...); totalPositions{chain->usd} gives per-chain aggregate; addresses{} carries the Arkham entity label. Pay per call via x402 (USDC on Base or Solana), $0.20 fixed.

name: Arkham Altcoin Index
description: Return Arkham's current Altcoin Index — a single 0-100 market-breadth reading of how strongly altcoins are outperforming Bitcoin (higher = more 'altcoin season').

inputSchema.description: No parameters. The documented request body is an empty JSON object.

altcoinIndex.description: The current Arkham Altcoin Index value (0-100 market-breadth reading; higher = altcoins outperforming BTC).

usage.callShape: POST https://api.arkm.com/x402/marketdata/altcoin-index with an empty JSON body ({}). No parameters, no path/query segments. The result is returned synchronously and inline in the 200 body (no job id, no poll). Pays $0.20 USDC flat via x402 on Base (eip155:8453) or Solana; no API key.
usage.outputShape: { altcoinIndex: number }
quirks: Takes no input — the documented (and only) request body is an empty JSON object {}. The empty-body probe is the real call, so the $0.20 quote is the true price, not a worst-case ceiling.
DYNAMIC PRICING host (api.arkm.com), but this op quoted a flat $0.20 (200000 USDC base units) and returned a paid 200, so the price is stable.

The 402 payment-required header carries a bazaar 'info' extension documenting the empty input body and the output example { altcoinIndex: 28 }; the paid 200 returned { altcoinIndex: 29 } — this is a single scalar market-breadth reading, not a per-token or per-address lookup.
Solana accepts carries a feePayer in 'extra'; Base accepts carries USDC name/version — normalize per the x402 client.
usage.needs: Nothing — no input, no files, no ids, no auth. Just pay the x402 402.
usage.guide: POST an empty JSON body {} to https://api.arkm.com/x402/marketdata/altcoin-index, paying the x402 402 with USDC on Base or Solana ($0.20 flat). The 200 response is synchronous and contains a single field { "altcoinIndex": <number> } — a 0-100 reading of altcoin market breadth vs BTC. No polling.

name: Arkham Network History
description: Get the daily historical market time series (USD price, 24h volume, market cap) of a blockchain network's native token from Arkham's onchain intelligence.

chain.description: The blockchain network identifier (e.g. 'ethereum', 'bsc', 'arbitrum_one'). Selects which network's native-token historical market series to return.

outputSchema.description: Array of daily historical market points for the network's native token, oldest first.

usd.description: Native-token price in USD on that day

volume24h.description: 24-hour trading volume in USD on that day

marketCap.description: Native-token market capitalization in USD on that day

usage.callShape: POST https://api.arkm.com/x402/networks/history with JSON body {"chain":"<network>"} (e.g. {"chain":"ethereum"}). No API key, no signup. Pays a fixed $0.20 USDC via x402 (HTTP 402) on Base (eip155:8453) or Solana; the historical time-series array is returned inline in the 200 body.
usage.outputShape: JSON array of daily points, oldest first, each {time (ISO 8601 UTC day), usd (native-token USD price), volume24h (24h USD trading volume), marketCap (USD market cap)}. Verified live for chain 'ethereum': ~440KB array of daily ETH points from 2015-08-07 (usd 2.83) through the present.
quirks: Fixed $0.20 per call (openapi x-payment-info mode:fixed) — this is NOT a dynamic worst-case ceiling; it is the real price.

Output is a flat array of daily points (not keyed by chain) covering the requested network's NATIVE token — usd is the native token's price, marketCap/volume24h are the native token's, not the whole chain's TVL.
The 'chain' body field is required; it accepts a network slug like 'ethereum', 'bsc', 'arbitrum_one'. Responses can be hundreds of KB for long-lived chains (full daily history since inception).
This is a per-NETWORK lookup keyed by a request-BODY 'chain' field — distinct from the by-address /x402/history/address and token-level /x402/token/price/history services.
400 = missing/invalid body, 404 = unknown network, 429 = rate limited; none of these settle payment (only successful upstream requests are charged).
usage.guide: Get the daily historical market series for a blockchain network's native token via Arkham's onchain intelligence. POST https://api.arkm.com/x402/networks/history with JSON body {"chain":"ethereum"} (or another network slug such as 'bsc', 'arbitrum_one'). No API key; pays a fixed $0.20 USDC via x402 on Base or Solana. The response (inline in the 200) is a JSON array of daily points, oldest first, each {time (ISO 8601 UTC), usd (native-token USD price), volume24h (24h USD volume), marketCap (USD market cap)}. Iterate the array directly; responses can be hundreds of KB for long-lived chains. Use /x402/history/address for a wallet's portfolio history and /x402/token/price/history for a specific token's price history.

name: Arkham Address Portfolio
description: Get the point-in-time token-holdings breakdown of a blockchain address for a given day, per chain, with per-token balance, price and USD value, using Arkham's onchain intelligence.

address.description: The blockchain address to query portfolio holdings for. EVM addresses accepted (also accepts an array of addresses).

time.description: Unix timestamp in MILLISECONDS for the historical snapshot. Truncated to the start of the UTC day. Provide as a string (e.g. '1704067200000') or number.

chains.description: Optional. Chains to filter by as a single comma-separated value (e.g. 'ethereum,bsc'). If omitted, returns holdings across all supported chains.

outputSchema.description: Map keyed by chain slug (e.g. ethereum, bsc, arbitrum_one, base, polygon, optimism, avalanche, flare, hyperevm, hypercore, robinhood). Each value is a map keyed by token id.

symbol.description: Token ticker symbol

balance.description: Token balance held on that chain at the snapshot day

price.description: USD unit price used for valuation

usd.description: USD value of the held balance (balance * price)

usage.callShape: POST https://api.arkm.com/x402/portfolio/address with JSON body {"address":"0x...","time":"<unix ms>"} (optional {"chains":"ethereum,bsc"}). No API key, no signup. Pays a fixed $0.20 USDC via x402 (HTTP 402) on Base (eip155:8453) or Solana; the holdings breakdown is returned inline in the 200 body.
usage.outputShape: JSON object keyed by chain slug (arbitrum_one, avalanche, base, bsc, ethereum, flare, hypercore, hyperevm, optimism, polygon, robinhood, ...). Each chain value is itself an object keyed by token id; each token entry is {id, name, symbol, balance (number), price (USD number), usd (balance*price)}. Verified live for address 0x28C6c06298d514Db089934071355E5743bf21d60 at time=1704067200000 (2024-01-01 UTC): ~48KB response spanning 11 chains with per-token balances/prices/USD values.
quirks: 'time' is REQUIRED (unix timestamp in MILLISECONDS, truncated to the start of the UTC day) — this is a point-in-time SNAPSHOT, not a live 'now' balance. Omitting time yields a 400.
Fixed $0.20 per call (openapi x-payment-info mode:fixed) — this is the real price, NOT a dynamic worst-case ceiling.
Output is a nested per-chain / per-token MAP (chain -> tokenId -> {balance,price,usd,...}), not a flat array — iterate chain keys then token keys under each.

Distinct from the sibling POST /x402/history/address ('Arkham Address History'), which returns a daily USD portfolio-VALUE time series rather than the token-level composition at one day. Also distinct from /x402/portfolio/entity (by-entity, $0.40) and /x402/portfolio/time-series/address (single-token daily series, $0.40).
x402 USDC accepted on Base (eip155:8453) or Solana; $0.20 observed and paid on Base.
400 = missing/invalid body (e.g. missing 'time'), 404 = address not found upstream; neither is charged (only successful upstream requests settle payment).
usage.guide: Get the point-in-time, per-chain token-holdings breakdown of a wallet address from Arkham. POST https://api.arkm.com/x402/portfolio/address with body {"address":"0x...","time":"<unix ms>"} (time is REQUIRED, unix milliseconds, truncated to the start of the UTC day; optionally {"chains":"ethereum,bsc"} to filter). No API key; pays a fixed $0.20 USDC via x402 on Base or Solana. Response (inline in the 200) is a JSON object keyed by chain slug (ethereum, bsc, arbitrum_one, base, ...); each chain value is an object keyed by token id, and each token entry is {id, name, symbol, balance, price, usd}. Iterate chain keys then token keys — it is a nested map, not a flat array. Use this for 'what did this wallet hold, token by token, on day X'; use /x402/history/address for a daily total-USD-value time series instead.

name: Arkham Tag Summary
description: Return summary statistics for an Arkham onchain tag (e.g. 'proof-of-reserves'): the number of addresses and entities carrying the tag and the number of unique tag parameter values.

id.description: The Arkham tag identifier to retrieve summary statistics for (e.g. 'proof-of-reserves'). Accepts string, number, boolean, or an array of those.

outputSchema.description: Summary statistics for the tag: { tagId (string), numAddresses (number of addresses carrying the tag), numEntities (number of entities carrying the tag), numUniqueTagParams (number of unique tag parameter values) }.

usage.callShape: POST https://api.arkm.com/x402/tag/summary with a JSON body. Required: id (the Arkham tag identifier string, e.g. 'proof-of-reserves'). Pure x402 (no API key); pays USDC on Base (eip155:8453) or Solana. Result is returned inline in the 200 body (synchronous).
usage.outputShape: JSON object with: tagId (echoed tag identifier), numAddresses (count of addresses carrying the tag), numEntities (count of entities carrying the tag), numUniqueTagParams (count of distinct tag parameter values). Example: {"tagId":"proof-of-reserves","numAddresses":1470239,"numEntities":41,"numUniqueTagParams":39}.
quirks: FIXED price $0.20 per call (not a dynamic empty-body ceiling): the 402 description states '$0.20 per call' and a real-body re-quote returned the same amount 200000 (=$0.20 USDC, 6 decimals) as the empty-body probe on both Base and Solana.

The 402 returns HTTP 402 with content-length 0; the payment requirements (accepts + input/output schema + documented example body) live in the base64 'payment-required' response HEADER (x402 v2), not the body.
'id' is a tag slug (e.g. 'proof-of-reserves'), not an address or entity. This is a distinct operation from /x402/tag/params (which lists a tag's parameter values), not an alias.
The host also emits an 'x-agent-identity' SIWX challenge header, but the endpoint is satisfied by x402 payment alone (no wallet signature required).
usage.guide: Get summary statistics for an Arkham onchain tag. POST https://api.arkm.com/x402/tag/summary with JSON body {"id":"<tag-id>"} (e.g. 'proof-of-reserves'). Pure x402, no API key; pay $0.20 USDC on Base or Solana. Returns {tagId, numAddresses, numEntities, numUniqueTagParams} inline in the 200 (synchronous). Verified with a live paid call.

name: Arkham Token Chain Addresses
description: Resolves a token (by its CoinGecko pricing ID) to its deployed contract addresses across every chain Arkham tracks, returned as a map of chain slug to contract/mint address.

id.description: The CoinGecko pricing ID of the token (e.g. 'usd-coin', 'ethereum'). Also accepts number/boolean/array per the provider schema, but the CoinGecko slug string is the documented form.

outputSchema.description: A map of chain slug (e.g. ethereum, base, arbitrum_one, avalanche, optimism, polygon, hyperevm, solana, tron) to the token's contract/mint address on that chain. Only chains where the token is deployed are present.

usage.callShape: POST https://api.arkm.com/x402/token/addresses with a JSON body { id: string } where id is the token's CoinGecko pricing ID. Result is returned inline in the 200 body. Pays a fixed $0.20 USDC per call via x402 on Base (eip155:8453) or Solana; no API key.
usage.outputShape: A flat JSON object mapping chain slug -> contract/mint address string. Verified for id 'usd-coin': { arbitrum_one: '0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831', avalanche: '0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E', base: '0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913', ethereum: '0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48', hyperevm: '0xb88339CB7199b77E23DB6E890353E22632Ba630f', optimism: '0x0b2C639c533813f4Aa9D7837CAf62653d097Ff85', polygon: '0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359', solana: 'EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v', tron: 'TEkxiTehnzSmSe2XqrBj4w32RUN966rdz8' }. EVM addresses are hex, Solana is a base58 mint, Tron is a base58 T-address.
quirks: Fixed price: the 402 description and openapi x-payment-info both state $0.20 per call, and the accepts amount is exactly 200000 (=$0.20 USDC) regardless of body — it is NOT a round-dollar worst-case ceiling.
The 'id' is a CoinGecko pricing ID (slug like 'usd-coin', 'ethereum'), NOT a contract address, ticker, or Arkham entity id.
Output keys are only the chains where the token is deployed; the set varies per token. Solana values are SPL mints and Tron values are TRC-20 T-addresses (not hex).
Pure x402, no API key. Both Base USDC and Solana USDC accepts are offered at the same $0.20.
usage.guide: Look up a token's contract addresses across all chains via Arkham. POST https://api.arkm.com/x402/token/addresses with JSON body { id: string } where id is the token's CoinGecko pricing ID (e.g. 'usd-coin', 'ethereum'). The response is a flat JSON object mapping chain slug (ethereum, base, arbitrum_one, avalanche, optimism, polygon, hyperevm, solana, tron, ...) to the token's contract/mint address on that chain; only deployed chains appear. Pays a fixed $0.20 USDC per call via x402 on Base (eip155:8453) or Solana — no API key. Result is synchronous (inline in the 200). Verified live with body { id: 'usd-coin' }.

name: Arkham Exchange Tokens
description: List the tokens available on the Arkham Exchange — separated into spot-market and perpetual (perp) markets — each returned as a CoinGecko pricing ID identifier.

inputSchema.description: No parameters — POST an empty JSON body {}. The endpoint returns the full list of Arkham Exchange spot and perp tokens.

pricingID.description: CoinGecko pricing ID of a spot-market token (e.g. 'bitcoin', 'ethereum').
CoinGecko pricing ID of a perpetual-market token (e.g. 'hyperliquid', 'solana').

usage.callShape: POST https://api.arkm.com/x402/token/arkham-exchange-tokens with an empty JSON body {} (no parameters). Pays a fixed $0.20 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453) or Solana. Synchronous JSON result returned inline in the 200 — no polling.
usage.outputShape: Object { spotTokens: [ { identifier: { pricingID } } ], perpTokens: [ { identifier: { pricingID } } ] } where pricingID is a CoinGecko pricing ID. Live verified: {} -> 42 spotTokens (bitcoin, ethereum, solana, arkham, cardano, ripple, dogecoin, chainlink, sui, arbitrum, avalanche-2, pepe, dogwifcoin, usd-coin, jupiter-exchange-solana, ...) and 47 perpTokens (hyperliquid, ethereum, solana, bitcoin, arkham, bittensor, sonic-3, caldera, walrus-2, xdce-crowd-sale, ...).
quirks: Takes NO input — POST an empty JSON body {} (the provider's bazaar schema documents body:{}).
Fixed $0.20 per call (402 resource description says '$0.20 per call'; accepts quote 200000 base-unit USDC = $0.20 on both Base and Solana). Not a dynamic empty-body ceiling.
Tokens are returned ONLY as CoinGecko pricing IDs (e.g. 'usd-coin', 'the-open-network') — no name/symbol/contract is echoed. Pair with /x402/token/market or /x402/token/addresses to resolve details.
Two separate lists: spotTokens (Arkham Exchange spot markets) and perpTokens (perpetual markets); they overlap but are not identical (e.g. hyperliquid appears only under perpTokens).
Cloudflare fronts the host and can block non-browser User-Agents (HTTP 403 'error code: 1010') — send a browser User-Agent when probing/calling.
usage.guide: List the tokens tradable on the Arkham Exchange. POST https://api.arkm.com/x402/token/arkham-exchange-tokens with an empty JSON body {} — no parameters. Pays a FIXED $0.20 USDC via x402 on Base or Solana (no API key), synchronous result. Returns { spotTokens:[{identifier:{pricingID}}], perpTokens:[{identifier:{pricingID}}] } where pricingID is a CoinGecko pricing ID; spot and perp are separate lists.
