Use to enumerate Arkham's listed spot/perp markets, then feed a pricingID into /x402/token/market for that token's price and market data. Live example returned 42 spot tokens and 47 perp tokens (bitcoin, ethereum, solana, hyperliquid, arkham, ...).

name: Arkham Token Balance
description: Resolve a single token by its CoinGecko pricing ID (or chain/address) and return its symbol, current price and balance/USD value, optionally for one or more given holder addresses or an Arkham entity.

id.description: The CoinGecko pricing ID of the token to resolve (e.g. 'usd-coin'). Provide either 'id' or a 'chain'/'address' pair to identify the token.

chain.description: Optional. Blockchain network where the token is deployed (used with a token address instead of a pricing 'id').

address.description: Optional. Holder address(es) to query the token balance for, passed as a single comma-separated string (e.g. '0x28C6...,0x21a3...'), not a JSON array.

entityID.description: Optional. Arkham entity ID to query the balance for. Provide either entityID or address; if both are given, address takes precedence.

pricingID.description: The CoinGecko pricing ID of the resolved token.

symbol.description: Token symbol.

balance.description: Token balance held by the queried address/entity (0 when no holder is specified).

usd.description: USD value of the balance (balance * price).

usage.callShape: POST https://api.arkm.com/x402/token/balance with a JSON body identifying the token by 'id' (CoinGecko pricing ID) or by 'chain'/'address', and optionally a holder via 'address' (comma-separated) or 'entityID'. Result is returned synchronously and inline in the 200 body (no job id, no poll). Pays $0.20 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453) or Solana; no API key.
usage.outputShape: { pricingID: string, name: string, symbol: string, balance: number, price: number, usd: number }
quirks: DYNAMIC PRICING host, but this op quoted a flat $0.20 (200000 USDC base units) on both an empty body and a real-body ({id:'usd-coin'}) re-quote — the price is stable, not a worst-case ceiling.

The 402 payment-required header carries a bazaar 'info' extension with a documented input example ({id:'usd-coin'}) and output example ({pricingID,name,symbol,balance,price,usd}) — that example is the source of this entry's schema/outputShape and the verified call.

With only a token 'id' and no holder address/entityID, 'balance' and 'usd' are 0 (the verified call returned USD Coin at price 0.999684, balance 0) — pass 'address' or 'entityID' to get a real holding.
Identify the token by EITHER 'id' (CoinGecko pricing ID) OR a 'chain'/'address' pair; identify the holder by 'address' (comma-separated string, not a JSON array) or 'entityID'.
Distinct from /balances/address (all-token balances for an address) and /balances/entity — this endpoint resolves and reports ONE token.
Solana accepts carries a feePayer in 'extra'; Base accepts carries USDC name/version — normalize per the x402 client.
usage.needs: A token identifier: either a CoinGecko pricing ID ('id', e.g. 'usd-coin') or a chain/address pair. To get a non-zero balance, also supply a holder address (comma-separated string) or an Arkham entityID. No files, ids, or auth required.
usage.guide: POST { "id": "usd-coin" } to https://api.arkm.com/x402/token/balance (or identify the token by chain/address), paying the x402 402 with USDC on Base or Solana ($0.20). To query a holder's balance, add "address": "0x28C6...,0x21a3..." (comma-separated string) or "entityID": "<arkham-entity>". The 200 response is synchronous and contains { pricingID, name, symbol, balance, price, usd }. Do not retry-pay on a 4xx; fix the input first.

name: Arkham Token Market Data by ID
description: Get Arkham's current market data for a token by its CoinGecko pricing ID — price, market cap, fully diluted value, circulating/total supply, 24h volume, 24h high/low, and price snapshots (24h/7d/30d/180d ago, ATH, ATL).

id.description: The CoinGecko pricing ID of the token (e.g. 'usd-coin', 'bitcoin', 'ethereum'). May also be a number, boolean, or array per the permissive upstream schema, but a string CoinGecko ID is the documented shape.

usage.callShape: POST https://api.arkm.com/x402/token/market/by-id with JSON body {"id":"<CoinGecko pricing ID>"} (e.g. {"id":"usd-coin"}). No API key, no signup. Pays a fixed $0.20 USDC via x402 (HTTP 402) on Base (eip155:8453) or Solana; the market-data object is returned inline in the 200 body.
usage.outputShape: Flat JSON object of current market metrics: {price, marketCap, fullyDilutedValue, circulatingSupply, totalSupply, totalVolume (24h USD), maxPrice24h, minPrice24h, price24hAgo, price7dAgo, price30dAgo, price180dAgo, allTimeHigh, allTimeLow}. Verified live for id 'usd-coin': price 0.999711, marketCap 71922833791, totalVolume 10879857519, allTimeHigh 1.043, allTimeLow 0.877647.
quirks: Fixed $0.20 per call (openapi x-payment-info mode:fixed) — this is NOT a dynamic worst-case ceiling; it is the real price.
Input 'id' is a CoinGecko pricing ID (slug like 'usd-coin', 'bitcoin', 'ethereum'), NOT a contract address — use the by-address / holders/by-address style siblings for address lookups.
The upstream schema is permissive (id may be a string, number, boolean, or array), but the documented/verified shape is a single string CoinGecko id.
Distinct from the sibling POST /x402/token/market (a separate service). This is the explicit by-pricing-ID variant.
400 = missing/invalid body, 404 = token id not found, 429 = rate limited; per the openapi these error responses are not charged (only successful upstream requests settle payment).
usage.guide: Get current market data for a token via Arkham's onchain intelligence, looked up by CoinGecko pricing ID. POST https://api.arkm.com/x402/token/market/by-id with JSON body {"id":"<coingecko-id>"} (e.g. {"id":"usd-coin"}, {"id":"bitcoin"}). No API key; pays a fixed $0.20 USDC via x402 on Base or Solana. The 200 body is a flat JSON object with price, marketCap, fullyDilutedValue, circulatingSupply, totalSupply, totalVolume (24h USD), 24h high/low, historical price snapshots (24h/7d/30d/180d ago), and allTimeHigh/allTimeLow. Use the CoinGecko slug, not a contract address. The sibling /x402/token/market is a separate endpoint.

name: Arkham Token Market Data
description: Get Arkham's current market data for one token by CoinGecko pricing ID: price, 24h/7d/30d/180d historical prices, 24h high/low, total volume, market cap, fully diluted value, circulating/total supply, and all-time high/low.

id.description: The CoinGecko pricing ID of the token (e.g. 'usd-coin', 'bitcoin', 'ethereum'). May also be a number/boolean/array per the schema, but a CoinGecko pricing-ID string is the documented usage.

usage.callShape: POST https://api.arkm.com/x402/token/market with JSON body {"id": "<coingecko-pricing-id>"} (required). Pays a fixed $0.20 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453) or Solana. Synchronous JSON market-data result returned inline in the 200.
usage.outputShape: Flat object of numeric market fields: price, price24hAgo, price7dAgo, price30dAgo, price180dAgo, maxPrice24h, minPrice24h, totalVolume, marketCap, fullyDilutedValue, circulatingSupply, totalSupply, allTimeHigh, allTimeLow. Live verified: {"id":"usd-coin"} -> {price:0.999711, totalVolume:10879857519, marketCap:71922833791, fullyDilutedValue:71932068834.53, circulatingSupply:71943556480.7, totalSupply:71952863211.99, allTimeHigh:1.043, allTimeLow:0.877647, price24hAgo:0.999759, maxPrice24h:0.999908, minPrice24h:0.999621}.
quirks: Fixed $0.20 per call (the 402 resource description says '$0.20 per call' and the accepts quote 200000 base-unit USDC = $0.20); not a dynamic empty-body ceiling.
The 'id' is a CoinGecko pricing ID (e.g. 'usd-coin', 'bitcoin'), NOT a contract address or ticker symbol.
Distinct from the sibling /x402/token/market/by-id, which takes Arkham's internal token id instead of the CoinGecko pricing id.
Output is a flat numeric object; no token name/symbol is echoed back — pair with /x402/token/addresses or /x402/search to resolve identifiers.
usage.guide: Get Arkham's current market data for one token. POST https://api.arkm.com/x402/token/market with JSON body {"id": "<coingecko-pricing-id>"} (e.g. {"id":"bitcoin"}). Pays a fixed $0.20 USDC via x402 on Base or Solana — no API key. Returns synchronously a flat object of numeric market fields: current price, historical prices (24h/7d/30d/180d ago), 24h high/low, total volume, market cap, fully diluted value, circulating/total supply, and all-time high/low. Use for token price and market-cap snapshots in trading and portfolio tooling. Example: {"id":"usd-coin"} returned price ~0.9997 and marketCap ~71.9B.

name: Arkham Token Price Change
description: Get a token's current price alongside its price at a given past timestamp (to derive the change since then), identified by CoinGecko pricing ID, using Arkham's onchain market data.

id.description: The CoinGecko pricing ID of the token (e.g. 'usd-coin', 'bitcoin', 'ethereum'). May also be a number/boolean/array per the schema, but a CoinGecko pricing-ID string is the documented usage.

pastTime.description: Past timestamp in RFC3339/ISO-8601 format (e.g. '2024-01-01T00:00:00Z') to calculate the price change from.

pricingID.description: The CoinGecko pricing ID that was queried.

historicalPrice.description: Token price in USD at the requested pastTime.

usage.callShape: POST https://api.arkm.com/x402/token/price-change with JSON body {"id": "<coingecko-pricing-id>", "pastTime": "<RFC3339 timestamp>"} (both required). No auth/API key; pays a flat $0.20 USDC via x402 (HTTP 402) on Base (eip155:8453) or Solana. Result returned inline in the 200 (synchronous).
usage.outputShape: Flat JSON object {pricingID (string, the queried CoinGecko pricing ID), currentPrice (number, current USD price), historicalPrice (number, USD price at pastTime)}. Live verified: {"id":"usd-coin","pastTime":"2024-01-01T00:00:00Z"} -> {"pricingID":"usd-coin","currentPrice":0.99972,"historicalPrice":1.0003}. The change is derived client-side (currentPrice - historicalPrice, or as a percentage).
quirks: Flat $0.20 per call (openapi x-payment-info mode:fixed, amount 0.20) — the empty-body 402 and the real-body 402 both quote 200000 (0.20 USDC), so this is a fixed price, NOT a worst-case ceiling.
Despite the 'price-change' name, the response does NOT contain a change value — it returns currentPrice and historicalPrice; compute the change yourself.
Both 'id' (CoinGecko pricing ID, e.g. 'usd-coin', 'bitcoin') and 'pastTime' (RFC3339/ISO-8601 timestamp) are required; 'id' is a CoinGecko pricing ID, NOT a contract address or ticker symbol.
Distinct sibling operations on the same host (do not conflate): /token/price/history (a full time series), /token/market, and /intelligence/token — each its own service.
Also accepts payment in USDC on Solana (solana:5eykt4UsFv8P8NJdTREpY1vzqKqZKvdp) with the same 0.20 amount.
400 = missing/invalid body, 404 = token not found upstream; per provider convention only successful upstream requests settle payment.
usage.guide: Get a token's price change since a past timestamp via Arkham's onchain market data. POST https://api.arkm.com/x402/token/price-change with JSON body {"id": "<coingecko-pricing-id>", "pastTime": "<RFC3339 timestamp>"} (e.g. {"id":"bitcoin","pastTime":"2024-01-01T00:00:00Z"}). No API key; pays a flat $0.20 USDC via x402 on Base or Solana, result returned inline. Response: {pricingID, currentPrice (USD), historicalPrice (USD at pastTime)} — derive the change from the two prices. Use for point-in-time performance/return calculations on a single token.

name: Arkham Token Price History
description: Get a token's price history — either the full daily series or every quote recorded in the last 24 hours — identified by CoinGecko pricing ID (or chain + contract address), using Arkham's onchain market data.

inputSchema.description: Identify the token either by CoinGecko pricing ID (id) OR by chain + address. Optionally set daily.

id.description: The CoinGecko pricing ID of the token (e.g. 'usd-coin').

chain.description: Blockchain network where the token is deployed (used with address).

address.description: The token contract address to query (used with chain).

daily.description: If true, returns the full daily price history for the token. Otherwise returns every quote recorded in the last 24 hours.

outputSchema.description: Array of price points, oldest to newest.

time.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of the quote.

usd.description: Token price in USD at that time.

volume24h.description: Trailing 24h trading volume in USD at that time.

marketCap.description: Market capitalization in USD at that time.

usage.callShape: POST https://api.arkm.com/x402/token/price/history with a JSON body identifying ONE token, either by CoinGecko pricing ID ({"id":"usd-coin"}) OR by chain + contract address ({"chain":"...","address":"0x..."}); add {"daily":true} for the full daily series (default returns the last 24h of quotes). No auth/API key; pays a flat $0.20 USDC via x402 (HTTP 402) on Base (eip155:8453) or Solana. Result array is returned inline in the 200 (synchronous).
usage.outputShape: JSON array of price points ordered oldest->newest, each {time (ISO 8601 UTC), usd (number, USD price), volume24h (number, trailing-24h USD volume), marketCap (number, USD market cap)}. Verified live for {"id":"usd-coin"}: ~82KB array of last-24h quotes, e.g. {"time":"2026-07-29T19:59:32.226Z","usd":0.99977,"volume24h":12265128205,"marketCap":72210684304}. Set daily:true for a full daily history instead.
quirks: Flat $0.20 per call (openapi x-payment-info mode:fixed) — the empty-body 402 and the real-body 402 both quote 200000 (0.20 USDC), so this is a fixed price, NOT a worst-case ceiling.
Identify the token with EITHER 'id' (CoinGecko pricing ID) OR the pair 'chain'+'address'. The documented example uses {"id":"usd-coin"}.

Default (no 'daily') returns every quote recorded in the last ~24 hours (fine-grained intraday points); set daily:true for the full daily-resolution history. Response is a flat array, oldest->newest, and can be large (tens of KB).
Distinct sibling operations on the same host (do not conflate): /token/price-change (a single price-change value), /token/market, and /intelligence/token — each its own service.
Also accepts payment in USDC on Solana (solana:5eykt4UsFv8P8NJdTREpY1vzqKqZKvdp) with the same 0.20 amount.
400 = missing/invalid body, 404 = token not found upstream; neither is charged (only successful upstream requests settle payment).
usage.guide: Get a token's price history via Arkham's onchain market data. POST https://api.arkm.com/x402/token/price/history with a JSON body identifying the token by CoinGecko pricing ID ({"id":"usd-coin"}) or by chain + contract address ({"chain":"ethereum","address":"0x..."}); optionally add {"daily":true} for the full daily series (default returns the last ~24h of intraday quotes). No API key; pays a flat $0.20 USDC via x402 on Base or Solana, result returned inline. name: Arkham Trending Token by ID

name: Arkham Address Transfer Volume

outputSchema.description: Object keyed by chain slug (e.g. arbitrum_one, avalanche, base, bsc, ethereum, flare, hypercore, hyperevm, optimism, polygon, robinhood). Each value is an array of daily points { time (ISO date), volumes: [{ exchangeID, exchangeName, withdrawnUSD, depositedUSD }] }.

usage.callShape: POST https://api.arkm.com/x402/volume/address with a JSON body { address: string (required), chains?: array (optional) }. Result is returned inline in the 200 body. Pays a fixed $0.20 USDC per call via x402 on Base (eip155:8453) or Solana; no API key.

'volumes' captures flows between the address and centralized exchanges (exchangeID/exchangeName + withdrawnUSD/depositedUSD), not raw on-chain DEX volume.
Pure x402, no API key. Both Base USDC and Solana USDC accepts are offered at the same $0.20.

name: 24kLabs EVM Keccak & Calldata Decoder
description: Compute the keccak256 hash and 4-byte function selector of a Solidity function/event signature, and optionally ABI-decode raw hex calldata against an ordered list of static Solidity types, via a pay-per-call x402 endpoint.

calldata.description: Optional raw hex calldata to ABI-decode (e.g. '0x...').

types.description: Optional ordered list of static Solidity types to ABI-decode the calldata against, e.g. ['address','uint256'].

keccak256.description: Full keccak256 hash of the signature string.

selector.description: 4-byte function selector (first 4 bytes of the keccak256 hash).

usage.callShape: POST https://api.24klabs.ai/api/eth-calldata-decode with a JSON body {"signature": "transfer(address,uint256)"} (signature = the Solidity function/event signature to hash). Optionally include raw hex 'calldata' plus an ordered 'types' array of static Solidity types to ABI-decode. Pure x402 (USDC on Base, no API key). Synchronous — the keccak256 hash and 4-byte selector are returned inline.
usage.outputShape: JSON object {service, result:{signature, keccak256, selector}, latency_ms}. Observed at index time: {"service":"eth-calldata-decode","result":{"signature":"transfer(address,uint256)","keccak256":"0xa9059cbb2ab09eb219583f4a59a5d0623ade346d962bcd4e46b11da047c9049b","selector":"0xa9059cbb"},"latency_ms":0}. When 'calldata'+'types' are supplied the result also carries the ABI-decoded parameter values.

'signature' must be a canonical Solidity signature with no spaces, e.g. 'transfer(address,uint256)'.
ABI-decoding raw calldata is optional (pass 'calldata' + an ordered 'types' list of static Solidity types); the base call only needs 'signature'.
Pure local compute — deterministic, no external upstream, latency ~0ms.

usage.guide: POST to https://api.24klabs.ai/api/eth-calldata-decode with a JSON body containing 'signature' (a canonical Solidity function/event signature like 'transfer(address,uint256)'). The endpoint is x402-paid (~$0.002 USDC on Base, scheme exact) and responds synchronously with the full keccak256 hash and the 4-byte function selector (the first 4 bytes of that hash). usage.outputShape: ok (bool); symbol (string); asof_day (date, latest anchor day); regime (string, e.g. consolidation); regime_confidence (0-1); total (int, count of firing signals); high_grade (int, count graded A on health); signals = array of firing signals, each { signal_id, name, description, class (OB/TR/EFF/FUT/VOL/CORR/FLOW/OPT), horizon (1d..365d), value, z, confidence (0-1), ic, hit_rate, ir, regime_accuracy, predictive_grade, operational_grade, health_grade (A/B/C/D/U or null), is_anti_predictive (bool), walk_forward ({ asof_day, window_days, split_pct, is_ic, is_hit_rate, is_n_triggers, is_n_obs, oos_ic, oos_hit_rate, oos_n_triggers, oos_n_obs, overfit_ratio, ic_delta, reliability_grade } or null) }; meta ({ ic_context, note }); _next ({ description, hints[] } of recommended follow-up paid Cryptyx endpoints).
quirks: symbol is REQUIRED — a bare GET with no symbol still returns a 402 challenge, but the paid call needs symbol to return a real feed; always supply it.
Many signals return null for ic/hit_rate/ir/regime_accuracy and null grades and a null walk_forward — only a subset of signals carry the full evaluation block; treat those fields as nullable.
z equals value for most rows (already z-scored); confidence is a separate 0-1 field.
grades use A/B/C/D and 'U' (unknown/unrated); reliability_grade inside walk_forward is a color (green/red).
meta.note flags that IC and grades are cross-sectional (universe-wide ranking power), not per-asset — per-asset signal evaluation is not yet available.
the 402 header's bazaar example is a small 4-signal sample; a real paid call returns up to `limit` (default 20) signals (observed 19 for BTC).
Response includes a _next.hints[] block advertising follow-up paid Cryptyx endpoints (thesis, signals/explain, asymmetry, top-setups, regime-context).
usage.guide: Cryptyx Active Signals returns every quantitative signal currently firing for one crypto asset on the latest day, in a single paid call. GET https://cryptyx.ai/api/asset/active-signals?symbol=BTC — symbol is REQUIRED (ticker like BTC/ETH/SOL); optional limit (1-50, default 20) caps the number of signals. No request body; pays $0.05 USDC via x402 on Base, result inline in the 200. Top level gives the asset's regime + regime_confidence, total firing count, and high_grade count. Each signal carries a class (OB/TR/EFF/FUT/VOL/CORR/FLOW/OPT), horizon (1d..365d), z-score, confidence, and — where available — IC, hit rate, regime accuracy, three-way health grading, and a walk-forward IS/OOS block with an overfit ratio and reliability color. Note: grades/IC are cross-sectional (universe-wide) per meta.note, and many rows leave the evaluation fields null. Use this to see what is actively triggering on an asset right now; the response's _next.hints point to thesis/explain/asymmetry/top-setups/regime-context for deeper follow-up.

name: Cryptyx Asymmetry
description: Cross-class positioning read for one crypto asset — futures funding stress, options 1M 25-delta risk-reversal skew, order-book imbalance at 100bp, and 7-day taker buy/sell flow bias — each panel giving current z-score, percentile, a 30-day sparkline, and a one-line narrative.

inputSchema.description: symbol (required) = target asset ticker, uppercased and trimmed server-side (e.g. BTC/ETH/SOL). No other parameters and no request body.

panels.description: The cross-class positioning panels (one per positioning axis). Each: { key (e.g. funding_stress/options_skew/liquidity_posture/flow_bias), class (factor class: FUT/OPT/OB/FLOW), metric_id (e.g. FUT_FUNDING_MA_7D), label, last_asof_day (YYYY-MM-DD), current_z (number, latest z-score), current_pctl (number 0-1, latest percentile), sparkline_30d (array of { d (date), z (number), pctl (number 0-1) }), one_liner (plain-language narrative) }.

_next.description: Recommended follow-up paid Cryptyx endpoints: { description, hints[] each with path/method/price_usd/reason }.

usage.callShape: GET https://cryptyx.ai/api/asset/asymmetry?symbol=BTC. REQUIRED query param: symbol (asset ticker, uppercased server-side, e.g. BTC/ETH/SOL). No other params and no request body. Pays $0.05 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453).
usage.outputShape: ok (bool); symbol (string); panels = array of positioning panels, each { key (funding_stress/options_skew/liquidity_posture/flow_bias), class (FUT/OPT/OB/FLOW), metric_id, label, last_asof_day (YYYY-MM-DD), current_z (number), current_pctl (0-1), sparkline_30d (array of { d, z, pctl }), one_liner }; _next = { description, hints[] } of recommended follow-up paid Cryptyx endpoints. Live BTC call returned 4 panels — funding_stress (z -6.87, 0th pctl, 'Extreme short-biased funding — shorts paying up.'), options_skew (near neutral), liquidity_posture (balanced at 100bp), flow_bias (taker flow balanced) — each with a full 30-day z/pctl sparkline.
quirks: symbol is REQUIRED and must be the QUERY param `symbol` (NOT `asset` like some sibling Cryptyx endpoints); a bare GET with no symbol still returns a 402 challenge but the paid call would 400 without it.
No optional parameters — asymmetry takes only `symbol` (unlike peer-cluster/asset-factors which add horizon/k).
Panels are keyed by positioning axis (funding_stress=FUT, options_skew=OPT, liquidity_posture=OB, flow_bias=FLOW); the set can vary if an asset lacks data for a class.

current_pctl and sparkline pctl are 0-1 fractions (0.00=0th percentile, 1.00=100th), not 0-100; current_z is a raw z-score and can be extreme (BTC funding_stress printed z=-6.87 at the 0th percentile).
sparkline_30d is ordered oldest->newest and its last point equals current_z/current_pctl for that panel.
Response includes a _next.hints[] block advertising follow-up paid Cryptyx asset endpoints (active-signals, thesis, regime-context, top-setups, peer-cluster) at $0.05 each.
usage.guide: Cryptyx Asymmetry gives a one-shot cross-class positioning read for a single crypto asset. GET https://cryptyx.ai/api/asset/asymmetry?symbol=BTC — symbol is REQUIRED (ticker like BTC/ETH/SOL). No other params and no request body; pays $0.05 USDC via x402 on Base. The response returns up to four panels — futures funding stress (FUT), options 1M 25-delta risk-reversal skew (OPT), order-book imbalance at 100bp (OB), and 7-day taker buy/sell flow bias (FLOW) — each with the latest z-score, its percentile (0-1), a 30-day sparkline of z/percentile, and a plain-language one_liner. Read the panels together to gauge whether positioning is stretched (extreme z / 0th or 100th percentile) or balanced; the _next.hints suggest deeper follow-ups (active-signals, thesis, regime-context, top-setups, peer-cluster) on the same asset.

name: Cryptyx Asset Factors
description: Standardised factor t-scores for one crypto asset across 8 factor-classes (OB, TR, EFF, FUT, VOL, CORR, FLOW, OPT) and 8 horizons (1d-365d) — a snapshot of the latest anchor day or a daily series window; each cell is a z-capped, policy-aware percentile score with a bull/bear/expand-contract band.

inputSchema.description: asset (required) = asset symbol, e.g. BTC/ETH/SOL (trimmed + uppercased server-side). mode (optional) = snapshot (default; latest anchor day only) or series (daily window). days (optional int 1-365, default 90) = lookback window for series mode. horizons (optional) = comma-separated horizon filter for series mode (valid: 1d,7d,14d,30d,60d,90d,180d,365d; invalid tokens dropped silently).

factors.description: One record per (horizon x factor-class): { asof_day, asset, horizon (1d..365d), class (OB/TR/EFF/FUT/VOL/CORR/FLOW/OPT), t_score_pct (string, 0-100 percentile), t_band (e.g. NEUTRAL/EXPAND/CONTRACT/BULLISH/BEARISH) }. ~64 records in snapshot mode (8 classes x 8 horizons).

_next.description: Recommended follow-up paid Cryptyx endpoints (hints[] with path/method/price_usd/reason).

usage.callShape: GET https://cryptyx.ai/api/asset-factors?asset=BTC. REQUIRED query param: asset (symbol, e.g. BTC/ETH/SOL). Optional: mode=snapshot|series (default snapshot), days=1-365 (series lookback, default 90), horizons=comma-separated filter (series only, e.g. 7d,30d). No request body. Pays $0.01 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453).
usage.outputShape: ok (bool); asset (string); asof_day (date, latest anchor day); mode (snapshot|series); factors = array of ~64 cells in snapshot mode, one per (horizon x factor-class): { asof_day, asset, horizon (one of 1d,7d,14d,30d,60d,90d,180d,365d), class (one of OB,TR,EFF,FUT,VOL,CORR,FLOW,OPT), t_score_pct (string 0-100 percentile), t_band (enum-like string: NEUTRAL, EXPAND, CONTRACT, and bull/bear variants) }; _next = { description, hints[] } of recommended follow-up paid Cryptyx endpoints. In series mode, factors spans a daily window (days back) rather than a single asof_day.
quirks: asset is REQUIRED — a bare GET with no asset returns a 402 challenge but the paid call would 400 without it; always supply asset.
8 factor-classes observed: OB, TR, EFF, FUT, VOL, CORR, FLOW, OPT (the openapi says '8 classes'; the 402 bazaar example only lists a 4-row subset).
t_score_pct is returned as a STRING (e.g. "48.32"), a 0-100 percentile, not a raw z-score; parse to number before math.
t_band is a free-form/enum-like label that varies (observed NEUTRAL/EXPAND/CONTRACT live; the openapi bazaar example shows bullish/bearish/neutral) — treat as a string.
mode=series with days/horizons returns a daily window instead of a single anchor day; snapshot (default) returns only the latest asof_day.
Response includes a _next.hints[] block advertising other paid Cryptyx asset endpoints (active-signals, asymmetry, top-predictors, thesis, regime-context) at $0.05 each.
usage.guide: Cryptyx Asset Factors returns the full factor cube for one crypto asset in a single paid call: t-scores across 8 factor-classes (OB, TR, EFF, FUT, VOL, CORR, FLOW, OPT) x 8 horizons (1d..365d). GET https://cryptyx.ai/api/asset-factors?asset=BTC — asset is REQUIRED (symbol like BTC/ETH/SOL). Default mode=snapshot gives the latest anchor day (~64 cells); mode=series with days (1-365, default 90) and an optional horizons filter (comma-separated, e.g. 7d,30d) returns a daily window instead. No request body; pays $0.01 USDC via x402 on Base. Each cell: { horizon, class, t_score_pct (string 0-100 percentile), t_band (label like NEUTRAL/EXPAND/CONTRACT/bullish/bearish) }. Use the snapshot for a current factor read, or series for a factor trend; the response's _next.hints suggest follow-up asset endpoints (active-signals, thesis, top-predictors) for deeper context.

name: Cryptyx Asset Liquidity
description: Per-asset spot order-book depth timeseries for one crypto asset — daily bid/ask USD available at 50/100/200bp from mid plus 1d/7d/30d spot volume, with an optional futures (perp) order-book depth envelope; a pre-trade depth and venue-routing input.

inputSchema.description: asset (required) = asset symbol, uppercased server-side (e.g. BTC/ETH/SOL). days (optional number) = trailing day window anchored to the latest available day (0 = full history, max 365; default returns full history). include (optional string) = comma/space list of extras; pass 'futures' to add the latest-day futures (perp) OB depth block to the response.

spot.description: One record per day: { asof_day, asset, spot_vol_1d_usd, spot_vol_7d_avg_usd, spot_vol_30d_avg_usd, ob_bid_50bp_usd, ob_ask_50bp_usd, ob_bid_100bp_usd, ob_ask_100bp_usd, ob_bid_200bp_usd, ob_ask_200bp_usd }. Older days have null ob_* depth (volume-only); recent days carry populated order-book depth.

futures.description: Present only when ?include=futures — latest-day perp OB depth block: { asof_day, asset, fut_ob_bid_50bp_usd, fut_ob_ask_50bp_usd, ... }.

_next.description: Recommended follow-up paid Cryptyx endpoints (hints[] with path/method/price_usd/reason).

usage.callShape: GET https://cryptyx.ai/api/asset-liquidity?asset=BTC. REQUIRED query param: asset (symbol, e.g. BTC/ETH/SOL). Optional: days=0-365 (trailing window anchored to latest day; 0/omitted = full history), include=futures (adds the latest-day futures OB depth block). No request body. Pays $0.01 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453).
usage.outputShape: ok (bool); asset (string); asof_day (date, latest anchor day); spot = array of daily rows (1931 rows spanning 2021-03-25..2026-07-29 observed for BTC with days omitted/full history), each row { asof_day, asset, spot_vol_1d_usd, spot_vol_7d_avg_usd, spot_vol_30d_avg_usd, ob_bid_50bp_usd, ob_ask_50bp_usd, ob_bid_100bp_usd, ob_ask_100bp_usd, ob_bid_200bp_usd, ob_ask_200bp_usd } — older days have null ob_* fields (spot volume only), recent days have populated bid/ask USD depth at 50/100/200bp; futures = array (only when include=futures) of latest-day perp OB depth (fut_ob_bid/ask_*bp_usd); _next = { description, hints[] } of recommended follow-up paid Cryptyx endpoints (asymmetry, active-signals, asset-factors) at $0.01-$0.05 each.
quirks: asset is REQUIRED — a bare GET (or GET without asset) still returns the 402 challenge, but the paid call needs asset supplied or it would not return the series; always pass asset.

days defaults to full history when omitted (observed 1931 daily rows 2021-03-25..2026-07-29 for BTC); pass days=1-365 to limit the trailing window and shrink the payload (the full response is ~600KB).
Order-book depth (ob_bid/ask_*bp_usd) is null on older days — the deep OB depth series only backfills for recent days; spot_vol_* is populated throughout.
Pass include=futures to append the latest-day futures (perp) OB depth block (fut_ob_bid/ask_*bp_usd); default response is spot-only.
ob_* and spot_vol_* values are plain numbers (USD), not strings.
Response includes a _next.hints[] block advertising other paid Cryptyx asset endpoints (asymmetry, active-signals, asset-factors) at $0.01-$0.05 each.
usage.guide: Cryptyx Asset Liquidity returns the spot order-book depth timeseries for one crypto asset in a single paid call: daily bid/ask USD available at 50/100/200bp from mid plus 1d/7d/30d spot volume. GET https://cryptyx.ai/api/asset-liquidity?asset=BTC — asset is REQUIRED (symbol like BTC/ETH/SOL). By default it returns the full daily history (~1900+ rows, ~600KB); pass days=1-365 to limit the trailing window, and include=futures to also get the latest-day perp OB depth block. No request body; pays $0.01 USDC via x402 on Base. Older rows carry only spot volume (ob_* depth is null); recent rows carry populated order-book depth. Use it as a pre-trade liquidity/depth read or venue-routing input; the response's _next.hints suggest follow-up asset endpoints (asymmetry, active-signals, asset-factors) for deeper context.

name: Cryptyx Asset Metric Health
description: Per-asset diagnostic grading of every quant metric for one crypto symbol: time-series (TS) vs cross-sectional (CS) grade divergence, per-metric information coefficient (ts_ic), hit-rate, anti-predictive flags and keep/deactivate recommendations — answering which metrics actually work on THIS asset vs the universe average.

symbol.description: REQUIRED. Asset symbol, uppercased server-side (e.g. BTC, ETH, SOL). Query param.

horizon.description: Optional. Forward-return horizon the metric grades are computed against. One of 7d/14d/30d, defaults to 14d. Query param.

metrics.description: One row per metric graded for this asset.

polarity.description: +1 or -1 expected sign of the metric.

grade_divergence.description: Whether TS and CS grades disagree for this metric.

_next.description: Recommended paid x402 next-call hints (sibling /api/asset/* endpoints).

usage.callShape: GET https://cryptyx.ai/api/asset/metric-health?symbol=<TICKER> and settle the x402 402 challenge (Base USDC, $0.01). REQUIRED query param 'symbol' (asset ticker, e.g. BTC/ETH/SOL; uppercased server-side) — a bare GET without it returns a 402 whose paid result is not usable. Optional query param 'horizon' (7d/14d/30d, default 14d). No request body; result is returned inline in the 200 response.
usage.outputShape: JSON object { ok, symbol, horizon, metrics[] { metric_id, class (TR/OPT/FUT/VOL/FLOW/OB/EFF/CORR), name, description, polarity (+1/-1), ts_grade (A..F), ts_ic, ts_hit_rate, ts_n_obs, ts_anti_predictive (bool), ts_recommendation ('keep'/'deactivate'), cs_grade, cs_ic, cs_hit_rate, cs_anti_predictive, grade_divergence (bool) }, summary { total, ts_grade_a, ts_grade_b, cs_grade_a, cs_grade_b, divergent, ts_anti_predictive }, _next { description, hints[] {path, method, price_usd, reason} } }. Paid live run for BTC (horizon 14d) returned 431 metrics; summary { total 431, ts_grade_a 58, ts_grade_b 35, cs_grade_a 11, cs_grade_b 31, divergent 324, ts_anti_predictive 235 } (e.g. OPT_SKEW_RR25D_1M_MA_30D graded A/A with ts_ic 0.487, hit_rate 0.72; TR_WIN_RATE_60D graded F/F, anti-predictive, recommendation 'deactivate').
quirks: REQUIRED query param 'symbol' — unlike the market-wide Cryptyx feeds (/api/assets, /api/market-pulse/*) this per-asset op needs a ticker; a bare GET is a wasted call.
Large response: the live BTC run returned 431 metric rows (~229KB JSON). Every metric carries both TS and CS grades plus a keep/deactivate recommendation.
'horizon' accepts 7d/14d/30d (default 14d) per the 402 bazaar input schema; grades are computed against that forward-return horizon.
Point-in-time snapshot; grades/ICs change as the underlying model updates.

Companion to /api/asset/top-predictors (which RANKS the working metrics); this endpoint DIAGNOSES per-metric health. Response includes a _next block pointing at sibling paid per-asset endpoints ($0.05 each) for drill-down.

The payment-required data (accepts + bazaar input/output schema + a documented output example) is delivered in the base64 'payment-required' HTTP header on the 402; the 402 JSON body itself is empty ({}).
usage.guide: Per-asset quant-metric health diagnostics from Cryptyx. GET https://cryptyx.ai/api/asset/metric-health?symbol=<TICKER> (e.g. BTC, ETH, SOL) and settle the $0.01 x402 payment (USDC on Base); add optional &horizon=7d|14d|30d (default 14d). Returns one row per metric with time-series (TS) and cross-sectional (CS) letter grades, information coefficient (ic), hit-rate, observation count, anti-predictive flags, a keep/deactivate recommendation, and a grade_divergence flag, plus a summary of grade counts. Use it to decide which metrics actually predict for a specific asset before trusting a signal, and pair it with /api/asset/top-predictors (ranking) and /api/asset/thesis (narrated conviction).

name: Cryptyx Peer Cluster
description: Nearest-neighbour peers for one crypto asset in Cryptyx's 8-class factor space at a chosen horizon — returns the target asset's metrics plus the k closest peers ranked by Euclidean distance with per-peer divergence and shared-factor-class stats, for hedge selection and basket construction.

inputSchema.description: symbol (required) = target asset ticker, uppercased (e.g. BTC/ETH/SOL). horizon (optional) = factor-score horizon, one of 7d/14d/30d/90d (default 30d). k (optional int) = number of peers to return, clamped 1-20 (default 8).

target.description: The queried asset in factor space: { asset, composite (number, overall factor score), ret_7d (number, 7d return), classes (array of the factor-classes present: OB/TR/EFF/FUT/OPT/VOL/CORR/FLOW) }.

peers.description: The k nearest peers, ranked ascending by distance. Each: { asset, distance (Euclidean distance in factor space), composite (peer overall factor score), divergence (signed divergence vs target), ret_7d (peer 7d return), shared_classes (array of factor-classes shared with the target) }.

_next.description: Recommended follow-up paid Cryptyx endpoints (description + hints[] with path/method/price_usd/reason).

usage.callShape: GET https://cryptyx.ai/api/asset/peer-cluster?symbol=BTC. REQUIRED query param: symbol (asset ticker, uppercased, e.g. BTC/ETH/SOL). Optional: horizon=7d|14d|30d|90d (default 30d), k=1-20 (number of peers, default 8). No request body. Pays $0.05 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453).
usage.outputShape: ok (bool); symbol (string); horizon (string, echoes the requested/default horizon); target = { asset, composite (number), ret_7d (number), classes (array of factor-classes: OB/TR/EFF/FUT/OPT/VOL/CORR/FLOW) }; peers = array of k objects ranked ascending by distance, each { asset, distance (Euclidean distance in factor space, number), composite (number), divergence (signed number vs target), ret_7d (number), shared_classes (array of factor-classes shared with target) }; _next = { description, hints[] } of recommended follow-up paid Cryptyx endpoints. Live BTC call returned 8 peers (RUNE, FRAX, PEPE, CRV, AAVE, RLUSD, SYRUP, TFUEL).
quirks: symbol is REQUIRED and must be the QUERY param `symbol` (NOT `asset` like some sibling endpoints); a bare GET with no symbol still returns a 402 challenge but the paid call would 400 without it.
horizon accepts only 7d/14d/30d/90d (default 30d) — note this is a shorter set than asset-factors' 8 horizons.
k (peer count) is clamped server-side to 1-20; default 8.
peers are ranked ascending by `distance` (smallest distance = closest peer); numbers are raw floats, not percentiles.
target.classes and peers[].shared_classes vary per asset (subset of OB/TR/EFF/FUT/OPT/VOL/CORR/FLOW); use shared_classes to gauge how comparable a peer is.
Response includes a _next.hints[] block advertising other paid Cryptyx asset endpoints (thesis, asymmetry, active-signals, regime-context, thesis-journal) at $0.05 each.
usage.guide: Cryptyx Peer Cluster finds the nearest peers for one crypto asset in Cryptyx's 8-class factor space, for hedge selection and basket construction. GET https://cryptyx.ai/api/asset/peer-cluster?symbol=BTC — symbol is REQUIRED (ticker like BTC/ETH/SOL). Optional horizon=7d|14d|30d|90d (default 30d) sets the factor-score horizon; optional k=1-20 (default 8) sets how many peers to return. No request body; pays $0.05 USDC via x402 on Base. The response gives the target asset's metrics (composite, ret_7d, factor classes) plus the k closest peers ranked ascending by Euclidean distance, each with divergence, composite, ret_7d and the factor-classes shared with the target. Use the closest low-divergence peers to build a comparable basket or pick a hedge; the response's _next.hints suggest follow-up asset endpoints (thesis, asymmetry, active-signals) for deeper context.

name: Cryptyx Asset Regime Context
description: Per-asset macro regime context for one crypto symbol — the current regime id and confidence, its days-in-regime streak, conditional forward-return stats (n, mean/median return, hit-rate) by regime across 1d/7d/14d/30d horizons, and the top historical regime transitions — grounding position sizing in what has historically happened next.

symbol.description: Asset ticker (uppercased server-side), e.g. BTC, ETH, SOL. Required.

horizon.description: Selected horizon echoed back in selected_horizon (default 14d). Note: the stats array still returns ALL horizons regardless of this value.

stats.description: Conditional forward-return stats, one row per (regime x horizon). Each: { regime, horizon (1d/7d/14d/30d), n (sample count), mean_return, median_return, hit_rate }.

transitions.description: Top historical regime transitions. Each: { from_regime, to_regime, n (observed count) }.

_next.description: Recommended follow-up paid Cryptyx endpoints (hints[] with path/method/price_usd/reason).

usage.callShape: GET https://cryptyx.ai/api/asset/regime-context?symbol={symbol}. REQUIRED query param: symbol (ticker, e.g. BTC/ETH/SOL; uppercased server-side). Optional: horizon=1d|7d|14d|30d (default 14d; echoed as selected_horizon, but the stats array returns all horizons regardless). No request body. Pays $0.05 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453). Result returned inline in the 200 (synchronous, no poll).
usage.outputShape: ok (bool); symbol; selected_horizon; current { asof_day, regime (e.g. REGIME_CONSOLIDATION/REGIME_EXPANSION/REGIME_DELEVERAGING), confidence (0-1), days_in_regime (int) }; stats[] one row per (regime x horizon) { regime, horizon (1d/7d/14d/30d), n (sample count), mean_return, median_return, hit_rate (0-1) }; transitions[] top historical regime moves { from_regime, to_regime, n }; _next { description, hints[] } of recommended paid Cryptyx endpoints. Verified live: symbol=BTC -> current { asof_day=2026-07-29, regime=REGIME_CONSOLIDATION, confidence=0.606, days_in_regime=56 }, 12 stats rows (3 regimes x 4 horizons), 6 transition rows.
quirks: The query param is `symbol` here (NOT `asset` as on sibling /api/asset-factors and /api/asset-regimes); a bare call without symbol returns a 402 challenge but the paid call would not yield meaningful data — always supply symbol.

Live regime ids come back with a REGIME_ prefix (REGIME_CONSOLIDATION, REGIME_EXPANSION, REGIME_DELEVERAGING); the 402 bazaar example shows lowercase (expansion/consolidation/contraction) — treat regime as an opaque string and don't hard-code the casing.
horizon only sets selected_horizon; the stats array always returns every horizon (1d/7d/14d/30d) x every regime regardless of the horizon param.

Returns aren't clamped to positive — mean/median_return and hit_rate can be negative/below 0.5 (e.g. REGIME_EXPANSION 30d mean_return -0.106 live); these are conditional historical forward returns, not forecasts.
Data is from a nightly pipeline — current.asof_day lags the wall-clock day and updates once daily, not intraday.
Response includes a _next.hints[] block advertising other paid Cryptyx asset endpoints (thesis, asymmetry, active-signals, thesis-journal) at $0.05 each; ignore unless chaining calls.
usage.guide: Cryptyx Asset Regime Context returns one crypto asset's macro-regime picture in a single paid call: the current regime (id + confidence + days-in-regime streak), conditional forward-return stats by regime across 1d/7d/14d/30d horizons (sample count n, mean/median return, hit-rate), and the top historical regime transitions. GET https://cryptyx.ai/api/asset/regime-context?symbol=BTC — symbol is REQUIRED (ticker like BTC/ETH/SOL); optional horizon=1d|7d|14d|30d (default 14d) only sets selected_horizon, the stats array always spans all horizons. No request body; pays $0.05 USDC via x402 on Base. Use it to gate/size positions in what historically follows a given regime, or to read transition odds; note the returns are historical conditionals (can be negative), not forecasts. The response's _next.hints suggest follow-up asset endpoints (thesis, asymmetry, active-signals) for deeper context.

name: Cryptyx Asset Regime
description: Per-asset market-regime state for one crypto asset across all 8 horizons (1d/7d/14d/30d/60d/90d/180d/365d) with regime label, confidence, factor scores, cross-class state, macro regime, per-horizon divergence flags and an asset-vs-market alignment call at each timescale.

symbol.description: Asset symbol (uppercased server-side), e.g. BTC. REQUIRED query param.

horizon.description: Optional horizon filter: 1d, 7d, 14d, 30d, 60d, 90d, 180d, 365d. Omit for all 8.

regimes.description: One entry per horizon; each has horizon, regime_label, regime_confidence, factor_scores {OB,TR,EFF,FUT,VOL,CORR,FLOW}, cross_class_state, n_classes, macro_regime, macro_confidence, asset_vs_market.

usage.callShape: GET https://cryptyx.ai/api/asset/regime?symbol={SYMBOL}. The ONLY required input is the query param `symbol` (asset ticker, e.g. BTC/ETH/SOL; uppercased server-side). Optional query params: `horizon` (one of 1d,7d,14d,30d,60d,90d,180d,365d) to restrict to a single timescale, and `days` (1-90 lookback window, default 1). No request body. Pays $0.01 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453).
usage.outputShape: { ok:true, symbol:"BTC", asof_day:"2026-07-29", regimes:[ { asof_day, horizon (1d..365d), regime_label (e.g. BROAD_EXPANSION, ACCUMULATION, CHOPPY, OVERSOLD_REVERSAL, VOLATILITY_REGIME, DIVERGENT), regime_confidence (0-1), factor_scores:{OB,TR,EFF,FUT,VOL,CORR,FLOW}, cross_class_state (e.g. TRANSITIONAL), n_classes, macro_regime, macro_confidence, asset_vs_market (aligned|divergent|divergent_bullish|divergent_bearish) } x8 horizons ], divergences:[...], _next:{ hints:[{path,method,price_usd,reason}] } }
quirks: The REQUIRED query param is `symbol` (NOT `asset`). The 402 resource.url and the pre-filter callHint both showed `?asset=BTC`, but the x402 gate returns 402 before validating params; the actual server-side required param per the 402 bazaar schema is `symbol`. Calling with `asset=` alone would buy an HTTP 400.
Live output `regimes` is an ARRAY of 8 horizon objects; the 402 extensions.bazaar example instead shows `regimes` as a horizon-keyed object with only 3 keys — the live array shape is authoritative.

`divergences` is a top-level array that can be empty (was [] on the verified BTC call even though per-horizon `asset_vs_market` flags showed divergence); the divergence signal is carried per-horizon inside each regimes[] entry via `asset_vs_market` / `macro_regime`.
Enhanced view over /api/asset-regimes (market-wide table): this endpoint adds per-horizon asset-vs-market comparison and divergence indicators for a single asset.
factor_scores can be negative and are unbounded (not 0-1); regime_confidence is 0-1.
Response includes a paid-endpoint `_next` recommendation block pointing at sibling Cryptyx per-asset ops (thesis, asymmetry, active-signals, regime-context, thesis-journal) at $0.05 each.
usage.guide: Get the current market-regime read for one crypto asset across every timescale in a single $0.01 x402 GET. Call GET https://cryptyx.ai/api/asset/regime?symbol=BTC (swap BTC for any ticker; add &horizon=30d to focus one timescale, &days=N for a wider lookback). Returns regimes[] with one object per horizon (1d,7d,14d,30d,60d,90d,180d,365d): each gives a regime_label, regime_confidence, seven factor_scores (OB order-book, TR trend, EFF efficiency, FUT futures, VOL volatility, CORR correlation, FLOW flow), the cross_class_state, the prevailing macro_regime + confidence, and an asset_vs_market alignment call (aligned / divergent / divergent_bullish / divergent_bearish) that flags whether the asset is in-step with the broader market at that horizon. Use it to detect regime shifts and asset-vs-macro divergence before acting. No body, no API key; pays $0.01 USDC via x402 on Base.

name: Cryptyx Asset Regimes
description: Per-asset macro regime classification with confidence — expansion, consolidation, or deleveraging — plus a secondary regime, its confidence, and the resolution mode; snapshot (latest canonical day) or series (last N days). Factor-derived from Cryptyx's nightly 04:15 UTC pipeline.

asset.description: Asset symbol (e.g. BTC, ETH, SOL) — uppercased server-side. Required.

mode.description: snapshot = latest canonical day only; series = last N days anchored to latest. Default snapshot.

days.description: Lookback days for series mode (1-365). Default 90. Ignored when mode=snapshot.

usage.callShape: GET https://cryptyx.ai/api/asset-regimes?asset={asset}. Required query param: asset (symbol, e.g. BTC/ETH/SOL; uppercased server-side). Optional: mode=snapshot|series (default snapshot), days=1-365 (default 90, only used for mode=series). No request body. Pays $0.01 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453). Result is returned inline in the 200 (synchronous, no poll).
usage.outputShape: ok (bool), asset, mode, asof_day, regimes[] each with { asof_day, asset, regime (expansion|consolidation|deleveraging), regime_confidence (0-1), regime_secondary (string|null), regime_secondary_confidence (number|null), resolution_mode (single|max_confidence|...) }. Also _next.hints[] — recommended follow-up Cryptyx endpoints with price_usd (informational; not part of the data). Verified live: asset=BTC snapshot -> regime=consolidation, regime_confidence=0.606, regime_secondary=null, resolution_mode=single, asof_day=2026-07-29.
quirks: asset query param is REQUIRED; without it the endpoint still returns a 402 challenge but a paid call without asset would not return meaningful data — always supply asset.
mode=snapshot returns a single-element regimes[] (latest canonical day); mode=series returns up to `days` daily rows anchored to the latest canonical day.

regime_secondary / regime_secondary_confidence are null when resolution_mode is 'single' (only one dominant regime); they are populated (with resolution_mode 'max_confidence') when a secondary regime is present.
Data is from a nightly 04:15 UTC pipeline — asof_day lags the wall-clock day and updates once daily, not intraday.
Response includes a _next.hints[] block advertising other paid Cryptyx endpoints; ignore it unless chaining calls.
usage.guide: Cryptyx Asset Regimes classifies one crypto asset's current macro regime — expansion, consolidation, or deleveraging — with a confidence score, plus a secondary regime and the resolution mode, factor-derived from Cryptyx's nightly 04:15 UTC pipeline. GET https://cryptyx.ai/api/asset-regimes?asset={asset}. Required query param asset is the symbol (e.g. BTC, ETH, SOL; uppercased server-side). Optional mode=snapshot (default; latest day only) or mode=series with days=1-365 (default 90) for a daily time series. No request body. Pays $0.01 USDC via x402 on Base. Returns JSON inline (synchronous): ok, asset, mode, asof_day, and regimes[] with regime, regime_confidence, regime_secondary, regime_secondary_confidence, and resolution_mode. Use it to gate position sizing/risk on whether an asset is expanding, consolidating, or deleveraging.

name: Cryptyx Signal Events
description: Per-asset historical ledger of triggered quantitative signals (A/B grades only) over a 7-365 day window: each event carries the signal id/name, factor class, direction (long/short/neutral), z-score, confidence, horizon, grade, close price, and its realised 7-day forward return.

inputSchema.description: symbol (required) = asset ticker, e.g. BTC/ETH/SOL (uppercased + trimmed server-side). days (optional number 7-365, default 90) = lookback window for the signal ledger. Both are query params on a GET; no request body.

events.description: One record per triggered signal (A/B grades only), chronological. Each: { asof_day (date), signal_id (e.g. TR_MOMO_CONT_14D), name (human label), class (factor class: OB/TR/EFF/FUT/VOL/CORR/FLOW/OPT), direction (long/short/neutral), z (number, raw z-score, can be negative), confidence (0-1 float), horizon (e.g. 7d/30d), grade (A|B), close_px (number, close price at trigger), fwd_return_7d (number, realised 7-day forward return, decimal fraction) }. 111 events observed for BTC over days=90.

_next.description: Recommended follow-up paid Cryptyx endpoints ({ description, hints[] } with path/method/price_usd/reason) — thesis, asymmetry, active-signals, regime-context, thesis-journal.

usage.callShape: GET https://cryptyx.ai/api/asset/signal-events?symbol=BTC&days=90. REQUIRED query param: symbol (asset ticker, e.g. BTC/ETH/SOL). Optional: days (7-365, default 90) = lookback window. No request body. Pays $0.05 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453).
usage.outputShape: ok (bool); symbol (string); days (number); events = array of triggered signal records (111 observed for BTC/90d), each { asof_day (date), signal_id (string), name (string), class (factor class OB/TR/EFF/FUT/VOL/CORR/FLOW/OPT), direction (long|short|neutral), z (number, raw z-score, may be negative), confidence (0-1 float), horizon (e.g. 7d/30d), grade (A|B), close_px (number), fwd_return_7d (number, decimal fraction) }; meta { ic_context } ; _next { description, hints[] } of recommended follow-up paid Cryptyx endpoints.
quirks: symbol is REQUIRED — a bare GET with no symbol still returns a 402 challenge, but the paid call would 400 without it; always supply symbol.
The query param is `symbol` (NOT `asset` as some sibling Cryptyx endpoints use); it is uppercased + trimmed server-side.
Only A and B grade signals are returned (the ledger is pre-filtered; C+ grades are omitted).
z is the raw z-score (can be negative, e.g. -2.11); confidence is a separate 0-1 float. Direction can disagree with the sign of z.
fwd_return_7d is a realised 7-day forward return as a decimal fraction (0.0412 = +4.12%); recent events near the window edge still carry a value (look-ahead within the historical ledger).
days accepts 7-365 (default 90); observed horizons in the BTC/90d window were 7d and 30d, classes OB/TR/EFF/VOL/CORR/FLOW.
Response includes a _next.hints[] block advertising other paid Cryptyx asset endpoints (thesis, asymmetry, active-signals, regime-context, thesis-journal) at $0.05 each.
usage.guide: Cryptyx Signal Events returns a per-asset historical ledger of triggered quantitative signals in one paid call. GET https://cryptyx.ai/api/asset/signal-events?symbol=BTC&days=90 — symbol is REQUIRED (ticker like BTC/ETH/SOL); days is optional (7-365, default 90) and sets the lookback window. No request body; pays $0.05 USDC via x402 on Base. The response's events[] lists only A/B-grade signals, each with signal_id/name, factor class (OB/TR/EFF/VOL/CORR/FLOW/...), direction (long/short/neutral), z-score, confidence (0-1), horizon (e.g. 7d/30d), grade (A|B), close price at trigger, and the realised 7-day forward return — useful for auditing which signals fired for an asset and how they actually paid off. meta.ic_context flags the scoring context; _next.hints suggest deeper per-asset endpoints (thesis, asymmetry, active-signals, regime-context) for follow-up.

name: Cryptyx Asset Thesis
description: Claude-narrated per-asset conviction thesis (3-5 sentences) plus a structured evidence pack for one crypto asset: composite score and rank vs the ~200-asset universe, 1d/7d/30d returns and realised vol, factor-class t-scores/bands, top active signals, and top per-asset time-series predictors.

symbol.description: REQUIRED. Asset symbol, uppercased server-side (e.g. BTC, ETH, SOL). Query param.

horizon.description: Optional. Factor horizon for the t_score_pct snapshot. One of 7d/14d/30d/90d, defaults to 30d. Query param.

evidence.description: composite {score, rank, rank_pct, score_yesterday, score_delta}; returns {ret_1d, ret_7d, ret_30d, vol_rv_30d}; factors[] {class, t_score_pct, t_band}; active_signals[] {signal_id, name, class, z, confidence, ic, hit_rate, grade}; active_signals_total; active_signals_high_grade; top_ts_metrics[] {metric_id, class, name, ts_grade, ts_ic, ts_hit_rate, cs_grade, cs_ic, grade_divergence}.

_next.description: Recommended paid x402 next-call hints (sibling /api/asset/* endpoints).

usage.callShape: GET https://cryptyx.ai/api/asset/thesis?symbol=<TICKER> and settle the x402 402 challenge (Base USDC, $0.05). REQUIRED query param 'symbol' (asset ticker, e.g. BTC/ETH/SOL; uppercased server-side) — a bare GET without it does not return usable data. Optional query param 'horizon' (7d/14d/30d/90d, default 30d). No request body; result is returned inline in the 200 response. 4-hour server cache per symbol/horizon.
usage.outputShape: JSON object { ok, symbol, asof_day (date), horizon, regime (e.g. consolidation/expansion/deleveraging), regime_confidence (0..1), source, thesis (3-5 sentence narrated string), evidence { composite {score, rank, rank_pct, score_yesterday, score_delta}, returns {ret_1d, ret_7d, ret_30d, vol_rv_30d}, factors[] {class (CORR/EFF/FLOW/FUT/OB/OPT/TR/VOL), t_score_pct, t_band (NEUTRAL/BULL/STRONG_BULL/...)}, active_signals[] {signal_id, name, class, z, confidence, ic, hit_rate, grade}, active_signals_total, active_signals_high_grade, top_ts_metrics[] {metric_id, class, name, ts_grade, ts_ic, ts_hit_rate, cs_grade, cs_ic, grade_divergence} }, model ('CRYPTYX AI'), generated_at (ISO ts), cache_hit (bool), _next {description, hints[] {path, method, price_usd, reason}} }. Paid live run for BTC (asof 2026-07-29, 30d): thesis narrated 'neutral with deteriorating conviction', composite score 48.7 / rank 112 of ~200, all 8 factor classes NEUTRAL, 19 active signals (1 high-grade).

Live-observed composite score and returns are on a different scale than the stale bazaar/openapi example: live composite.score is ~0-100 with rank_pct ~0-100 (e.g. score 48.7, rank_pct 56.92), and returns/vol appear to be in percent (ret_30d 6.27, vol_rv_30d 31.29) — do not assume the 0..1 values shown in the provider's documented example.
Response is a point-in-time daily snapshot keyed by asof_day with a 4-hour server cache (cache_hit flag); contents and the narrated thesis change day to day.
The 'thesis' field is a short Claude-narrated ('model':'CRYPTYX AI') natural-language paragraph; everything else in 'evidence' is the structured data behind it.

Response includes a _next block whose hints reference other paid Cryptyx per-asset endpoints (/api/asset/asymmetry, /api/asset/active-signals, /api/asset/regime-context, /api/asset/thesis-journal) at $0.05 each for drill-down.
The payment-required data (accepts + input/output schema + a documented output example) is delivered in the base64 'payment-required' HTTP header on the 402, matching the JSON body.
usage.guide: Per-asset AI conviction thesis from Cryptyx. GET https://cryptyx.ai/api/asset/thesis?symbol=<TICKER> (e.g. BTC, ETH, SOL) and settle the $0.05 x402 payment (USDC on Base); add optional &horizon=7d|14d|30d|90d (default 30d). Returns a 3-5 sentence narrated 'thesis' plus a structured 'evidence' pack: composite score/rank vs the ~200-asset universe, 1d/7d/30d returns and 30d realised vol, per-factor-class t-scores/bands (CORR/EFF/FLOW/FUT/OB/OPT/TR/VOL), top active signals (with z/IC/hit-rate/grade), and top per-asset time-series predictors, plus regime + regime_confidence. Use it to drill into one asset after a market-wide scan (e.g. /api/market-pulse/conviction or /api/assets). Note numeric fields are on a ~0-100 / percent scale in live responses, and a _next block points at sibling per-asset endpoints for deeper drill-down.

name: Cryptyx Top Predictors
description: Per-asset predictor explorer for one crypto asset — the top atomic signals and top 5 metrics ranked by absolute information coefficient (IC) times hit rate, restricted to A/B grades, anti-predictive filtered and family-deduped (max 2 per class). Signals carry walk-forward robustness; metrics carry time-series-vs-cross-sectional divergence.

inputSchema.description: symbol (required) = asset ticker, uppercased server-side (e.g. BTC/ETH/SOL). horizon (optional) = forward-return horizon, one of 7d/14d/30d, defaults to 14d.

signals.description: Top atomic signals ranked by |IC| x hit-rate (A/B grades only, family-deduped). Each: { signal_id, name, class (TR/VOL/OB/EFF/FUT/CORR/FLOW/OPT), horizon, ic, hit_rate, ir, grade (A/B), n_triggered_180d, last_triggered (date), walk_forward ({ asof_day, window_days, split_pct, is_ic, is_hit_rate, is_n_triggers, is_n_obs, oos_ic, oos_hit_rate, oos_n_triggers, oos_n_obs, overfit_ratio, ic_delta, reliability_grade } or absent) }. May be empty for an asset with no qualifying signals.

metrics.description: Top 5 metrics ranked by per-asset time-series |IC| x hit-rate. Each: { metric_id, name, class (OPT/FLOW/EFF/FUT/TR/...), ts_grade, cs_grade (A/B/C/F), polarity (1 or -1), description, ts_ic, ts_hit_rate, cs_ic, cs_hit_rate, n_obs, current_z, current_pctl, asof_day (date) }.

meta.description: { signals_candidates, metrics_candidates, gate (e.g. 'ts_health_grade IN (A,B) AND NOT is_anti_predictive'), per_asset_metric_hit_rate (bool), ic_context (e.g. time_series), diversity (e.g. 'family-dedup + max 2 per class'), note (clarifies metric rankings use per-asset time-series IC while signals use cross-sectional IC) }.

_next.description: Recommended follow-up paid Cryptyx endpoints ({ description, hints[] } with path/method/price_usd/reason).

usage.callShape: GET https://cryptyx.ai/api/asset/top-predictors?symbol=BTC. REQUIRED query param: symbol (asset ticker, e.g. BTC/ETH/SOL; uppercased server-side). Optional: horizon (7d/14d/30d, default 14d). No request body. Pays $0.05 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453); result returns inline in the 200.
usage.outputShape: ok (bool); symbol (string); horizon (string, e.g. 14d); signals = array of top atomic signals (each { signal_id, name, class (TR/VOL/OB/EFF/FUT/CORR/FLOW/OPT), horizon, ic, hit_rate, ir, grade (A/B), n_triggered_180d, last_triggered, walk_forward { asof_day, window_days, split_pct, is_ic, is_hit_rate, is_n_triggers, is_n_obs, oos_ic, oos_hit_rate, oos_n_triggers, oos_n_obs, overfit_ratio, ic_delta, reliability_grade } }) — MAY BE EMPTY; metrics = up to 5 top metrics (each { metric_id, name, class (OPT/FLOW/EFF/FUT/...), ts_grade, cs_grade (A/B/C/F), polarity (+/-1), description, ts_ic, ts_hit_rate, cs_ic, cs_hit_rate, n_obs, current_z, current_pctl, asof_day }); meta ({ signals_candidates, metrics_candidates, gate, per_asset_metric_hit_rate, ic_context, diversity, note }); _next ({ description, hints[] } of recommended follow-up paid Cryptyx endpoints).
quirks: symbol is REQUIRED — a bare GET with no symbol still returns a 402 challenge (and even 402 with a wrong/echoed param), but the paid call needs a valid symbol to return a real explorer; always supply it.
The provider-note hint used 'asset=BTC' generically, but the actual documented + server-accepted query param name is `symbol` (confirmed via openapi.json parameters and the 402 bazaar input schema).
signals[] can be EMPTY even on a successful 200 (observed for BTC: signals_candidates=0, so 0 signals) while metrics[] still returned 5 rows — treat both arrays as independently optional.

Two distinct scoring contexts: signal ranking uses CROSS-SECTIONAL IC, metric ranking uses PER-ASSET TIME-SERIES IC (meta.note + meta.ic_context spell this out); metrics carry both ts_* and cs_* IC/hit-rate so you can see the divergence.
cs_grade can be 'F' (and ts_grade A) on the same metric — the two grades measure different things; polarity (+1/-1) tells you the direction the metric predicts.
Diversity is enforced: family-dedup plus max 2 per class, A/B grades only, anti-predictive signals filtered out (meta.gate/meta.diversity).
Response includes a _next.hints[] block advertising follow-up paid Cryptyx endpoints (thesis, asymmetry, active-signals, regime-context, thesis-journal).
usage.guide: Cryptyx Top Predictors is a per-asset best-of explorer: in one paid call it returns the top atomic signals and top 5 metrics for one crypto asset, ranked by absolute information coefficient times hit rate, restricted to A/B grades, anti-predictive filtered and family-deduped (max 2 per class). GET https://cryptyx.ai/api/asset/top-predictors?symbol=BTC — symbol is REQUIRED (ticker like BTC/ETH/SOL, uppercased server-side); optional horizon is one of 7d/14d/30d (default 14d). No request body; pays $0.05 USDC via x402 on Base, result inline in the 200. signals[] entries carry class/horizon/IC/hit-rate/IR/grade plus a walk-forward IS/OOS robustness block; metrics[] entries carry both time-series (ts_*) and cross-sectional (cs_*) IC/hit-rate, a polarity, current z-score and percentile, and separate ts_grade/cs_grade. Note the two ranking contexts differ (signals cross-sectional, metrics per-asset time-series per meta.note), and signals[] can come back empty for an asset while metrics[] still populates. Use this when you want the single strongest predictive signals/metrics for an asset rather than the full firing panel; the response's _next.hints point to thesis/asymmetry/active-signals/regime-context/thesis-journal for deeper follow-up.

name: Cryptyx Top Setups
description: Historical signal edge for one crypto asset and forward horizon — up to 6 A/B-graded atomic signals that actually worked on that asset, grouped into reversal/continuation/breakout lanes, each with hit rate, mean forward return and walk-forward in-sample/out-of-sample stats.

inputSchema.description: symbol (required) = asset ticker, e.g. BTC/ETH/SOL (trimmed + uppercased server-side). horizon (optional) = forward-return horizon used for ranking; one of 7d, 14d, 30d (default 14d).

setups.description: Up to ~6 graded setups. Each: { lane (reversal|continuation|breakout), signal_id, name, class (e.g. VOL/TR/EFF), grade (A/B), tags[], n_triggers, hit_rate, mean_fwd_return, median_fwd_return, last_triggered (date), ic_global, hit_rate_global, score, walk_forward: { asof_day, window_days, split_pct, is_ic, is_hit_rate, is_n_triggers, is_n_obs, oos_ic, oos_hit_rate, oos_n_triggers, oos_n_obs, overfit_ratio, ic_delta, reliability_grade (green|yellow|red) } }.

counts.description: { reversal, continuation, breakout, qualified } — number of setups per lane and total qualified.

_next.description: Recommended follow-up paid Cryptyx endpoints (hints[] with path/method/price_usd/reason).

usage.callShape: GET https://cryptyx.ai/api/asset/top-setups?symbol=BTC&horizon=14d. REQUIRED query param: symbol (asset ticker, e.g. BTC/ETH/SOL). Optional: horizon = 7d|14d|30d (default 14d). No request body. Pays $0.05 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453).
usage.outputShape: ok (bool); symbol (string); horizon (string, 7d|14d|30d); setups = array of up to ~6 graded setups, each { lane (reversal|continuation|breakout), signal_id (e.g. VOL_COMPRESSION_7v30), name, class (VOL/TR/EFF/...), grade (A|B), tags[], n_triggers (int), hit_rate (0-1), mean_fwd_return (fraction), median_fwd_return, last_triggered (date), ic_global, hit_rate_global, score, walk_forward { asof_day, window_days, split_pct, is_ic, is_hit_rate, is_n_triggers, is_n_obs, oos_ic, oos_hit_rate, oos_n_triggers, oos_n_obs, overfit_ratio, ic_delta, reliability_grade (green|yellow|red) } }; counts { reversal, continuation, breakout, qualified }; meta { ic_context, gate, scope, note }; _next { description, hints[] } of recommended follow-up paid Cryptyx endpoints.
quirks: The required query param is `symbol` (NOT `asset` — the discovery callHint said asset=BTC, but the live 402 bazaar input and the paid 200 both use symbol). A bare GET with no symbol still returns a 402 challenge, but the paid call needs symbol or it would 400 — always supply symbol.
horizon accepts only 7d, 14d, or 30d and defaults to 14d; other values are not documented.

setups can be empty or short — the response is gated (health_grade IN (A,B) AND NOT is_anti_predictive AND n_triggers >= 3), so a low-activity asset/horizon returns few or zero qualified setups (counts.qualified shows how many).
hit_rate and *_return are fractions (e.g. hit_rate 0.52 = 52%, mean_fwd_return 0.0022 = 0.22%), not percentages.

walk_forward.reliability_grade is a green/yellow/red label; overfit_ratio and ic_delta compare in-sample vs out-of-sample edge — a yellow/red grade or negative is_ic means the setup is weakly out-of-sample.
Response includes a _next.hints[] block advertising other paid Cryptyx asset endpoints (thesis, asymmetry, active-signals, regime-context, thesis-journal) at $0.05 each.
usage.guide: Cryptyx Top Setups returns the historically-proven signal edge for one crypto asset over a chosen forward horizon in a single paid call: up to ~6 A/B-graded atomic signals that actually worked on that asset, grouped into reversal / continuation / breakout lanes. GET https://cryptyx.ai/api/asset/top-setups?symbol=BTC&horizon=14d — symbol is REQUIRED (ticker like BTC/ETH/SOL); horizon is optional and must be 7d, 14d or 30d (default 14d). No request body; pays $0.05 USDC via x402 on Base. Each setup gives lane, signal name/class, grade, n_triggers, hit_rate, mean/median forward return, and a walk_forward block with in-sample vs out-of-sample IC, hit rate, overfit_ratio and a reliability_grade (green/yellow/red) so you can judge whether the edge held out of sample. Setups are gated to graded, non-anti-predictive signals with >=3 triggers, so counts.qualified may be small or zero for quiet assets. Use it to see which historical signals have an edge on an asset right now; the response's _next.hints suggest follow-ups (thesis, active-signals, asymmetry, regime-context).

name: Cryptyx Assets
description: The 200+ crypto-asset master ranking feed: per-asset composite score and rank, recent 1d/7d/30d returns, realised volatility (7d/30d), Sharpe ratios, and macro regime with confidence — as a same-day snapshot or a daily series over the last N days, for portfolio construction and rotation.
