name: Cryptyx Signal Explain
description: Factor t-score attribution for one crypto (asset, day): raw z-score t_scores across the 8 factor-classes (OB, TR, EFF, FUT, VOL, CORR, FLOW, OPT) x 8 horizons (1d-365d) plus the single weighted composite score — showing which factor classes drove a given signal call.

inputSchema.description: signal_id (required) = signal registry ID, uppercased (e.g. TR_MOMO_CONT_14D); echoed back in the response but NOT used by the underlying SQL function, so any registry id is accepted. day (required) = anchor day in YYYY-MM-DD (UTC-1 canonical). asset (required) = asset symbol, uppercased (e.g. BTC/ETH/SOL). The factor cube returned is keyed on (asset, day).

explanation.description: { asset, asof_day, signal_id, composite (number, the single weighted composite score), factors: array of ~64 cells one per (class x horizon): { class (OB/TR/EFF/FUT/VOL/CORR/FLOW/OPT), horizon (1d/7d/14d/30d/60d/90d/180d/365d), t_score (number, raw z-score, can be negative) } }.

_next.description: Recommended follow-up paid Cryptyx endpoints: { description, hints[] } where each hint has path/method/price_usd/reason (e.g. /api/signals/backtest, /api/signals/simulate, /api/asset/active-signals, /api/asset/top-predictors, /api/asset/thesis).

usage.callShape: GET https://cryptyx.ai/api/signals/explain?signal_id=TR_MOMO_CONT_14D&day=2026-06-18&asset=BTC. THREE required query params: signal_id (registry id, uppercased — echoed but not used by SQL), day (YYYY-MM-DD anchor day), asset (uppercased symbol, e.g. BTC). No request body. Pays $0.01 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453). Result is keyed on (asset, day).
usage.outputShape: ok (bool); signal_id (string, echoed); day (string, echoed); asset (string, echoed); explanation = { asset, asof_day (date), signal_id, composite (number, single weighted composite score — observed 0.0243 live), factors: array of ~64 cells (8 classes x 8 horizons), each { class (one of OB,TR,EFF,FUT,VOL,CORR,FLOW,OPT), horizon (one of 1d,7d,14d,30d,60d,90d,180d,365d), t_score (number, RAW z-score, can be negative) } }; _next = { description, hints[] } of recommended follow-up paid Cryptyx endpoints (backtest, simulate, active-signals, top-predictors, thesis).
quirks: All THREE params (signal_id, day, asset) are required — a bare GET returns a 402 challenge but a paid call missing them would fail; always supply all three.

signal_id is echoed back verbatim but NOT used by the underlying SQL function (documented in the 402 input schema) — the factor cube is computed purely from (asset, day). Any valid uppercase registry id works; the response is identical regardless of which id you pass for a given (asset, day).
day must be a real anchor day with data (YYYY-MM-DD, UTC-1 canonical). The provider's documented example 2026-06-18 works.
t_score is a RAW z-score number (e.g. -0.994, 1.552), NOT the 0-100 percentile string that /api/asset-factors returns; it can be negative and has no t_band label.
composite is a single number in explanation.composite (observed 0.0243), not the {score, comp_version, rank} object shown in the stale 402 bazaar example.
Live response returns all 64 cells (8 classes x 8 horizons); the 402 bazaar 'example' only shows a 5-row illustrative subset under a different key (factor_scores) — trust the live shape.
Response includes a _next.hints[] block advertising other paid Cryptyx endpoints (backtest/simulate at $0.05, active-signals/top-predictors/thesis at $0.05).
usage.guide: Cryptyx Signal Explain returns the factor attribution behind a signal for one crypto (asset, day) in a single paid call: raw z-score t_scores across 8 factor-classes (OB, TR, EFF, FUT, VOL, CORR, FLOW, OPT) x 8 horizons (1d..365d) plus a single weighted composite. GET https://cryptyx.ai/api/signals/explain?signal_id=TR_MOMO_CONT_14D&day=2026-06-18&asset=BTC — all three params are required: asset (uppercase symbol like BTC/ETH/SOL) and day (YYYY-MM-DD anchor day) determine the result; signal_id is echoed back but not used by the SQL, so pass any uppercase registry id (e.g. TR_MOMO_CONT_14D). No request body; pays $0.01 USDC via x402 on Base. Each cell: { class, horizon, t_score (raw z-score, can be negative) }; explanation.composite is the weighted composite score. Use this to inspect WHICH factor classes/horizons drove a signal on a specific day; the response's _next.hints suggest follow-ups (backtest, simulate, active-signals, top-predictors, thesis). Note vs /api/asset-factors: that endpoint gives the current/series percentile-banded cube (t_score_pct string + t_band), while this gives raw z-scores + a composite for an explicit (asset, day).

name: Cryptyx Top Signals
description: Returns the top 10 atomic crypto quant signals ranked by 7-day cross-sectional information coefficient (IC), gated to A/B health grades and non-anti-predictive names, each with trigger stats and a 7-day walk-forward in-sample/out-of-sample robustness block.

backends.outputSchema: { ok:boolean, count:number, signals:[ { signal_id, name, description, class, horizon, tags:string[], geometry_type, active_version, active_params:object, ic_7d, hit_rate_7d, n_obs_7d, n_triggers_7d, health_grade, unique_assets_observed, unique_assets_ever_triggered, trigger_rate_per_asset_day, walk_forward:{ asof_day, window_days, split_pct, is_ic, is_hit_rate, is_n_triggers, is_n_obs, oos_ic, oos_hit_rate, oos_n_triggers, oos_n_obs, overfit_ratio, ic_delta, reliability_grade } } ], selection_criteria:object, durationMs:number, _next:object }

usage.callShape: GET https://cryptyx.ai/api/signals/top with no query params and no request body. Pays $0.01 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453). Result (top-10 signals) is returned inline in the 200 response.
usage.outputShape: Top-level: ok (boolean), count (number, =10), signals[] (array), selection_criteria (object describing the ranking gate), durationMs, and _next (recommended follow-up Cryptyx endpoints). Each signals[] item: signal_id, name, description, class (TR/VOL/CORR/OB/EFF...), horizon (e.g. 7d/30d/180d), tags[], geometry_type, active_version, active_params, ic_7d, hit_rate_7d, n_obs_7d, n_triggers_7d, health_grade (A/B), unique_assets_observed, unique_assets_ever_triggered, trigger_rate_per_asset_day, and a walk_forward block (asof_day, window_days, split_pct, is_ic, is_hit_rate, is_n_triggers, is_n_obs, oos_ic, oos_hit_rate, oos_n_triggers, oos_n_obs, overfit_ratio, ic_delta, reliability_grade).
quirks: Takes NO input at all: bare GET, no query params, no body. This is a whole-market leaderboard, not per-asset (contrast with per-asset Cryptyx ops that require ?asset=BTC).
Numeric metrics like ic_7d, hit_rate_7d and trigger_rate_per_asset_day are returned as STRINGS (e.g. "0.2012"), while walk_forward numeric fields are real JSON numbers.

walk_forward.oos_ic / overfit_ratio / ic_delta can be null and reliability_grade can be 'red' for a signal with too few out-of-sample triggers; a large or negative overfit_ratio flags an unreliable signal even when it ranks high by ic_7d.

Response includes a _next block of recommended paid follow-up Cryptyx endpoints (signals/explain, signals/backtest, signals/catalog, signals/leaderboard) with their prices; these are hints, not part of the signal data.
The selection gate is fixed: health_grade in A/B, is_anti_predictive false, min_n_obs_7d 30, ranked by ic_7d descending, max_results 10.
usage.guide: Fetch the current top 10 crypto quant signals across the whole tracked market, ranked by 7-day cross-sectional information coefficient. Call it with a bare GET https://cryptyx.ai/api/signals/top (no params, no body); pay $0.01 USDC via x402 on Base. Use it to surface which alpha signals (momentum, volatility, correlation, orderbook-liquidity, efficiency) are currently strongest and how robust each is out-of-sample (walk_forward.oos_ic, reliability_grade). Prefer signals with health_grade A and reliability_grade green, and treat ic_7d and hit_rate_7d as strings. To drill into a specific signal on a specific asset, follow up with the paid /api/signals/explain or /api/signals/backtest endpoints listed in the response's _next block.

name: Cryptyx Taker Flow
description: Per-asset daily taker buy/sell flow: taker buy USD, taker sell USD and buy/sell ratio, split into spot and futures arrays, over the last N days — the raw order-flow tape for custom flow models.

inputSchema.description: asset (required) = asset symbol, uppercased server-side (e.g. BTC, ETH, SOL). days (optional int, 1-365, default 30) = lookback window.

asset.description: Asset symbol, uppercased server-side

spot.description: Daily spot taker-flow rows; item fields: asof_day (date), asset, taker_buy_usd (number), taker_sell_usd (number), bs_ratio (number, taker_buy_usd/taker_sell_usd).

futures.description: Daily futures taker-flow rows; same item fields as spot[].

_next.description: Recommended paid x402 next-call hints (e.g. /api/asset/asymmetry, /api/asset/thesis, /api/market-pulse/conviction).

usage.callShape: GET https://cryptyx.ai/api/taker-flow?asset=<SYMBOL>&days=<N> and settle the x402 402 challenge (Base USDC, $0.01). asset is REQUIRED (a bare GET returns 402 but no payload without it); days is optional (1-365, default 30). Result is returned inline in the 200 response.
usage.outputShape: JSON object { spot: [ { asof_day, asset, taker_buy_usd, taker_sell_usd, bs_ratio } ], futures: [ { asof_day, asset, taker_buy_usd, taker_sell_usd, bs_ratio } ], _next: {...} }. Paid run for asset=BTC&days=7 returned 7 spot rows and 7 futures rows (e.g. 2026-07-29 spot taker_buy_usd 572,491,996.73 / taker_sell_usd 503,132,911.02 / bs_ratio 1.1379; futures taker_buy_usd 29.5B / taker_sell_usd 30.1B / bs_ratio 0.9804).
usage.quirks: asset query param is REQUIRED for a real payload — a bare GET (no asset) still returns a payable 402 with an empty {} body, so pay only with asset set or you buy an empty result. Numeric fields (taker_buy_usd, taker_sell_usd, bs_ratio) come back as real JSON numbers (not strings). bs_ratio = taker_buy_usd / taker_sell_usd (>1 = net buying, <1 = net selling). Futures notional dwarfs spot (~50x for BTC). Rows are newest-first, one per day for the last N days. The _next block points at sibling paid endpoints for drill-down.
usage.guide: Call GET https://cryptyx.ai/api/taker-flow?asset=<SYMBOL>&days=<N> (asset required, e.g. BTC/ETH/SOL; days 1-365, default 30) and settle the $0.01 x402 payment (USDC on Base). You get two arrays — spot[] and futures[] — each a daily series of taker_buy_usd, taker_sell_usd and bs_ratio (buy/sell ratio). Use bs_ratio > 1 as net taker buying and < 1 as net taker selling; compare spot vs futures flow to read positioning. This is the raw tape for building custom flow/momentum models. Numeric fields are real numbers; rows are newest-first.

name: Cryptyx Agent Context
description: One-shot crypto market-grounding snapshot for agents in ~200-400ms: factor breadth across 8 factor classes, the top/bottom composite-score assets with their regime, full recent-signal aggregation (per signal_id trigger counts + avg confidence), platform metric/signal/class counts, and pipeline status. Designed to be called before any market-reasoning task.

asset.description: OPTIONAL asset symbol (uppercased/trimmed server-side, e.g. BTC). When set, the response additionally includes `asset`, `perAssetMetrics` (top-10 metrics by abs time-series IC, A/B grades only, anti-predictive excluded) and `gradeContextNote`. Omit for the market-wide grounding snapshot.

pipelineStatus.description: Last pipeline run status (can be null).

_next.description: Recommended next paid x402 calls: { description, hints:[{path,method,price_usd,reason}] }.

usage.callShape: GET https://cryptyx.ai/api/v1/agent-context. No required input and no request body — the bare GET returns the market-wide grounding snapshot. Optional query param `asset` (ticker, e.g. BTC; uppercased server-side) adds per-asset metric grades to the response. Pays $0.01 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453).
usage.outputShape: { ok:true, asofDay:"2026-07-29T00:00:00.000Z", factorBreadth:{ assetsWithScores:196, activeClasses:["CORR","EFF","FLOW","FUT","OB","OPT","TR","VOL"] }, compositeScores:{ topAssets:[{asset:"KAITO",score:"0.389...",asof_day,regime:"deleveraging",regime_confidence:0.8083}, ...10], bottomAssets:[{asset:"XDC",score,...},...] }, recentSignals:{ day, totalTriggered:5509, bySignal:[{signal_id:"CORR_BETA_60D_THR",total_assets:197,triggered_count:8,avg_confidence:"0.4785",asof_day}, ...~150 signals] }, platformCounts:{ metrics:474, signals:160, classes:8 }, pipelineStatus:null, durationMs:1258, _next:{ description, hints:[{path,method,price_usd,reason}] } }
quirks: The `asset` query param is OPTIONAL, not required (unlike most Cryptyx per-asset ops): the 402 bazaar schema lists required:[type,method] only, and the bare GET returned HTTP 200 with the full market-wide snapshot. Passing `asset=BTC` enriches the response with per-asset metric grades (perAssetMetrics + gradeContextNote) but is never required.

Numeric scores/confidences come back as strings in some fields (e.g. compositeScores[].score and recentSignals.bySignal[].avg_confidence are high-precision strings; avg_confidence is null when triggered_count is 0).
This is /api/v1/agent-context and it is the only namespace in the sweep (no /api/agent-context alias exists), so it is the canonical path to index.

Response carries a paid-endpoint `_next` block recommending sibling Cryptyx calls (signals/catalog $0.01, market-pulse/conviction $0.05, intelligence/query $0.25, asset/thesis $0.05, v1/ai/trade-ideas $0.10).
Live `pipelineStatus` was null on the verified call even though the 402 example showed it populated (lastRunDay/status/totalDurationMs/createdAt) — treat pipelineStatus as nullable.
usage.guide: Ground an agent on the whole crypto market in one $0.01 x402 GET before it reasons about assets. Call GET https://cryptyx.ai/api/v1/agent-context with no params and no body: you get factorBreadth (how many of ~200 assets are scored, across the 8 factor classes CORR/EFF/FLOW/FUT/OB/OPT/TR/VOL), compositeScores.topAssets / bottomAssets (the current best- and worst-ranked assets with each one's regime label + confidence), recentSignals (the day's total triggered count plus a per-signal_id breakdown of how many assets fired and the average confidence), platformCounts (total metrics/signals/classes live), pipelineStatus (last data-pipeline run, may be null), and a _next block suggesting cheap follow-up Cryptyx endpoints to drill in (signals/catalog, market-pulse/conviction, asset/thesis, intelligence/query). Add &asset=BTC to also get per-asset metric grades for that ticker. No API key; pays $0.01 USDC via x402 on Base.

name: Cryptyx Market Brief
description: Single-call crypto market grounding bundle for agents: today's composite-ranked top 10 and bottom 5 assets, every signal triggered today with per-signal trigger counts and confidence, a 30-day factor-breadth pulse across 8 factor classes, and a ready-to-drop plaintext brief — all in one $0.01 x402 GET, no input required.

inputSchema.note: No query params, no path params, no request body. Bare GET.

properties.asofDay: string (YYYY-MM-DD, data computed daily at UTC 00:00)

structured.pulse: [{class, positive_count, negative_count, neutral_count, total, avg_t_score, expand_share_pct, factor_state}]

properties._next: {description, hints:[{path, method, price_usd, reason}]} — recommended follow-up paid Cryptyx endpoints

usage.callShape: GET https://cryptyx.ai/api/v1/ai/market-brief with NO query params, NO path params, and NO request body. The full daily market bundle is returned synchronously in the 200 body. Pays a fixed $0.01 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453); no API key.
usage.outputShape: 200 JSON: { ok:true, asofDay:"YYYY-MM-DD", brief:"<plaintext LLM-ready brief>", structured:{ topAssets:[{asset,score,asof_day}] (10), bottomAssets:[{asset,score,asof_day}] (5), signals:[{signal_id,triggered_count,total_assets,avg_confidence,asof_day}] (143 rows), pulse:[{class,positive_count,negative_count,neutral_count,total,avg_t_score,expand_share_pct,factor_state}] (8 factor classes: CORR/EFF/FLOW/FUT/OB/OPT/TR/VOL), totalSignalTriggers:number }, durationMs:number, _next:{description, hints:[{path,method,price_usd,reason}]} }. Verified live 2026-07-30: asofDay 2026-07-29, 5509 total signal triggers, top asset KAITO (0.389), bottom DAI (-0.74).
quirks: No input at all — a bare GET returns the whole bundle. There are NO query/path params to vary; it is a single fixed daily snapshot, not per-asset.

Numeric fields are returned as STRINGS, not numbers: structured.topAssets/bottomAssets scores are high-precision strings (e.g. "0.38913392274327694589286"), signals.avg_confidence are strings (e.g. "0.3279"), and ALL pulse counts (positive_count/negative_count/neutral_count/total/avg_t_score/expand_share_pct) are strings. Cast before doing math.

Data is computed once daily at UTC 00:00, so asofDay is typically yesterday's date and the payload is identical across calls within the same UTC day — do not re-pay for the same day expecting fresh data.
The 'brief' string is a truncated/rounded human summary; the 'structured' object holds the full precise data (143 signals vs the ~few shown in the brief).

Response includes a '_next' block of recommended follow-up paid Cryptyx x402 endpoints (conviction, signals/top, factor-cross-section, asset/thesis, v1/ai/trade-ideas) with their prices — a cross-sell/navigation hint, not part of the market data.

OBSERVED FLAKINESS: during indexing the payment path returned a transient facilitator 502 and once an endpoint 500 (no charge, paid:false) before the same bare GET succeeded with a clean 200; the unpaid probe returned 402 consistently throughout. Retry on 5xx during settlement.
The provider also exposes the same OpenAPI at https://cryptyx.ai/openapi.json (the /api/openapi.json and /api/v1/openapi.json variants are auth-gated and return 401).
usage.guide: Use this as a one-shot crypto market grounding call to drop into an agent prompt. GET https://cryptyx.ai/api/v1/ai/market-brief with no params/body; pay the fixed $0.01 USDC over x402 on Base. You get: (1) a plaintext 'brief' ready to paste into an LLM context, and (2) a 'structured' object with the precise data — the day's composite-ranked top 10 and bottom 5 assets (with multi-factor scores), all 143 signals with how many of ~200 assets triggered each plus average confidence, and an 8-class factor 'pulse' (CORR, EFF, FLOW, FUT, OB, OPT, TR, VOL) summarizing 30-day breadth/expansion. All numeric values come back as strings; cast before computing. Data refreshes once daily at UTC 00:00 (asofDay), so don't re-pay within the same UTC day. For per-asset detail or ranked trade ideas, follow the _next hints (separate paid endpoints).

name: 2s Crypto Coin Profile
description: Full coin profile by CoinGecko id (e.g. bitcoin, ethereum, solana): price, market cap + rank, FDV, 24h volume, all-time high/low with dates, circulating/total/max supply, price changes (1h/24h/7d/30d/1y), categories, and official links (homepage, X, GitHub, subreddit).

inputSchema.id: CoinGecko coin id, e.g. bitcoin, ethereum, solana (string, 1-80 chars, required)

id.description: Input/filter query param (name from the provider's own example; added during baked-query remediation so it stays discoverable).

usage.callShape: GET https://2s.io/api/crypto/coin?id=<coingecko-id> -- x402 USDC on Base (eip155:8453) or Solana. Single required query param `id` (a CoinGecko coin id like bitcoin, ethereum, solana). No request body.
usage.outputShape: body.data.ok, body.data.items[0] {id,symbol,name,marketCapRank,categories[],priceUsd,marketCapUsd,fdvUsd,volume24hUsd,athUsd,athDate,atlUsd,atlDate,circulatingSupply,totalSupply,maxSupply,change1hPct,change24hPct,change7dPct,change30dPct,change1yPct,homepage,twitter,github,subreddit}, body.data.total, body.data.source {provider:'CoinGecko',url,license}; settlement at body.meta.settlement {txHash,network,success}
quirks: Result is nested under body.data.items[] (an array even for a single coin) — read items[0].
`id` is a query-string param, not a path segment, and must be a CoinGecko coin id (slug) not a ticker symbol — 'bitcoin' works, 'BTC' does not.
Data sourced from CoinGecko; attribution required ('Data by CoinGecko').
Richer than 2s crypto.token-price (spot only) and crypto.markets (list row).
usage.guide: Call GET https://2s.io/api/crypto/coin with a query parameter id set to a CoinGecko coin id (slug), e.g. ?id=bitcoin (also ethereum, solana). It is an x402 paid endpoint at ~$0.00144 USDC on Base (eip155:8453) or Solana; no request body. The response is synchronous JSON — read the coin profile from body.data.items[0] (price, market cap + rank, FDV, 24h volume, ATH/ATL with dates, supplies, price changes over 1h/24h/7d/30d/1y, categories, and official homepage/X/GitHub/subreddit links). Use a CoinGecko slug, not a ticker (bitcoin, not BTC). Data is CoinGecko-sourced (attribution required).

name: 2s DeFi Yields
description: DeFi yield and lending rates across protocols (DefiLlama-sourced) via 2s.io's x402 endpoint: pools ranked by APY or TVL with base vs reward APY, TVL, 1d/7d/30d APY trend, stablecoin flag, IL-risk and the DefiLlama pool UUID. Filter by chain, project (aave, compound, lido...), symbol (USDC, ETH...), minApy and minTvlUsd.

chain.description: Filter to a single chain (e.g. Base, Ethereum, BSC, Sonic).

project.description: Filter to a single protocol/project slug (e.g. aave, compound, lido, aerodrome-slipstream).

symbol.description: Filter to a pool token symbol (e.g. USDC, ETH, USDC-PROS).

sort.description: Field to rank results by: apy or tvl.

limit.description: Maximum number of pool rows to return (1-100).

usage.callShape: GET https://2s.io/api/crypto/defi-yields?sort={apy|tvl}&limit={1-100}&chain={CHAIN}&project={SLUG}&symbol={SYMBOL}&minApy={n}&minTvlUsd={n} (x402 paid, no request body). All params are optional query-string params. The endpoint returns HTTP 402 with x402 payment requirements on the first call, then HTTP 200 with the data once an EIP-3009 USDC authorization is signed. Pays ~$0.00144 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453) or Solana USDC.
usage.outputShape: JSON object: body.data.ok (bool), body.data.items[] each {project, symbol, chain, tvlUsd, apy, apyBase, apyReward, apyPct1D, apyPct7D, apyPct30D, stablecoin, ilRisk ('yes'/'no'), pool (DefiLlama pool UUID)}, body.data.total (count returned), body.data.source {provider:'DefiLlama', url, license}. Settlement/cost at body.meta {endpoint:'crypto.defi-yields', version, caller, cost{usd}, settlement{txHash, network, success}}. Verified live (limit=10, sort=apy): rank 1 zeebu/ZBU on BSC (tvlUsd 563976, apy 401569.85), then shadow-exchange-clmm WS-STS on Sonic, aerodrome-slipstream USDC-PROS on Base, ...; total 10; source DefiLlama.
quirks: Result rows are nested under body.data.items[] (an array) — read items[], not a top-level items; count is body.data.total.
All inputs are query-string params (?limit=10&sort=apy) — there is no request body and no path segment.
sort accepts only 'apy' or 'tvl' (default upstream ordering otherwise); limit range is 1-100.
apy/apyBase/apyReward are percentages (e.g. apy 401569.85 = 401569.85%); many raw DefiLlama pools have extreme/degenerate APYs, so use minTvlUsd and minApy filters to get investable pools.
ilRisk is a string ('yes'/'no'); apyBase/apyReward/trend fields can be null; pool is the DefiLlama pool UUID for cross-referencing.
Data is sourced from DefiLlama (body.data.source; license: 'DefiLlama open API (free). Attribution appreciated.') — attribute DefiLlama.
Provider offers a free trial: append ?trial=1 for one free real call per endpoint per hour (not used for the registry price).
Synchronous: data is inline in the 200 body; no polling.
usage.guide: Get DeFi yield/lending rates across protocols (DefiLlama data) from 2s.io. Call GET https://2s.io/api/crypto/defi-yields with optional query params: sort=apy|tvl to rank by APY or TVL, limit=1..100 to cap rows, and filters chain=<CHAIN> (e.g. Base, Ethereum, BSC), project=<slug> (aave, compound, lido, aerodrome-slipstream), symbol=<token> (USDC, ETH), minApy=<pct> and minTvlUsd=<usd> (e.g. ?limit=10&sort=apy). It is an x402 paid endpoint at ~$0.00144 USDC on Base (eip155:8453); Solana USDC is also accepted; no API key, no signup — the pay layer handles the 402. The response is synchronous JSON: read pools from body.data.items[], each with project, symbol, chain, tvlUsd, apy, apyBase, apyReward, apyPct1D/7D/30D, stablecoin, ilRisk, and pool (DefiLlama UUID); count at body.data.total. Because raw DefiLlama pools include extreme/degenerate APYs, filter with minTvlUsd and minApy for investable pools. Attribute data to DefiLlama.

name: 2s Hyperliquid Funding
description: Live Hyperliquid perpetual-futures funding rates, open interest, and mark/oracle/mid prices across 200+ perps. Each row carries hourly funding rate, open interest, mark/oracle/mid price, premium, prior-day price, 24h notional volume, and max leverage. Filter by coin; sort by open interest, volume, or funding. Onchain perp microstructure for funding-arb and OI signals.

coin.description: Filter to a single coin symbol (e.g. BTC, ETH, PUMP). Omit for all perps.

sort.description: Sort field: oi (open interest), volume (24h notional), or funding (hourly funding rate).

limit.description: Maximum number of perp rows to return (1-250).

usage.callShape: GET https://2s.io/api/crypto/hyperliquid-funding?sort={oi|volume|funding}&limit={1-250}&coin={SYMBOL} (x402 paid, no request body). All params are optional query-string params: coin (single-coin filter), sort (oi|volume|funding), limit (1-250).
usage.outputShape: body.data.items[] (array of perp rows). Each item: .coin (symbol, e.g. 'PUMP','kPEPE'), .maxLeverage, .fundingHourly (hourly funding rate, e.g. 0.0000125), .openInterest (in coin units), .markPx, .oraclePx, .midPx, .premium, .prevDayPx (prior-day price), .dayNotionalVolume (24h notional USD). body.data.ok, body.data.total (nullable), body.data.source{provider:'Hyperliquid',url,license}. Settlement/cost echoed at body.meta{endpoint,cost.usd,settlement{txHash,network,success}}.

name: Agentstools Bitcoin Block
description: One-call composite view of a Bitcoin block (by height or hash, or the chain tip) fused with current difficulty-adjustment context, a computed halving countdown, and a network hashrate snapshot.

height.description: Block height; omit height and hash for the chain tip

hash.description: Block hash (64 hex characters); alternative to height

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/btc/block with OPTIONAL query params: height (integer block height) OR hash (64-hex block hash); omit both to get the current chain tip. No request body. Pays $0.008 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453). Result is returned inline in the 200 body (synchronous, no poll).
usage.outputShape: block.{hash,height,timestamp,median_time,tx_count,size_bytes,weight,version,merkle_root,previous_block_hash,nonce,bits,difficulty,confirmations}; difficulty_adjustment.{progress_percent,difficulty_change_percent,estimated_retarget_date_ms,remaining_blocks,next_retarget_height}; halving.{halving_interval,current_era,current_block_subsidy_btc,next_halving_height,blocks_until_halving,estimated_seconds_until_halving,estimated_halving_date_unix}; hashrate.{current_hashrate_ehs,current_difficulty}; sources.{errors,partial,providers}; attribution[]; disclaimer.
quirks: All input is OPTIONAL query params (height OR hash); passing neither returns the current chain tip. There is no request body.
confirmations, difficulty_adjustment, halving countdown and hashrate are computed relative to the CURRENT tip at call time, so they change every block even for a fixed historical height.

Block reads use the Esplora schema (mempool.space primary, Blockstream Esplora fallback); network context (difficulty/halving/hashrate) comes from mempool.space extended API and degrades gracefully — sources.partial=true and sources.errors populate when a source is briefly unavailable.
Provider labels output as informational only, not financial advice; the halving countdown is computed by the provider from tip height, not proxied.
usage.guide: Look up Bitcoin block metadata plus fused network state in one paid call. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/btc/block?height=800000 (or ?hash=<64-hex>, or no params for the chain tip). Pays $0.008 USDC via x402 on Base. Returns the block (hash, height, timestamp, tx_count, size, weight, difficulty, confirmations, etc.), the current difficulty-adjustment period (progress percent, estimated change, remaining blocks, next retarget height), a computed halving countdown (era, current subsidy, next halving height, blocks/seconds until halving, estimated halving date), and a network hashrate snapshot (current_hashrate_ehs, current_difficulty). Verified live: height=800000 returned tx_count 3721, subsidy 3.125 BTC, era 4, ~898 EH/s.

name: Agentstools Crypto Signature Verify
description: Verify an EIP-191 personal_sign or EIP-712 typed-data signature and recover the signer address from public inputs (message + signature); optionally assert it matches an expected signer. Verification/recovery only — never signs.

message.description: Plain text / 0x-hex (eip191) OR a full typed-data object with types/domain/primaryType/message (eip712)

expected_signer.description: Optional address to compare the recovered signer against

usage.callShape: POST https://api.agentstools.dev/crypto/verify with a JSON body: scheme ('eip191'|'eip712', required), message (required — plain text or 0x-hex for eip191, OR a full typed-data object with types/domain/primaryType/message for eip712), signature (required — 0x 65-byte hex), expected_signer (optional address to compare against). Pays $0.003 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453). Result is returned inline in the 200 body (synchronous, no poll).
usage.outputShape: {scheme (echoes the requested scheme), signer (0x-checksummed recovered address), matches (boolean — true only when expected_signer is supplied AND equals the recovered signer)}
quirks: Verification/recovery ONLY — the service never signs and never holds a key; it just runs ecrecover on public inputs.
For eip191, `message` is a plain string / 0x-hex. For eip712, pass the FULL typed-data object (types/domain/primaryType/message) as `message` and set scheme:'eip712'.
`matches` reflects the expected_signer comparison; omit expected_signer and you still get the recovered `signer` but `matches` has no address to compare against.
signature must be a 0x-prefixed 65-byte hex string.
The live 402 self-identifies the service as 'crypto-verify' under the Agentstools host.
usage.guide: Verify an Ethereum signature and recover who signed it, in one paid call. POST https://api.agentstools.dev/crypto/verify with {scheme:'eip191'|'eip712', message, signature, expected_signer?}. For eip191 send the plain/0x-hex message; for eip712 send the full typed-data object as `message`. Pays $0.003 USDC via x402 on Base. Returns {scheme, signer (recovered address), matches (true iff expected_signer was given and equals the recovered signer)}. Verified live: eip191 message 'Hello, Ethereum!' recovered signer 0x19E7E376E7C213B7E7e7e46cc70A5dD086DAff2A with matches:true.

cached:true indicates a recently-cached result rather than a fresh chain read

name: Agentstools Stablecoin Peg
description: A focused, low-cost peg check for a single dollar token — returns current price, absolute deviation from the $1 peg, a coarse depeg status (stable / watch / depegged), and the collateral mechanism with a short note, sourced from DefiLlama Stablecoins open data.

symbol.description: Stablecoin ticker or DefiLlama id (e.g. USDT, USDC, DAI, 1)

address.description: Contract address (alternative to symbol)

chain.description: Chain for the address (used with address)

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/stablecoin/peg?symbol=<TICKER> — identify the token by symbol (ticker or DefiLlama id) OR by address (+optional chain). All params are query params; no request body. x402 v2 on Base USDC, $0.008. Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous, no poll).

quirks: Identify the token by symbol (ticker or DefiLlama id) OR by address (+chain); all are passed as query params on a GET — there is no request body.
depeg_status is a coarse DERIVED label — stable within a tight band, watch when drifting, depegged when deviation is large; the provider states it is a signal, not financial advice or an audit.

name: Agentstools Signature Safety
description: Pre-sign safety verdict for an off-chain EIP-712 signature (EIP-2612, Permit2, EIP-3009): decodes what it authorizes (spender, token, amount, deadline), checks domain-spoof, approval hygiene and a scam blocklist, and returns allow/warn/block plus a 0-100 risk score.

network.description: EVM network the signature is for (default base)

typed_data.description: Full EIP-712 typed-data object with domain, primaryType and message

signature.description: Optional 0x signature to recover the signer

expected_signer.description: Optional address to compare the recovered signer against

usage.callShape: POST https://api.agentstools.dev/tx/signature with a JSON body: required typed_data (the full EIP-712 typed-data object with domain, primaryType and message); optional network (base|ethereum|arbitrum|optimism|polygon|bnb, default base), signature (0x hex to recover the signer), expected_signer (address to compare against). No auth. Pays $0.02 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453). Verdict returned inline in the 200 body (synchronous, no poll).
usage.outputShape: kind:'signature'; network; chain_id; recognized(bool); authorizes.{standard,primary_type,spender,token,amount,unlimited(bool),deadline,nonce,owner,note}; domain.{verifyingContract,chainId,name}; flags.{unlimited_approval,no_expiry,unknown_spender}; scam_matches[]; risk_score(0-100); verdict('allow'|'warn'|'block'); reasons[]; signals[].{signal,severity,weight,reason}; attribution[]; disclaimer; ts.
quirks: typed_data is the only required field; it must be the full EIP-712 object (domain + primaryType + message). Passing an incomplete typed_data reduces what can be decoded.
Verdict is deterministic risk indicators, NOT advice or a guarantee — 'allow' is not an endorsement, 'block' is not proof of fraud. Off-chain signatures are decoded, not simulated end-to-end.
risk_score is a weighted sum of triggered signals (e.g. unlimited_approval weight 35, unknown_spender 20, no_expiry 12); verdict thresholds map score+flags to allow/warn/block.

The 402 header's bazaar output example shows verdict 'warn' (score 52) but a live paid call with the same body returned verdict 'block' (score 67) — the scoring/blocklist is updated over time, so treat the example as illustrative, not fixed.
Scam-blocklist attribution is MyEtherWallet ethereum-lists (MIT). Optional signature/expected_signer let it recover and compare the actual signer address.
usage.guide: Screen an off-chain EIP-712 signature before a wallet signs it. POST https://api.agentstools.dev/tx/signature with JSON {typed_data:<full EIP-712 object>, network?:'base', signature?, expected_signer?}. Pays $0.02 USDC via x402 on Base. Returns what the signature authorizes (standard, spender, token, amount, whether it's unlimited, deadline, nonce), risk flags (unlimited_approval, no_expiry, unknown_spender), a scam-blocklist match list, a 0-100 risk_score, an allow/warn/block verdict, and human-readable reasons+signals. Verified live: a Permit2 PermitSingle granting a max-uint allowance to an unknown spender with no expiry returned risk_score 67, verdict 'block', with 3 signals. Deterministic risk indicators, not advice.

usage.guide: Fetch a live onchain price from a Chainlink Ethereum-mainnet oracle feed. name: x402node Gas Compare
description: Return the live gas price across Base, Ethereum, Arbitrum, Optimism, Polygon and BSC sorted cheapest-first as JSON, so an agent can pick the cheapest chain to execute an operation right now.

format.description: Optional response format hint (query param). Not required; omit for the default JSON ranking.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.x402node.dev/chain/gas-compare with no body and no required params (an optional ?format= hint is accepted). Pay the fixed $0.005 x402 quote (USDC on Base or Solana, no API key) and retry with the payment header.
usage.outputShape: Synchronous JSON object (from the paid 200): { timestamp: ISO-8601 string, cheapest: chain name of the lowest-gas chain (e.g. 'optimism'), chains: array of { chain: string, gasPriceGwei: number } sorted cheapest-first across optimism/base/arbitrum/bsc/ethereum (Polygon also covered per the docs), note: caveat string (L2 gas excludes L1 data fee; real cost also depends on per-chain token price), source: 'multi-rpc', _hint: provider promo string }.
quirks: Zero-param GET — send no body and no query params (only an optional ?format= hint exists); the documented example input is {}.
Returns ONE cross-chain ranking sorted cheapest-first — distinct from x402node's single-chain /chain/gas-oracle (fee tiers) and from the /chain/chainlink-price onchain feed reader.

The `note` field warns that L2 gasPriceGwei excludes the L1 data fee and that true execution cost also depends on each chain's native token price, so gasPriceGwei alone is not the full USD cost (use /chain/gas-estimate for USD cost).
Fixed price ($0.005 in OpenAPI x-payment-info, matching the 5000-atomic live 402 accept) — not a dynamic quote.
Response includes a promotional _hint field that can be ignored.
Live 402 advertised both a Base USDC accept and a Solana USDC accept (both recorded); the paid call was settled on Base ($0.005).
usage.guide: Find the cheapest EVM chain to transact on right now. Issue a plain GET to https://api.x402node.dev/finance/crypto with a symbol query param (symbol=BTC, or symbols=BTC,ETH,SOL to batch) or a CoinGecko id (id=bitcoin), plus an optional vs quote currency (vs=usd default), no body, and pay the x402 quote (~$0.004 USDC on Base or Solana, no API key). On the 200, read `data` — a map keyed by CoinGecko id where each entry carries `<vs>` (spot price, number), `<vs>_market_cap`, `<vs>_24h_vol`, `<vs>_24h_change` (percent) and `last_updated_at` (unix seconds); `ids` and `vs_currencies` echo what resolved and `count` is how many tokens returned. Synchronous — no polling.

name: x402node Order Book Snapshot
description: Return a live perpetual-futures order-book snapshot for a coin (built from OKX top-of-book depth) as JSON: best bid/ask, mid, spread and spread in bps, bid/ask depth, bid-ask imbalance and a near-term pressure read for momentum and execution decisions.

symbol.description: Coin symbol for the perpetual, e.g. BTC (query param, optional; default BTC).

usage.callShape: GET https://api.x402node.dev/market/orderbook with an optional ?symbol= query param (default BTC). No body. Pay the fixed $0.012 x402 quote (USDC on Base or Solana, no API key) and retry with the payment header.
usage.outputShape: Synchronous JSON object (from the paid 200): { symbol:'BTC', bestBid: number, bestAsk: number, mid: number, spread: number, spreadBps: number, bidDepth: number, askDepth: number, bidAskImbalance: number (0-1, share of top-of-book size on the bid), pressure: string (e.g. 'ask-heavy (sell pressure)'), note: string, source:'okx', _hint: provider promo string }.
quirks: symbol is an optional query param; omit it for BTC by default. Value is a coin symbol (e.g. BTC, ETH, SOL) — the OKX perpetual is resolved server-side.
Built from OKX top-of-book (top-50-level) market depth — a perpetual-futures order book, not spot.
Fixed price ($0.012 in the openapi x-payment-info, matching the 12000-atomic live 402 accept) — not a dynamic quote.
bidAskImbalance is a 0-1 ratio; pressure is a derived human-readable label (bid-heavy / ask-heavy) for near-term direction.
Response includes a promotional _hint field that can be ignored.

Live 402 advertised both a Base USDC accept and a Solana USDC accept (both recorded, both 12000 atomic = $0.012); the payment was settled on Base (paid HTTP 200, costUsd 0.012, tx 0xa122849f3f2c89b401a74e53ff67c7ec152390cd06e74e5bbf150baaddf50ecf).
usage.guide: Get a live perpetual order-book snapshot for a coin so an agent can gauge liquidity, spread and near-term pressure before trading. Issue a plain GET to https://api.x402node.dev/market/orderbook, optionally with ?symbol=BTC (default), ETH, SOL, etc., with no body, and pay the x402 quote (~$0.012 USDC on Base or Solana, no API key). On the 200, read the flat JSON: `bestBid`/`bestAsk` are top-of-book prices, `mid` the midpoint, `spread`/`spreadBps` the absolute and basis-point spread, `bidDepth`/`askDepth` the top-of-book size on each side, and `bidAskImbalance` (0-1) plus `pressure` (a bid-heavy / ask-heavy label) signal near-term direction. Data is from OKX. Synchronous — no polling.

name: Agentstools Crypto News
description: Aggregated crypto news with sentiment: deduplicated headlines from major crypto outlets (CoinDesk, Cointelegraph, Decrypt, Bitcoin Magazine, The Block, CryptoSlate), each scored bullish/bearish/neutral by a crypto-tuned lexicon, optionally filtered by coin or free-text query.

coin.description: Input/filter query param (name from the provider's own example; added during baked-query remediation so it stays discoverable).

limit.description: Input/filter query param (name from the provider's own example; added during baked-query remediation so it stays discoverable).

backends.outputSchema: {coin, query, count, items[]:{title, link, source, published, summary, sentiment:{label, score}}, summary:{sources_ok, sources_failed, total_fetched, after_dedup, sentiment:{label, score, items_scored, breakdown:{bullish,bearish,neutral}}, errors[]}, attribution}

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/crypto/news with OPTIONAL query params: coin (ticker or name), query (free-text filter), limit (1-30, default 20). No request body. x402 v2 on Base USDC (eip155:8453), $0.005. Result inline in the 200 body (synchronous, no poll).
usage.outputShape: {coin, query, count, items:[{title, link, source, published, summary, sentiment:{label:'bullish'|'bearish'|'neutral', score}}], summary:{sources_ok, sources_failed, total_fetched, after_dedup, sentiment:{label, score, items_scored, breakdown:{bullish, bearish, neutral}}, errors:[{source, error}]}, attribution}
usage.quirks: Metadata only — each item carries title/link-back/source/published time/short feed-summary plus sentiment; full articles stay at the publisher's link. Source feeds are fixed server-side (no SSRF surface). A failed feed is skipped, not a 500; total upstream failure -> 502; empty filter result -> 422; bad input -> 400. Verified live: coin=BTC&limit=15 returned 15 items (5 bullish/6 bearish/4 neutral, aggregate bearish -0.0855) from CoinDesk + Cointelegraph, with CryptoSlate's feed skipped (HTTP 403).
usage.guide: One-call crypto news radar with built-in sentiment for trading/research agents. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/crypto/news?coin=BTC&limit=15 (all params optional: coin filters by ticker/name, query is a free-text filter on headline+summary, limit is 1-30 default 20). No body. Pays $0.005 USDC via x402 on Base. Returns deduplicated recent headlines from major crypto outlets (CoinDesk, Cointelegraph, Decrypt, Bitcoin Magazine, The Block, CryptoSlate) each scored bullish/bearish/neutral, plus an aggregate sentiment breakdown and per-feed error report. Verified live: coin=BTC&limit=15 -> 15 headlines, aggregate sentiment bearish (-0.0855).

name: Agentstools Crypto Sentiment
description: Composite crypto market sentiment for trading/risk agents — the alternative.me Crypto Fear & Greed index (value, classification, trend) blended with aggregated crypto news-headline sentiment into a single bullish/bearish/neutral score, optionally focused on a coin or free-text query.

coin.description: Focus the news-sentiment component on a coin by ticker or name (BTC, ETH, ...); the Fear & Greed component is always market-wide. Optional.

query.description: Free-text filter for the news-sentiment component. Optional.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/crypto/sentiment with OPTIONAL query params: coin (ticker or name, e.g. ETH — focuses the news component; F&G is market-wide) and/or query (free-text news filter). No request body. Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous). Pays $0.003 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.
usage.outputShape: JSON object: coin, query, composite {label (bullish|bearish|neutral), score [-1,1]}, fear_greed {value 0-100, classification, trend (rising|falling|flat), window_points, history[] each {value, classification, timestamp (unix seconds string)}}, news_sentiment {label, score, items_scored, breakdown {bullish, bearish, neutral}}, sources {fear_greed (bool), news_feeds_ok (int), errors[] each {source, error}}, attribution. Verified paid response (coin=ETH): composite {label 'bearish', score -0.2857}, fear_greed {value 29, classification 'Fear', trend 'flat', 14 history points}, news_sentiment {label 'bearish', score -0.1514, items_scored 3, breakdown {bullish 1, bearish 2, neutral 0}}, sources {fear_greed true, news_feeds_ok 5, errors [{source 'CryptoSlate', error 'feed returned HTTP 403'}]}, attribution 'Data by alternative.me'.
quirks: Params go in the QUERY STRING, not a body — this is a GET; both coin and query are optional (omit both for a purely market-wide read).
The Fear & Greed component is always market-wide; coin/query only narrow the news-headline sentiment component.

Each source is best-effort: a down feed is reported under sources.errors and the composite is computed from what remains (observed live: CryptoSlate feed returned HTTP 403 yet the call still succeeded); only a total failure of every source is a 502, and bad input is a 400.
Fear & Greed data is attributed to alternative.me per its terms (response carries attribution 'Data by alternative.me'); scores are market signals, not investment advice.
402 body is empty ({}) — the x402 challenge (accepts + bazaar input/output schema) is carried in the base64 `payment-required` response header, not the body.
Bazaar input schema lists methods GET/HEAD/DELETE, but this is a read op — use GET.
usage.guide: Get a single composite read on crypto market mood with one keyless x402 call. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/crypto/sentiment with OPTIONAL query params: coin (ticker or name, e.g. ETH, to focus the news component) and/or query (free-text news filter); omit both for a market-wide read. Synchronous — the 200 body carries composite {label bullish/bearish/neutral, score in [-1,1]}, fear_greed {value 0-100, classification, trend rising/falling/flat, history[]}, news_sentiment {label, score, items_scored, breakdown}, sources {fear_greed, news_feeds_ok, errors[]}, and attribution. The Fear & Greed index (from alternative.me) is market-wide; coin/query only narrow the news-headline sentiment. Pays $0.003 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453). Example: {coin:'ETH'} returned composite bearish -0.29 with F&G value 29 ('Fear', flat).

name: Agentstools RWA Category
description: Market-intelligence aggregate over a normalized tokenized real-world-asset (RWA) sub-category: total TVL, top products ranked with their TVL share, issuer concentration and the leading product's growth trend; called without a category it returns a market-wide roll-up of every sub-category. Sourced from DefiLlama.

category.description: Normalized RWA sub-category (query param); omit for a market-wide roll-up of every sub-category.

windows.description: 7d/30d/90d objects, each with abs_change and pct_change

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/rwa/category?category=<sub-category> — single optional query param `category` (enum tokenized-treasury|private-credit|tokenized-fund|commodity|real-estate|tokenized-equity|tokenized-rwa). Omit the param entirely for a market-wide roll-up of every sub-category. No request body, no API key. First call returns HTTP 402 with an x402 challenge (USDC on Base eip155:8453); settling it returns HTTP 200 with the aggregate inline.
usage.outputShape: JSON: category, sub_category, sub_category_note, product_count (19), total_tvl (~1.39e10), top_products[] each {slug, name, issuer, backing_type, tvl, tvl_share} (ranked by TVL — e.g. BlackRock BUIDL 25.3% share, Circle USYC 21.6%, Ondo Yield Assets 18.1%), issuer_concentration {distinct_issuers (13), top_issuer ('BlackRock'), top_issuer_tvl_share (0.2529)}, leader_growth_trend {latest_tvl, windows{7d,30d,90d each abs_change & pct_change}}, provenance {source:'defillama', dataset:'protocols (RWA categories)'}, attribution[], disclaimer. Observed on a verified 200.
quirks: `category` is a QUERY param, not a body field, and is optional — omitting it returns a market-wide roll-up of every sub-category's TVL and product count instead of a single-category aggregate.
Fixed price $0.01 (amount 10000, USDC 6 decimals on Base); not dynamic.
402 challenge is delivered in the `payment-required` response HEADER (base64 x402 v2), not the body — the 402 body is an empty {}.
Data is a DERIVED aggregate over DefiLlama open data (RWA / RWA Lending / Treasury Manager categories); response carries an explicit not-financial-advice disclaimer.
Distinct from /rwa/list (product catalog) and /rwa/product (single-product due-diligence profile) — same host, different operations, not aliases.
An upstream data-source failure returns 502, never a 500.
usage.guide: Get a market lens over a tokenized real-world-asset sub-category. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/rwa/category?category=tokenized-treasury (enum tokenized-treasury|private-credit|tokenized-fund|commodity|real-estate|tokenized-equity|tokenized-rwa; omit for a market-wide roll-up). Pay $0.01 USDC via x402 on Base — no API key or account. Returns the summed TVL for the class, the top products ranked with each one's share of category TVL, an issuer-concentration read (largest issuer + its share across N distinct issuers), and the leading product's 7/30/90-day growth trend as a momentum proxy — all sourced from DefiLlama. Use /rwa/list first to resolve a product name to a slug, /rwa/product for a single product's full profile. Verified live 2026-08-07 with category='tokenized-treasury' → HTTP 200, $0.01 charged, product_count 19, total_tvl ~$13.9B, top issuer BlackRock (25.3% share).

name: Agentstools RWA List
description: Catalog of tokenized real-world-asset (RWA) products ranked by total value locked, drawn from DefiLlama's RWA, RWA Lending and Treasury Manager universe (~180 products). Each row carries the DefiLlama slug (join key for the other RWA routes), name, symbol, normalized sub-category, backing type, resolved issuer, DefiLlama category, TVL and the chains it lives on. Optionally filter by sub-category, chain or issuer.

chain.description: Filter to products present on this chain, such as Ethereum

issuer.description: Filter by issuer name, such as BlackRock or Ondo

limit.description: Max rows to return (ranked by TVL)

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/rwa/list with optional query params ?category=<enum>&chain=<name>&issuer=<name>&limit=<1-300>. No body. All params optional (unfiltered returns the whole ~180-product universe ranked by TVL). x402 v2 on Base USDC, $0.005. Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous).
usage.outputShape: count (int, rows returned), total_matched (int, total after filters), filters (object echoing category/chain/issuer), products[] (each: slug — the join key used by rwa/product, rwa/yield, rwa/category; name; symbol (string|null); sub_category; backing_type; issuer; defillama_category; tvl (number, USD); chains[] (string[])), provenance (object), attribution (string[]), disclaimer (string). Products are ranked by TVL, largest first.
quirks: All query params are OPTIONAL; with none supplied it returns the full RWA universe (~180 products) ranked by TVL
category is a fixed enum: tokenized-treasury, private-credit, tokenized-fund, commodity, real-estate, tokenized-equity, tokenized-rwa
402 is x402 v2: the response BODY is empty ({}) and the quote (accepts) lives in the base64-encoded payment-required response HEADER
This is the cheap first step that resolves a name/issuer/symbol to the DefiLlama slug the other RWA routes (product, yield, category) consume
symbol may be null for products without a published token symbol
Data is derived from DefiLlama open data (source: defillama, dataset: protocols RWA categories); response carries an explicit not-financial-advice disclaimer; upstream failure returns 502, never 500
usage.guide: List tokenized real-world-asset (RWA) products ranked by TVL from DefiLlama. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/rwa/list with optional query params: category (enum: tokenized-treasury | private-credit | tokenized-fund | commodity | real-estate | tokenized-equity | tokenized-rwa), chain (e.g. Ethereum), issuer (e.g. BlackRock, Ondo), limit (1-300, default returns all). No body. x402 v2 on Base USDC, $0.005 per call; synchronous — the 200 body carries {count, total_matched, filters, products[], provenance, attribution, disclaimer}. Each product has slug (the join key for the sibling rwa/product, rwa/yield and rwa/category routes), name, symbol, sub_category, backing_type, issuer, defillama_category, tvl and chains[]. Use this cheap first step to resolve a name to a slug, then call rwa/product for a full profile.

name: Agentstools RWA Product Profile
description: Full due-diligence profile for a tokenized real-world-asset product — resolved by DefiLlama slug, token symbol, or issuer+name — fusing identity/issuer, normalized sub-category and backing type, on-chain TVL with per-chain distribution, 7/30/90-day TVL growth trend, pool-level yield/APY, and an independent on-chain ERC-20 totalSupply cross-check, cited to DefiLlama open data.

slug.description: DefiLlama product slug, such as blackrock-buidl

symbol.description: Token symbol, such as BUIDL or PAXG (alternative to slug)

issuer.description: Issuer name, paired with name (alternative to slug)

chain.description: Chain to prefer for the on-chain cross-check

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/rwa/product?slug=<SLUG> — identify the product by slug (DefiLlama slug) OR symbol (token ticker) OR issuer+name; optional chain to prefer for the on-chain cross-check. All params are query params; no request body. Pays $0.02 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453). Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous, no poll).
usage.outputShape: identity{slug,name,symbol,issuer,description,url,curated}, classification{sub_category,backing_type,sub_category_note,defillama_category}, tvl{total,per_chain{chain->usd},chains[]}, growth_trend{latest_tvl,windows{7d,30d,90d each with abs_change & pct_change}}, yield{available,pool_count,avg_apy,total_pool_tvl_usd,pools[{pool,project,symbol,chain,tvlUsd,apy,apyBase,apyReward,apyMean30d,apyPct30D}],attribution}, onchain_verification{available,token_symbol,chain,network,address,onchain_total_supply,onchain_total_supply_raw,onchain_symbol,decimals,attribution}, contracts[{chain,network,address}], citations[], disclaimer.
quirks: Identify the product by slug OR symbol OR issuer+name (all query params on a GET); no request body. slug is the join key returned by the sibling /rwa/list route.
yield.available is false (no invented figure) when the product has no tracked DefiLlama yield pools; onchain_verification.available is false for a product without a curated on-chain contract.

All figures are DERIVED signals over public DefiLlama open data plus a public-RPC ERC-20 totalSupply read — explicitly not financial advice, not an audit. Unknown product returns 404, an upstream failure 502 (never 500).

Verified live: slug=blackrock-buidl returned issuer BlackRock, sub_category tokenized-treasury, backing us-treasuries, TVL ~$3.51B across 8 chains, 30d growth +15.09%, yield avg_apy ~3.44% over 9 pools, on-chain BUIDL totalSupply ~224.9M (Ethereum, 6 decimals).
usage.guide: Read the full due-diligence profile for a tokenized real-world asset before comparing or holding it. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/rwa/product?slug=<SLUG> (or ?symbol=<TICKER>, or ?issuer=<X>&name=<Y>; optional &chain=<C>). No body. Pays $0.02 USDC via x402 on Base. Returns one fused object: identity (issuer, symbol, description, product URL), classification (normalized sub-category + backing type with a note), TVL with per-chain distribution, a 7/30/90-day TVL growth trend, pool-level yield/APY with a TVL-weighted average, and an independent on-chain ERC-20 totalSupply cross-check — each facet cited to DefiLlama open data or a public RPC. Resolve a name to its slug first via the cheaper /rwa/list route. Verified live: blackrock-buidl -> BlackRock BUIDL, tokenized-treasury, TVL ~$3.51B, 30d +15.09%, avg APY ~3.44%.

name: Agentstools Address Screen
description: Check whether a crypto wallet address appears on the official public sanctions lists (OFAC SDN, UK, EU, UN) via a deterministic exact lookup, returning the matched record (list, program, entity name, reference, currency).

address.description: Crypto address to screen (any chain).

chain.description: Optional currency symbol to restrict the match (e.g. ETH, XBT, TRX, USDT, SOL).

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/screen/address?address=<crypto address>&chain=<optional currency symbol>. Required query param: address. No body. x402 v2 on Base USDC, $0.003. Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous).
usage.outputShape: listed (bool — true if any sanctions hit), query (string echo of the address), chain (string echo), match_count (int), matches[] (each: list e.g. OFAC/UK/EU/UN, ref (list reference id), name (entity name), type e.g. entity/individual, programs[] (sanctions programs), country (string|null), matched_address, currency, match_type e.g. exact), disclaimer (string)
quirks: address is REQUIRED and passed as a query param on a GET (no body); omitting it 4xx
chain is OPTIONAL — a currency symbol (ETH, XBT, TRX, USDT, SOL, ...) that restricts the match to that chain/currency; omit to screen across all
Deterministic EXACT lookup on the address, not a fuzzy/name match — the address must be literally present on a list (OFAC SDN, UK, EU, UN)
listed:true with match_count>0 means a hit; the same address can appear on multiple lists (paid probe returned both OFAC and UK matches for GARANTEX EUROPE OU)
Output is informational screening against public sanctions lists, not legal advice (see disclaimer) — verify against official sources before any decision
For name-based entity/person screening use the sibling /screen/entity (fuzzy name match) instead
usage.guide: Check whether a crypto wallet address appears on the official public sanctions lists (OFAC SDN, UK, EU, UN) via a deterministic exact address lookup. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/screen/address?address=<crypto address> (required); optionally add &chain=<currency symbol> (ETH, XBT, TRX, USDT, SOL, ...) to restrict the match to one chain. No body. x402 v2 on Base USDC, $0.003, no API key — pay the 402 quote and re-request; the result is inline in the synchronous 200 body. Read listed (bool) and match_count, then matches[] (list, ref, name, type, programs[], country, matched_address, currency, match_type) for each hit. Treat any match as review-required, not a decision (informational, not legal advice). For name-based person/org screening use /screen/entity instead.

name: Agentstools Token Risk
description: Composite rug-check risk score for an ERC-20 token: a 0-100 score, a category (low/medium/high/critical), per-dimension flags, reasons and weighted signals, scored deterministically across six dimensions — contract integrity, ownership, holder concentration, liquidity, honeypot and age. Multi-chain EVM.

token.description: ERC-20 token contract address (0x-prefixed, 40 hex chars)

network.description: EVM network the token lives on (default base)

dimensions.description: Per-dimension detail: contract_integrity, ownership, holder_concentration, liquidity, honeypot, age (each with a status and dimension-specific fields + flags)

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/token/risk?token=<0x-ERC20-address>&network=<base|ethereum|arbitrum|optimism|polygon> (token REQUIRED query param; network optional, default base). No body. x402 v2 on Base USDC, $0.02. Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous).
usage.outputShape: token (echo), network (echo), chain (CAIP-2, e.g. eip155:8453), risk_score (int 0-100), risk_category (low/medium/high/critical), reasons[] (plain-English strings), signals[] ({signal, dimension, severity, weight, reason}), raw_weight_sum (int), dimensions{contract_integrity, ownership, holder_concentration, liquidity, honeypot, age} (each a status + dimension-specific fields + flags; status can be 'ok' or 'unavailable' with a reason), coverage{dimensions_total, dimensions_evaluated, evaluated[], confidence}, attribution (string), disclaimer (string), ts (Unix seconds), cached (bool)
quirks: token is REQUIRED and passed as a query param on a GET (no body); network is optional and defaults to base
network enum: base, ethereum, arbitrum, optimism, polygon (multi-chain EVM)
risk_score is a weighted sum of matched signals (raw_weight_sum); higher = riskier; risk_category buckets it into low/medium/high/critical

Not all six dimensions always evaluate — liquidity and honeypot report status:'unavailable' when a token has no tracked Base pool; coverage.confidence (e.g. 0.67) reflects how many of the 6 dimensions were scored
Contract/holder/age data via Blockscout; on-chain reads (ownership, code, liquidity, swaps) computed by the provider
Automated on-chain risk indicators, not financial advice — a low score is not an endorsement and a high score is not proof of fraud
The score can vary between the 402 example (58) and a live call (46) as chain state / coverage changes
usage.guide: Composite rug-pull/honeypot risk score for an ERC-20 token, scored deterministically across six dimensions (contract integrity, ownership, holder concentration, liquidity, honeypot, age). GET https://api.agentstools.dev/token/risk?token=<0x-address>&network=<base|ethereum|arbitrum|optimism|polygon> (token required; network defaults to base). No body. x402 v2 on Base USDC, $0.02. Synchronous — the 200 body carries {risk_score (0-100), risk_category, reasons[], signals[], dimensions{...}, coverage{...}, ts, cached}. Use coverage.confidence to judge how complete the assessment is; treat it as an automated risk indicator, not financial advice.

name: Agentstools Raw Transaction Safety
description: Pre-sign safety verdict for a raw EVM transaction ({to,data,value}): decodes the calldata selector into a human-readable function + args, surfaces known-pattern effects (approval delta, transfer target, setApprovalForAll), dry-runs eth_call for revert, checks a scam blocklist, and returns allow/warn/block plus a 0-100 risk score.

network.description: EVM network the transaction is for (default base)

usage.callShape: POST https://api.agentstools.dev/tx/raw with a JSON body: required to (destination contract address); optional data (0x-prefixed calldata hex), network (base|ethereum|arbitrum|optimism|polygon|bnb, default base), from (sender address — enables allowance-delta read), value (native value in wei), simulate (bool, dry-run eth_call for revert, default true). No auth. Pays $0.02 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453). Verdict returned inline in the 200 body (synchronous, no poll).
usage.outputShape: kind:'raw'; network; chain_id; to; from; value; decoded.{selector,function,signature,semantic,verified(bool),args:{...}}; effects.{type,spender,token,new_allowance,unlimited}; execution.{reverts(bool|null),note}; flags.{unlimited_approval,unknown_spender}; scam_matches[]; risk_score(0-100); verdict('allow'|'warn'|'block'); reasons[]; signals[].{signal,severity,weight,reason}; attribution[]; disclaimer; ts.
quirks: 'to' is the ONLY required field; without 'data' it can only assess the target, not the calldata. Supply the 0x calldata hex to get a decoded function + effects + verdict.

This is decode + approval-hygiene + known-pattern effects + scam-match, NOT a full trace-based generic asset-diff — public RPCs often lack tracing, so execution.reverts is an eth_call dry-run only (can be null) and there is no exhaustive balance-change simulation.
Passing 'from' enables an allowance-delta read (current vs new allowance) for approval calldata; omit it and only the new_allowance is shown.

Verdict is deterministic risk indicators, NOT advice — 'allow' is not an endorsement, 'block' is not proof of fraud. risk_score is a weighted sum of triggered signals (unlimited_approval weight 35, unknown_spender 20).

The 402 header's bazaar example showed risk_score 40 / verdict 'warn', but the live paid call with the same body returned risk_score 55 / verdict 'warn' — the scoring/blocklist is updated over time, so treat the example score as illustrative.
Scam-blocklist attribution is MyEtherWallet ethereum-lists (MIT). Bad input returns 4xx.
usage.guide: Screen a raw EVM transaction before a wallet signs it. POST https://api.agentstools.dev/tx/raw with JSON {to:<contract>, data?:<0x calldata>, network?:'base', from?, value?, simulate?}. Pays $0.02 USDC via x402 on Base. Decodes the calldata selector against a known-signature registry (approve, increaseAllowance, transfer, transferFrom, setApprovalForAll, EIP-2612 permit, Permit2 approve, NFT safeTransferFrom, etc.) into a human-readable function + args + a plain-English semantic, surfaces known-pattern effects (approval spender/token/new_allowance/unlimited, transfer recipient/amount, full-collection operator control), optionally dry-runs an eth_call for revert, matches the target and decoded spender against public scam blocklists, and returns risk flags, a 0-100 risk_score, an allow/warn/block verdict, and cited reasons+signals. Verified live: an unlimited (max-uint) ERC-20 approve to an unknown spender on Base USDC decoded to function 'approve', effects.type 'approval' unlimited:true, flags unlimited_approval+unknown_spender, risk_score 55, verdict 'warn', with 2 signals. Multi-chain EVM only. Deterministic risk indicators, not advice.

name: Agentstools Address Code
description: Determine whether an EVM address is a contract or an EOA in one paid call: returns is_contract, the deployed bytecode size in bytes and the keccak256 code hash (eth_getCode) on Base, Ethereum, Arbitrum, Optimism, Polygon or BNB.

address.description: EVM address (0x-prefixed) to inspect.

network.description: EVM network to read from (default base).

code_size.description: Deployed bytecode size in bytes (0 for an EOA).

code_hash.description: keccak256 hash of the deployed code.

chain.description: CAIP-2 chain id, e.g. eip155:8453.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/code?address=<0x EVM address>&network=<base|ethereum|arbitrum|optimism|polygon|bnb> (address REQUIRED query param; network optional, default base). No body. x402 v2 on Base USDC (eip155:8453), $0.003. Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous, no poll).
usage.outputShape: address (echo), is_contract (bool — true if the address has deployed bytecode), code_size (int — deployed bytecode length in bytes, 0 for an EOA), code_hash (0x keccak256 hash of the code), network (echo), chain (CAIP-2 chain id, e.g. eip155:8453), ts (Unix seconds), cached (bool)
quirks: address is REQUIRED and passed as a query param on a GET (no body); network is optional and defaults to base
network enum: base, ethereum, arbitrum, optimism, polygon, bnb (multi-chain EVM)

is_contract is derived from eth_getCode: an address with non-empty deployed bytecode is a contract; code_size 0 / is_contract false means an EOA (or a contract not yet deployed / self-destructed on this chain)
code_hash is the keccak256 of the deployed bytecode — useful to fingerprint/compare identical contract deployments
A contract that only exists on one chain will read as an EOA on the others — pick the right network
Result is returned inline in the synchronous 200 (no polling)
usage.guide: Check whether an EVM address is a smart contract or a plain wallet (EOA) in one keyless paid call. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/code?address=<0x address> (required); optionally add &network=<base|ethereum|arbitrum|optimism|polygon|bnb> (default base). No body. Pays $0.003 USDC via x402 v2 on Base — pay the 402 quote and re-request; the result is inline in the synchronous 200. Read is_contract (bool) for the go/no-go, code_size (deployed bytecode length in bytes, 0 for an EOA) and code_hash (keccak256 of the code, to fingerprint a deployment). Verified live 2026-08-07: the documented USDC-on-Base address returned is_contract:true, code_size:1852, chain eip155:8453.

name: Agentstools Crypto Convert
description: Exact-math on-chain conversion utility: convert token units (wei/gwei/ether or arbitrary decimals), convert between hex and int, and compute/validate an EIP-55 checksummed address.

op.description: Input/filter query param (name from the provider's own example; added during baked-query remediation so it stays discoverable).

value.description: Input/filter query param (name from the provider's own example; added during baked-query remediation so it stays discoverable).

from.description: Input/filter query param (name from the provider's own example; added during baked-query remediation so it stays discoverable).

to.description: Input/filter query param (name from the provider's own example; added during baked-query remediation so it stays discoverable).

backends.outputSchema: op=units -> {value (converted amount as exact string), from, to}. op=hex -> converted value between hex and int. op=checksum -> EIP-55 checksummed address plus a validity flag. All exact integer/Decimal math, no float precision loss.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/crypto/convert with query params. Required: op (units|checksum|hex). For op=units: value, from, to (units among wei|gwei|ether or an integer decimals count). For op=hex: value (int or 0x hex), from/to (int|hex). For op=checksum: address. No request body. x402 v2 on Base USDC (eip155:8453), $0.001. Result inline in the 200 body (synchronous, no poll).
usage.outputShape: {value, from, to} for op=units. Verified live: op=units&value=1.5&from=ether&to=gwei -> {"value":"1500000000","from":"ether","to":"gwei"}. op=hex converts between hex and int; op=checksum returns the EIP-55 checksummed address plus a validity flag.
usage.quirks: One multiplexed endpoint with an op selector (units|checksum|hex). op is the only always-required param; the other params depend on op (value/from/to for units and hex, address for checksum). Pure local computation with exact integer/Decimal math — no network calls, no float precision loss. Verified live: 1.5 ether -> 1500000000 gwei.
usage.guide: Deterministic on-chain conversion helper for agents. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/crypto/convert?op=<units|checksum|hex>&... . op=units converts an amount between wei/gwei/ether or any integer `decimals` (arbitrary token) — pass value, from, to (e.g. op=units&value=1.5&from=ether&to=gwei -> 1500000000). op=hex converts a value between hex and int (value + from/to = int|hex). op=checksum returns the EIP-55 checksummed form of an address plus a validity flag (pass address). No body, no API key. Pays $0.001 USDC via x402 on Base. All math is exact (integer/Decimal), no float precision loss. Verified live: op=units&value=1.5&from=ether&to=gwei returned {"value":"1500000000","from":"ether","to":"gwei"}.

name: Agentstools DePIN Coverage
description: Coverage density and deployment-opportunity intelligence for a geography on a DePIN wireless network (Helium): geocodes the geo to an H3 cell, counts the Helium IoT and Mobile hotspots asserted within it, and returns hotspot density per km2 plus a coverage rating and a deployment-opportunity signal, sourced from Relay Wireless.

geo.description: A city, state, country string (e.g. 'Austin, Texas') or an H3 cell — the geography to assess. Query param. Required.

network.description: DePIN network id. Query param; defaults to helium.

hotspots.description: Per-subnetwork counts: iot and mobile, each { count, available, provenance{source,ref,network,as_of} }.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/depin/coverage?geo=<city, state, country or H3 cell>&network=helium — `geo` is a required query param; `network` is optional (enum: helium; defaults to helium). No request body, no API key. First call returns HTTP 402 with an x402 challenge (USDC on Base eip155:8453); settling it returns HTTP 200 with the coverage report inline.
usage.outputShape: JSON: network, geo (echoed), available (bool), resolution_mode ('geocoded'), h3_cell, h3_resolution (5), centroid{lat,lon}, area_km2 (252.9), hotspots{iot{count,available,provenance{source,ref,network,as_of}}, mobile{...}}, total_hotspots (418), density_per_km2 (1.65), rating ('dense'), opportunity ('low'), note, attribution[] (OpenStreetMap geocoding + Relay Wireless source), disclaimer. Observed on the verified 200 for Austin, Texas + helium.
quirks: `geo` is the required QUERY param; `network` is an optional query param defaulting to helium (enum currently only 'helium'). Not a body field.
Fixed price $0.015 (amount 15000, USDC 6 decimals on Base); not dynamic.
402 challenge is delivered in the `payment-required` response HEADER (base64 x402 v2); the 402 body is an empty {}.

This is a KEYED enrichment upstream (Relay Wireless): the provider had the Relay key configured, so the paid call returned available:true with real hotspot counts. The 402 self-description warns that without that key the route can return available:false with a note — the sibling keyless network/hotspot/wallet routes do not need it.

total_hotspots = sum of the iot and mobile subnetwork counts within the H3 cell containing the geo (hierarchical H3 match). Density and the opportunity signal are computed indicators, not a guarantee of RF quality — carries a not-investment-advice disclaimer.
Distinct from same-host /depin/rewards, /depin/network, /depin/wallet, /depin/hotspot — different operations, not aliases.
usage.guide: Assess DePIN wireless coverage and deployment opportunity for a place. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/depin/coverage?geo=Austin,%20Texas&network=helium — pass a `geo` (city/state/country string or an H3 cell; required) and optionally `network` (helium, the default). Pay $0.015 USDC via x402 on Base — no API key or account. The service geocodes the geo to an H3 cell (resolution 5, ~253 km2), counts the Helium IoT and Mobile hotspots asserted inside it, and returns total_hotspots, density_per_km2, a coverage `rating` (e.g. dense) and an `opportunity` signal (e.g. low = already well covered, so higher opportunity means underserved) — with per-subnetwork provenance from Relay Wireless and OpenStreetMap geocoding attribution. Synchronous: read the 200 JSON directly. Use to gauge whether a location is saturated or worth deploying new DePIN hardware. Verified live 2026-08-07 with geo='Austin, Texas', network='helium' → HTTP 200, $0.015 charged, available:true, total_hotspots 418 (10 IoT + 408 mobile), density 1.65/km2, rating 'dense', opportunity 'low'.

Every value is cited to its source.

key.description: Hotspot entity key or asset key (base58). Required.

Pays $0.01 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453). Result is returned inline in the 200 body (synchronous, no poll).
usage.outputShape: network (string), key (string echo), found (bool), name (string, animal-word hotspot name), asset_id (Solana asset pubkey), entity_key (on-chain entity key), key_to_asset_key (string), subnetworks (string[] e.g. [iot,mobile]), by_subnetwork ({<subnet>: {location:{city,state,country,h3,lat,long}, elevation?, gain?, dc_onboarding_fee, device_type?}}), flags ({has_asserted_location bool, multi_network bool, deployment_completeness number 0-1}), owner_wallet ({value: Solana address, available bool, provenance}), earnings ({available bool, reason} — points at /depin/rewards for reward history), provenance ({source, ref, network, as_of}), attribution (string[] source citations), disclaimer (string)

name: Agentstools DePIN Network
description: Network health and token-economics verdict for a DePIN network (e.g. Helium) from public data: IOT/MOBILE node counts, on-chain token supply for HNT/IOT/MOBILE/DC, emission and halving context, and a coverage-scale decentralization indicator, each value cited to its source.

name: Agentstools DePIN Rewards

network.description: DePIN network id (query param; default helium).

subnetwork.description: Optional Helium subnetwork (query param; default mobile).

key.description: Optional hotspot entity or asset key (base58) to scope rewards to a single entity.

days.description: Lookback window in days (query param; default 7, max 30).

by_reward_type.description: Map of reward_type -> {count, total_amount} over the sampled records.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/depin/rewards with OPTIONAL query params: network (enum: helium, default helium), subnetwork (enum: iot|mobile, default mobile), key (optional base58 hotspot entity/asset key to scope to one entity), days (integer lookback 1-30, default 7). No request body, no API key. First call returns HTTP 402 with an x402 v2 challenge in the `payment-required` header (USDC on Base eip155:8453, $0.02); settling it returns HTTP 200 with the aggregate inline (synchronous, no poll).

Distinct same-host ops: /depin/coverage, /depin/network, /depin/wallet, /depin/hotspot are different operations, not aliases or path-param variants of this one.
