name: BlockRun Binance Book Ticker
description: Binance raw book-ticker (best bid/ask) data for a trading pair at microsecond granularity over a requested time range (via BlockRun's Predexon proxy).

symbol.description: Binance trading pair, e.g. BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT.

ticks.description: Book-ticker records (best bid/ask) at microsecond granularity within the window.

usage.callShape: GET /api/v1/pm/binance/ticks/{symbol}?start_time=<unixMs>&end_time=<unixMs> — {symbol} is a Binance trading pair (e.g. BTCUSDT). start_time and end_time (both Unix milliseconds) are REQUIRED query params. No request body. x402 USDC on Base, $0.0085/call.
usage.outputShape: { symbol: string, ticks: [ {best bid/ask book-ticker records at microsecond granularity} ], pagination: { limit: int, count: int, pagination_key: string|null, has_more: bool } }
quirks: Pay-tested live 2026-08-07: HTTP 200, $0.0085, tx 0xbf11beebf02a9914ce4d7e3ff89a3728df9ec81b98a75ded80c8cee0bb548f00 (Base USDC).

start_time & end_time (Unix ms) are REQUIRED query params but are NOT in the provider openapi (which lists zero parameters) — omitting them returns HTTP 422 'Predexon rejected the request. Check required parameters. Payment was NOT charged.'
Tier 2 pricing: payTo is the Predexon recipient wallet 0x6E007731870EDe419CfB31889Cd5C4493CEcb04c, distinct from other BlockRun endpoints' payTo (0xe903...).
The path segment is the Binance symbol (BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT, ...); returns microsecond-granularity best bid/ask (book ticker), not OHLCV candles (see /pm/binance/candles/{symbol} for candles).

The verified 2-second window returned ticks:[] (count 0) — the endpoint responded with the correct schema but historical tick coverage may not include every window; widen start_time/end_time for populated results.
usage.guide: Call GET https://blockrun.ai/api/v1/pm/binance/ticks/{symbol} substituting {symbol} with a Binance trading pair (e.g. BTCUSDT). Supply BOTH required query params start_time and end_time as Unix millisecond timestamps bounding the window you want (keep the window small — tick data is microsecond-granular and can be large). No body, no API key; pay the $0.0085 x402 charge in USDC on Base. Response is JSON: symbol, a ticks[] array of best bid/ask records, and a pagination object (use pagination_key when has_more is true).

name: BlockRun Polymarket Market Leaderboard
description: Ranked leaderboard of the top traders (by PnL, volume, ROI, win rate and trading style) for one specific Polymarket market, keyed by the market's condition_id (BlockRun /pm/polymarket, Predexon data).

inputSchema.hash: Polymarket market condition_id (0x-prefixed 32-byte / 66-char hex hash) in the URL path

outputSchema.entries: array of {rank, user (wallet address), metrics:{realized_pnl, total_pnl, volume, roi, trades, wins, losses, win_rate, profit_factor, positions_closed, avg_buy_price, avg_sell_price, fees_paid, fees_refunded}, trading_styles:{is_whale, is_market_maker, is_active_trader, is_buy_and_hold, is_degen, is_high_conviction, is_contrarian, is_value_hunter, primary_style}, entry_edge, first_trade_at}

usage.callShape: GET https://blockrun.ai/api/v1/pm/polymarket/leaderboard/market/{hash} where {hash} is a Polymarket market condition_id (e.g. .../leaderboard/market/0x7d0aaf81bbd3fd73b6a1651cce08a452c0cbf9c0cbb4520ce0f981065b639d88)
usage.outputShape: {condition_id, window (e.g. all_time), sort_by (e.g. total_pnl), entries[100 of {rank, user (wallet addr), metrics:{realized_pnl, total_pnl, volume, roi, trades, wins, losses, win_rate, profit_factor, positions_closed, avg_buy_price, avg_sell_price, fees_paid, fees_refunded}, trading_styles:{is_whale, is_market_maker, is_active_trader, is_buy_and_hold, is_degen, is_high_conviction, is_contrarian, is_value_hunter, primary_style}, entry_edge, first_trade_at}], pagination:{limit, count, pagination_key, has_more}}
quirks: The path segment {hash} is the Polymarket market CONDITION_ID (0x-prefixed 66-char hex), NOT a clobTokenId or slug. Discover condition_ids via /pm/polymarket/markets or /pm/markets/search, or Polymarket's public gamma-api (verified with 0x7d0aaf...d88, a live high-volume market).
This is the PER-MARKET leaderboard; the sibling /pm/polymarket/leaderboard (no /market/{hash}) is the separate GLOBAL cross-market leaderboard.
Returns up to 100 entries per page, ranked by total_pnl (all_time window) by default; paginate with pagination.pagination_key (cursor) while pagination.has_more is true.
Predexon (Tier 1) pricing: payment routes to the Predexon recipient wallet (payTo 0x6E00...b04c). Fixed price 0.0085 USDC (8500 atomic) on Base; no dynamic pricing.
x402 v2 challenge present in www-authenticate, payment-required, x-payment-required headers and JSON body; unpaid GET returns the 402 and is NOT charged.
usage.guide: Get the leaderboard of top traders for ONE specific Polymarket market. GET https://blockrun.ai/api/v1/pm/polymarket/leaderboard/market/{hash} where {hash} is the market's condition_id (0x-prefixed 66-char hex, e.g. 0x7d0aaf81bbd3fd73b6a1651cce08a452c0cbf9c0cbb4520ce0f981065b639d88). Get condition_ids from /pm/polymarket/markets, /pm/markets/search, or Polymarket's gamma-api. Payment is x402 USDC on Base, ~$0.0085/call, no API key. Response is JSON: read body.entries[] (each has rank, user wallet, metrics.total_pnl/volume/roi/win_rate, trading_styles.primary_style); up to 100 per page, cursor-paginate via body.pagination.pagination_key while body.pagination.has_more.

name: BlockRun Polymarket Market Price
description: Current or historical price for a single Polymarket outcome token by its CLOB token id (BlockRun /pm/polymarket).

inputSchema.id: Polymarket outcome-token CLOB id (long numeric ERC-1155 token id) in the URL path

usage.callShape: GET https://blockrun.ai/api/v1/pm/polymarket/market-price/{id} where {id} is a Polymarket outcome-token CLOB id (e.g. .../market-price/21742633143463906290569050155826241533067272736897614950488156847949938836455)
usage.outputShape: {price (number, token price 0-1), at_time (number, unix epoch seconds)}
quirks: The path segment {id} is the Polymarket CLOB TOKEN id (the long numeric ERC-1155 clobTokenId for one outcome), NOT the market condition_id/slug. Get token ids from /pm/polymarket/markets or /pm/markets/search (its condition_id → the market's clobTokenIds).
Response is a single tiny object {price, at_time} — the CURRENT price by default (verified: {"price":1,"at_time":1786143870} for a resolved YES token).
The op name/summary implies historical prices too, but the default no-query call returns only the latest point; historical params were not documented and not exercised.
x402 USDC on Base, ~$0.0085/call, no API key. Unpaid GET returns the 402 challenge (accepts in www-authenticate/x-payment-required header and body) and is NOT charged.
usage.guide: Get the current price of a single Polymarket outcome token. GET https://blockrun.ai/api/v1/pm/polymarket/market-price/{id} where {id} is the Polymarket CLOB token id (the long numeric ERC-1155 clobTokenId for one YES/NO outcome, e.g. 21742633143463906290569050155826241533067272736897614950488156847949938836455). Discover token ids via /pm/polymarket/markets or /pm/markets/search. Payment is x402 USDC on Base, ~$0.0085/call, no API key. Response is a single JSON object: read body.price (0-1 token price) and body.at_time (unix epoch seconds).

name: BlockRun Polymarket Market Volume
description: Historical cumulative trading-volume time-series (daily, split into buy/sell) for a single Polymarket market identified by its outcome-token id.

usage.callShape: GET https://blockrun.ai/api/v1/pm/polymarket/markets/{tokenId}/volume where {tokenId} is a Polymarket outcome-token id (uint256 decimal string). No query params or body.
usage.outputShape: { token_id (string, echoes input), granularity ('day'), start_time (unix seconds), end_time (unix seconds), volume_over_time[]: each { timestamp (unix seconds, day bucket), volume (cumulative total USD volume up to that day), buy_volume (cumulative buy-side USD), sell_volume (cumulative sell-side USD) } }. The series is CUMULATIVE and monotonically non-decreasing; the last point's volume is the market's lifetime total to date.
quirks: The {tokenId} path segment is the Polymarket outcome-token id (a uint256 decimal string), NOT a condition_id, market_id, or slug. Get it from Polymarket's free gamma API (market.clobTokenIds[]) or from BlockRun's own /pm/polymarket/markets outcomes[].token_id.
volume/buy_volume/sell_volume are CUMULATIVE running totals, not per-day deltas — subtract consecutive points to get daily volume.
granularity is fixed to 'day' in the response (no interval param is documented or accepted).
Some day buckets report volume 0 — that means the cumulative total was unchanged that day (no trades), not missing data.
An unknown/invalid token id still costs the x402 payment; verify the token id against gamma/clobTokenIds before calling to avoid paying for an empty series.
needs: A Polymarket outcome-token id (uint256 decimal string) — obtainable free from gamma-api.polymarket.com market.clobTokenIds or from BlockRun /pm/polymarket/markets.
usage.guide: Get the historical cumulative trading-volume curve for one Polymarket market. GET https://blockrun.ai/api/v1/pm/polymarket/markets/{tokenId}/volume where {tokenId} is a Polymarket outcome-token id (uint256 decimal string, e.g. 27146956652877944551877724690365745048289675287536243265951843487691050802191 — source it from Polymarket gamma clobTokenIds or BlockRun /pm/polymarket/markets outcomes[].token_id). No query string, no body. Pays $0.0085 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453), no API key, returns synchronously. Response: token_id, granularity ('day'), start_time, end_time (unix seconds), and volume_over_time[] — an array of daily points { timestamp, volume, buy_volume, sell_volume }. All three volume figures are CUMULATIVE running totals in USD (not daily deltas); read the final point for lifetime volume, or diff consecutive points for per-day volume. Verified live 2026-08-07 with the token id above: HTTP 200, ~106 daily points, ending cumulative volume ~$177,392 (buy ~$89,421 / sell ~$87,972).

name: BlockRun Exchange Depth
description: Live centralized-exchange order-book depth snapshot for a trading pair from BlockRun's Surf data suite — top bid/ask levels with price/amount, spread, mid price, and aggregated bid/ask depth.

backends.inputSchema: Query params: pair (string, required) — trading pair symbol, e.g. BTCUSDT; normalized server-side to BASE/QUOTE.
backends.outputSchema: SimpleListResponseExchangeDepthItem: { $schema, data: [{ exchange (string, e.g. 'binance'), pair (string, e.g. 'BTC/USDT'), bids: [{price, amount}], asks: [{price, amount}], spread (number), spread_pct (number), bid_depth (number, summed base amount across bid levels), ask_depth (number), mid_price (number) }], meta: { credits_used, cached } }

usage.callShape: GET https://blockrun.ai/api/v1/surf/exchange/depth?pair=BTCUSDT (required query param: pair). No request body.
usage.outputShape: body.data[] = array (one item observed, for binance) of { exchange (string, e.g. 'binance'), pair (string, normalized e.g. 'BTC/USDT'), bids[] and asks[] = arrays of ~20 { price (number), amount (number, base units) } levels sorted best-first, spread (number = best ask - best bid), spread_pct (number, fraction), bid_depth (number, summed bid amounts), ask_depth (number, summed ask amounts), mid_price (number) }. body.meta = { credits_used (1), cached (bool) }.
quirks: REQUIRED query param 'pair' (e.g. ?pair=BTCUSDT). Omitting it returns HTTP 400 with required_params:['pair'] and payment is NOT charged.
Pair is passed compact (BTCUSDT) and echoed back normalized as BASE/QUOTE (e.g. 'BTC/USDT'); same convention as sibling surf/exchange/klines.
Returns a top-of-book snapshot (~20 bid + ~20 ask levels), not full-book — for pre-trade spread/mid/near-book liquidity reads.
openapi lists price $0.0085; live 402 and the actual charge were both $0.0085 USDC on Base (registry probe hint said $0.0075).
Payment is x402 USDC on Base (eip155:8453), no API key; meta.credits_used=1 per call.
$schema points at api.asksurf.ai/schemas/SimpleListResponseExchangeDepthItem.json (Surf is the underlying data provider).
usage.guide: Call GET https://blockrun.ai/api/v1/surf/exchange/depth with a REQUIRED ?pair=<SYMBOL> query param (e.g. pair=BTCUSDT; omitting it returns a 400 with no charge). The x402 wallet pays automatically (~$0.0085 USDC on Base, no API key). The 200 response returns body.data[] with an order-book snapshot per exchange: bids[] and asks[] as {price, amount} levels (best-first), plus spread, spread_pct, bid_depth, ask_depth and mid_price; body.meta gives credits_used/cached. Use it as a live pre-trade liquidity/spread read for a CEX pair. Change the pair to quote other markets (ETHUSDT, SOLUSDT, etc.).

name: BlockRun Long/Short Ratio
description: Historical long/short account ratio for a perpetual trading pair on centralized exchanges (BlockRun Surf).

pair.description: Required query param: a CEX perpetual market symbol, e.g. BTCUSDT / ETHUSDT (binance market notation).

usage.callShape: GET https://blockrun.ai/api/v1/surf/exchange/long-short-ratio?pair=BTCUSDT (required query param: pair, a binance perpetual market symbol) -> long/short ratio history as sync JSON.
usage.outputShape: body.data[] = array of {exchange (string, e.g. 'binance'), pair (string, e.g. 'BTC/USDT'), long_short_ratio (number, e.g. 1.14 = longs/shorts account ratio), timestamp (unix seconds, hourly points)}. body.$schema = SimpleListResponseExchangeLongShortRatioItem; body.meta = {credits_used, cached}.
quirks: REQUIRED query param 'pair'. It must be a real CEX (binance) market symbol like BTCUSDT or ETHUSDT — NOT a bare coin ticker. Passing pair=BTC returns HTTP 400 {error:'Bad Request', details.error.code:'INVALID_REQUEST', message:'binance does not have market symbol BTC:USDT'} and the provider states 'Payment was NOT charged.'
On a validation 400 the provider does NOT settle payment (no txHash, unconfirmed), so only the corrected BTCUSDT request incurred the charge.
Response is a TIME SERIES: body.data[] is an array of hourly {long_short_ratio, timestamp} points; latest = last element.
Fixed price $0.0085 USDC; live 402 amount '8500' is atomic USDC (6 decimals) = 0.0085. Probe hint said $0.0095 but the live 402 quoted 8500 = $0.0085.

x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), asset USDC 0x8335...2913, payTo 0x058a...8F17, maxTimeoutSeconds 300; accepts present in www-authenticate + payment-required/x-payment-required base64 headers and echoed (price + required_params) in the JSON 402 body.
Sync data endpoint: result returned inline on the paid 200, no job id / polling.
usage.guide: Call GET https://blockrun.ai/api/v1/surf/exchange/long-short-ratio with a required ?pair=<BINANCE_PERP_SYMBOL> query param (e.g. pair=BTCUSDT or ETHUSDT); a bare coin like BTC returns a 400 with no charge. The x402 wallet pays automatically (~$0.0085 USDC on Base). The 200 response is a long/short-ratio time series at body.data[], an array of {exchange, pair, long_short_ratio, timestamp} hourly points; take the last element for the most recent ratio (>1 = more longs than shorts). Change the symbol for other pairs.

name: BlockRun Exchange Markets
description: Catalog of centralized-exchange trading pairs (symbol, base/quote, spot/perp type, active flag, maker/taker fees) via BlockRun's Surf gateway.

usage.callShape: GET https://blockrun.ai/api/v1/surf/exchange/markets (no required params; optional ?exchange=<name> filter). Returns the exchange trading-pairs catalog as sync JSON.
usage.outputShape: JSON object { $schema (string), data[] = array of { exchange, pair (e.g. 'ETH/BTC'), base, quote, type ('spot'|perp), active (bool), maker_fee (number), taker_fee (number) }, meta { credits_used, cached } }. Default response returns Binance pairs.
quirks: No required parameters — live 402 body reports required_params:[] and the call succeeds with an empty GET.
Default catalog returned is Binance spot/perp pairs (~13KB, ~100+ pairs in this probe); an optional ?exchange=<name> query narrows the exchange.
Fixed price $0.0085 (8500 atomic USDC) on Base; the sweep's $0.0095 probe hint is a stale worst-case figure — the live 402 and x-payment-info both quote 8500 atomic = $0.0085.
Sync response, no job id to poll; data returns inline as application/json.
x402 v2: accepts delivered in www-authenticate / payment-required / x-payment-required headers (base64) and mirrored in the JSON body paymentInfo.
BlockRun proxies /api/v1/surf/<path> to https://api.asksurf.ai/gateway/v1/<path>; the $schema field points at api.asksurf.ai/schemas/SimpleListResponseExchangeMarketItem.json.
usage.guide: Fetch the centralized-exchange trading-pairs catalog. GET https://blockrun.ai/api/v1/surf/exchange/markets with no required params (optional ?exchange=<name> to filter). x402 pays automatically (~$0.0085 USDC on Base). The 200 response is JSON with data[] = { exchange, pair, base, quote, type, active, maker_fee, taker_fee }; default is Binance pairs. Sync — no polling.

name: BlockRun Surf Perpetual Snapshot
description: Perpetual futures snapshot for a trading pair — funding rate (with 1h/8h/annualized variants and next funding time), open interest (amount + USD), and mark/index price — across major derivatives exchanges (BlockRun Surf).

pair.description: Trading pair in BASE/QUOTE slash format, e.g. BTC/USDT (the swap settle suffix is added automatically based on quote currency). Required query param.

fields.description: Optional comma-separated list of fields to return, e.g. funding,oi.

exchange.description: Optional exchange id; defaults to binance. One of binance, okx, bybit, bitget, htx, bitfinex, bitmex, hyperliquid.

funding.description: funding_rate, funding_rate_raw, next_funding (ISO), mark_price, index_price, interval, funding_interval_hours, funding_rate_1h, funding_rate_8h, funding_rate_annualized

usage.callShape: GET https://blockrun.ai/api/v1/surf/exchange/perp?pair=BTC/USDT (required query param: pair, in BASE/QUOTE slash format; optional fields=funding,oi and exchange=binance) -> synchronous perpetual-contract snapshot JSON.
usage.outputShape: Synchronous JSON. data.exchange + data.pair echo the request; data.funding{funding_rate, funding_rate_raw, next_funding(ISO), mark_price, index_price, interval('8h'), funding_interval_hours, funding_rate_1h, funding_rate_8h, funding_rate_annualized}; data.open_interest{open_interest_amount, open_interest_usd, timestamp(unix s)}; meta{credits_used, cached}. $schema=DataObjectResponseExchangePerpResponse. Verified run (pair=BTC/USDT, binance): funding_rate 0.00006131, mark_price 64859.85, open_interest_usd ~6.94B.
quirks: REQUIRED query param 'pair' MUST be in BASE/QUOTE slash format (e.g. pair=BTC/USDT). A bare ticker (pair=BTC) is internally mapped to 'BTC:USDT' and returns HTTP 400 {error:'Bad Request', 'NOT_FOUND: Symbol ... not found'} with 'Payment was NOT charged' (no charge on this validation failure).
The perpetual swap settle suffix is added automatically based on the quote currency — pass just BASE/QUOTE.
Optional 'fields' picks which sections to return (e.g. fields=funding,oi); optional 'exchange' defaults to binance and accepts binance, okx, bybit, bitget, htx, bitfinex, bitmex, hyperliquid.
Fixed price $0.0085 USDC (atomic amount '8500' / 10^6) on Base eip155:8453, asset USDC 0x8335...2913, payTo 0x058a...8F17.
Sync JSON data response (no job id to poll).
x402 v2: accepts present in the base64 www-authenticate + payment-required + x-payment-required headers; JSON 402 body also echoes price + required_params.
Pay-verified live 2026-08-07 with pair=BTC/USDT -> HTTP 200, $0.0085 charged (tx 0xc3685d5b7870e77ca683a42baf65cf0d2fed3b43ab5df1dbe134f1ff8c8eb7c0 on Base).
usage.guide: Call GET https://blockrun.ai/api/v1/surf/exchange/perp with a required ?pair=<BASE/QUOTE> query param in slash format (e.g. pair=BTC/USDT); a bare ticker like BTC returns a 400 with no charge, so always include the quote. Optionally add fields=funding,oi to select sections and exchange=<id> (default binance; also okx, bybit, bitget, htx, bitfinex, bitmex, hyperliquid). The x402 wallet pays automatically (~$0.0085 USDC on Base, no API key). The 200 response is a synchronous snapshot at data: data.funding holds the funding rate (funding_rate plus 1h/8h/annualized variants, next_funding ISO time, mark_price, index_price, interval), and data.open_interest holds open_interest_amount + open_interest_usd + timestamp. Use it to read live perpetual funding and open interest for a pair on a chosen exchange.

name: BlockRun Futures Market
description: Crypto perpetual-futures market overview from BlockRun's Surf data suite — per-symbol open interest, funding rate, long/short ratio, and 24h volume across ~100 assets.

name: Cryptyx Funding Rate
description: Aggregated-exchange daily perpetual-swap funding rate history for one crypto asset over the last N days: a raw feed of per-day funding-rate closes (no annualisation, no z-score) intended as cheap historical input for carry-trade backtests and crowding diagnostics.

asset.description: REQUIRED. Asset symbol (e.g. BTC, ETH, SOL). Trimmed and uppercased server-side.

days.description: Optional. Number of trailing days to return (1-365, default 30).

items.description: One row per trailing day: { asof_day (date), asset (symbol), fr_close (daily funding-rate close, decimal — can be negative) }.

usage.callShape: GET https://cryptyx.ai/api/funding-rate?asset=BTC with a REQUIRED 'asset' query param (asset symbol; trimmed and uppercased server-side) and an optional 'days' param (1-365, default 30). No request body. Pays $0.01 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453). Response is synchronous JSON inline in the 200.
usage.outputShape: {ok, asset, days, asof_day (latest anchor date), count, rates:[{asof_day, asset, fr_close}], _next:{description, hints:[{path,method,price_usd,reason}]}}
quirks: 'asset' is REQUIRED — omitting it (calling with {}) will error; always pass a symbol like BTC/ETH/SOL. (The provider's bazaar input example shows asset:'' but the schema marks it required.)

fr_close is a raw daily funding-rate close (a small decimal, e.g. 0.066657 or -0.184184 in the observed BTC feed) — no annualisation and no z-score are applied; negative values mean shorts paid longs.
asof_day is a daily EOD snapshot — data is daily, not intraday/tick.
'rates' is ordered most-recent-first; 'count' equals the number of rows returned (up to 'days').

Response includes a non-data '_next' block of recommended follow-up paid Cryptyx endpoints (asymmetry, active-signals, thesis, conviction, trade-ideas); it is guidance, not part of the funding-rate payload.
usage.guide: Cryptyx Funding Rate returns the aggregated-exchange daily perpetual funding-rate history for one crypto asset. Call GET https://cryptyx.ai/api/funding-rate?asset=BTC — 'asset' is REQUIRED (ticker like BTC/ETH/SOL); optional 'days' (1-365, default 30) sets the trailing window. No body, no API key — pay $0.01 USDC via x402 on Base. Result is inline JSON in the 200 (synchronous): ok, asset, days, asof_day, count, and rates[] (most-recent-first) where each row has asof_day, asset and fr_close (the raw daily funding-rate close, a small decimal that can be negative). It is a raw feed (no annualisation, no z-score) meant as cheap historical input for carry-trade backtests and funding-crowding diagnostics; the response's _next hints point to asymmetry/active-signals/thesis for deeper positioning context.

name: Cryptyx Signal Threshold Simulator
description: Pre-flight threshold simulator for a Cryptyx trading signal: given a signal_id, a parameter name and a proposed cutoff value for one anchor day, it counts how many of ~200 assets would trigger, returning current vs proposed threshold plus the estimated trigger rate — a non-mutating dry-run to tune a signal before forking its parameters.

body.signal_id: REQUIRED. Atomic signal registry ID, uppercased server-side (e.g. TR_MOMO_CONT_14D, FLOW_ACCUM_NETUSD_7D, VOL_COMPRESSION_7v30). Enumerate valid ids via GET /api/signals/catalog.
body.threshold_key: REQUIRED. Parameter name to simulate (e.g. t_thr, z_thr). Used to fetch the current_threshold from signals.signal_params for comparison. The relevant key comes from the signal's active_params in the catalog.
body.threshold_value: REQUIRED (number). Proposed cutoff value. Interpreted as a z-score for most signals, a t-score for TR_MOMO_* signals.
body.asof_day: OPTIONAL. YYYY-MM-DD lookup day. Defaults to metrics.aligned_day_1d() (the latest aligned day).

_next.description: Recommended next paid x402 Cryptyx calls

usage.callShape: POST https://cryptyx.ai/api/signals/simulate with a JSON body {signal_id, threshold_key, threshold_value, asof_day?}. signal_id, threshold_key and threshold_value are REQUIRED; asof_day is optional (defaults to the latest aligned day). Returns synchronously — no polling. Non-mutating dry run (no DB write). Pay-per-call over x402 (exact scheme, USDC on Base, $0.05).
usage.outputShape: {ok:true, signal_id (string, echoed uppercased), threshold_key (string), proposed_threshold (number, = the threshold_value you sent), current_threshold (number, the signal's live cutoff from signal_params), asof_day (YYYY-MM-DD), n_triggered (integer count of assets that would trigger at the proposed cutoff), n_total (integer universe size evaluated, ~196-200), estimated_trigger_rate (float 0-1), estimated_trigger_pct (float percentage), _next{description, hints[]:{path, method, price_usd, reason}}}
quirks: Read-only PRE-FLIGHT simulator — unlike the sibling /api/signals/eval (which writes to signal_log), simulate never mutates; it just counts would-trigger assets at a hypothetical cutoff. Safe to call repeatedly.

The 402 details (accepts + JSON input/output schema + example) live in the response's payment-required HEADER (base64 x402 v2 envelope with an extensions.bazaar block), NOT the JSON body (a bare POST returns body {} with status 402).

signal_id is uppercased server-side; valid ids and their tunable parameter keys come from GET /api/signals/catalog (each signal row carries active_params like {t_thr}/{z_thr}/{thr}/{vol_thr} and an _actions.simulate_threshold ready-to-call template).

threshold_value is interpreted as a z-score for most signals but a t-score for TR_MOMO_* signals (per the provider's schema description); pick the value in the same units as the signal's current_threshold.
asof_day is optional; omitting it defaults to metrics.aligned_day_1d() (the latest aligned trading day).
Every response carries a _next block of recommended follow-on paid Cryptyx endpoints (signals/explain, signals/catalog, signals/top, asset/thesis, v1/ai/trade-ideas).
Hosted on Vercel behind the first-party custom domain cryptyx.ai, so the *.vercel.app platform-hosting caveat does not apply. $0.05 = Cryptyx 'premium' pricing tier.
needs: A valid signal_id and its tunable parameter key (threshold_key) plus a proposed numeric cutoff — all obtainable from GET /api/signals/catalog (no external artifacts required).
usage.guide: POST https://cryptyx.ai/api/signals/simulate to pre-flight a proposed threshold change on a Cryptyx trading signal WITHOUT writing anything. Send a JSON body {signal_id, threshold_key, threshold_value, asof_day?}: pick signal_id and its tunable parameter key (threshold_key, e.g. t_thr or z_thr) from GET /api/signals/catalog, then set threshold_value to the proposed cutoff (z-score for most signals, t-score for TR_MOMO_* signals). You get back {ok, signal_id, threshold_key, proposed_threshold, current_threshold, asof_day, n_triggered, n_total, estimated_trigger_rate, estimated_trigger_pct} — how many of ~200 assets would trigger at the new cutoff vs the live one. Use this to tune a signal before forking its parameters via POST /api/signals/fork. Pays $0.05 USDC on Base via x402 per call.

name: Cryptyx Trade Ideas
description: Returns a ranked starter pack of N crypto trade ideas — each a composite-scored asset with returns, derivatives positioning (funding/OI z-scores), current regime, dominant factor class, and the top validated setups and predictive metrics backing it — in a single $0.10 x402 GET, tunable by count (limit) and forward-return horizon.

queryParams.limit: integer, optional — number of ideas to return (range 3-20, default 5)
queryParams.horizon: string, optional — forward-return horizon for setup stats: 7d, 14d, or 30d (default 14d)

inputSchema.note: All query params optional; a bare GET returns 5 ideas over the 14d horizon. No path params, no request body.

properties.ideas: [{asset, rank, composite_score, returns:{ret_1d,ret_7d}, sharpe_7d, derivatives:{funding_z,oi_momentum_z} (may be null), regime, regime_confidence, dominant_factor:{class,t_score}, signal_count:{atomic,composite}, top_setups:[{signal_id,name,class,grade,n_triggers,hit_rate,mean_fwd_return,last_triggered,score}], top_predictors:[{metric_id,class,name,ts_grade,ts_ic,cs_grade}]}]
properties._next: {description, hints:[{path, method, price_usd, reason}]} — recommended follow-up paid Cryptyx endpoints

usage.callShape: GET https://cryptyx.ai/api/v1/ai/trade-ideas with optional query params ?limit=<3-20>&horizon=<7d|14d|30d>. Both optional (defaults: limit=5, horizon=14d) — a bare GET works. No path params, no request body. The ranked ideas are returned synchronously in the 200 body. Pays a fixed $0.10 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453); no API key.
usage.outputShape: 200 JSON: { ok:true, horizon:"14d", asof_day:"latest", ideas:[ {asset, rank, composite_score, returns:{ret_1d,ret_7d}, sharpe_7d, derivatives:{funding_z,oi_momentum_z}, regime, regime_confidence, dominant_factor:{class,t_score}, signal_count:{atomic,composite}, top_setups:[{signal_id,name,class,grade,n_triggers,hit_rate,mean_fwd_return,last_triggered,score}], top_predictors:[{metric_id,class,name,ts_grade,ts_ic,cs_grade}] } ], meta:{total_universe,setup_gate,scope:"signals_only",x402_price_usd:0.1}, durationMs, _cache:{hit,ageMs}, _next:{description,hints:[{path,method,price_usd,reason}]} }. Verified live 2026-08-07 (bare GET, defaults): horizon 14d, 5 ideas ranked GT/XMR/OKB/PUMP/FRAX, GT #1 (composite_score 0.3199, regime consolidation, dominant factor OB).
quirks: All numeric fields are returned as real JSON numbers (not strings, unlike the sibling Cryptyx market-brief). derivatives.funding_z / oi_momentum_z can be null for some assets (e.g. FRAX).
limit is clamped to 3-20 (default 5) and horizon to 7d/14d/30d (default 14d); out-of-range values fall back to defaults rather than erroring.

meta.scope is 'signals_only' and meta.setup_gate documents the filter used ('health_grade IN (A,B), NOT anti-predictive, n_triggers >= 5') — ideas are ranked by signal/factor confluence, not price forecasts; top_setups.mean_fwd_return can be negative even for a top-ranked idea.
durationMs can be very large (observed ~167s on a cache miss); _cache.hit indicates whether the response was served warm. asof_day comes back as the literal string 'latest' rather than a date.

Response includes a '_next' block of recommended follow-up paid Cryptyx x402 endpoints (asset/thesis, asset/active-signals, asset/asymmetry, asset/regime-context $0.05 each, v1/agent-context $0.01) — a cross-sell/navigation hint, not part of the trade-ideas data.

The provider exposes the same OpenAPI at https://cryptyx.ai/openapi.json (documents price $0.10 fixed and the limit/horizon params); the /api/openapi.json and /api/v1/openapi.json variants are auth-gated (401).
usage.guide: Use this as a one-call ranked crypto trade-idea generator to drop into an agent. GET https://cryptyx.ai/api/v1/ai/trade-ideas (optionally ?limit=3-20&horizon=7d|14d|30d; defaults limit=5, horizon=14d); pay the fixed $0.10 USDC over x402 on Base, no API key. You get an ideas[] array ranked by composite score, each carrying: the asset ticker and rank, 1d/7d returns and 7d Sharpe, derivatives positioning (funding/OI momentum z-scores), the current market regime + confidence, the dominant factor class (t-score), atomic/composite signal counts, the top validated setups (signal_id, class, health grade, historical n_triggers/hit_rate/mean forward return, last-triggered date, score), and the top predictive metrics (metric_id, time-series and cross-sectional grades, IC). All numbers are real JSON numbers. Ideas are gated on signal health (grade A/B, non-anti-predictive, >=5 triggers) — treat them as research leads, not price forecasts. Drill into any ranked asset via the _next hints (thesis, active-signals, asymmetry, regime-context).

name: Strale Fear & Greed Index
description: Returns the Crypto Fear & Greed Index (0 = Extreme Fear to 100 = Extreme Greed) — current value, classification, and optional daily history up to 30 days, with an average and trend, sourced from Alternative.me.

days.description: Number of days of history (1-30). Default: 1

usage.callShape: GET https://api.strale.io/x402/fear-greed-index?days=7 (optional query param: days = number of days of history, 1-30, default 1)
usage.outputShape: body.current_value (0-100), body.classification (e.g. 'Fear'), body.timestamp; body.history[] = [{value, classification, date}] when days>1; body.average, body.trend (e.g. 'stable'); provenance + payment under body._meta
quirks: All params are optional; with no params it returns just the current value (days defaults to 1).
days accepts 1-30; values are integers 0-100 with classification buckets (Extreme Fear / Fear / Neutral / Greed / Extreme Greed).
Data sourced from alternative.me; index is crypto-market-wide, not per-token.
usage.guide: Make a GET request to https://api.strale.io/x402/fear-greed-index. Optionally set ?days=N (1-30) to include daily history; omit it for just the current reading. Pay via x402 (USDC on Base, ~$0.0216/call). Read body.current_value for the 0-100 index and body.classification for the label; body.history[] holds the daily series, body.average and body.trend summarize it. Provenance and settlement info are under body._meta.

name: Strale Wallet Age Check
description: Check when a wallet address made its first on-chain transaction and how old it is in days (first_tx_date, first_tx_hash, age_days) across Ethereum, Base, and other EVM chains via Etherscan V2 — a wallet-risk / KYT signal. Pay-per-call x402.

backends.inputSchema: GET query params: address (string, REQUIRED — wallet address, 0x...), chain_id (string, chain ID: 1=Ethereum, 8453=Base; default 1). No request body.
backends.outputSchema: { address (string), chain_id (string), has_activity (boolean), first_tx_date (ISO string), first_tx_hash (string), age_days (number), _meta: { capability, latency_ms, provenance:{source,fetched_at}, payment:{method,settlement_id,price_usd} } }

usage.callShape: GET https://api.strale.io/x402/wallet-age-check?address=0xd8dA6BF26964aF9D7eEd9e03E53415D37aA96045&chain_id=1 (address REQUIRED query param; chain_id optional query param, default 1; no request body)
usage.outputShape: Synchronous JSON object. body.has_activity (boolean) = whether the wallet has any transactions; body.first_tx_date (ISO timestamp of the first tx), body.first_tx_hash, body.age_days (integer days since first tx). Echoes body.address and body.chain_id. Payment/provenance under body._meta {capability, latency_ms, provenance:{source='etherscan.io', fetched_at}, payment:{method,settlement_id,price_usd}}.
quirks: address is the ONLY required query param; chain_id is optional (defaults to 1=Ethereum; use 8453 for Base). Both are query-string params, no request body.
Supports Ethereum, Base and other EVM chains via Etherscan V2 (pass the numeric chain_id).
If the wallet has no transactions, has_activity is false and the age fields will be absent/null.
Data sourced from etherscan.io (see body._meta.provenance.source).
Price $0.0216 USDC on Base; no API key.
usage.guide: Look up a wallet's age (days since its first on-chain transaction) — a KYT/risk signal, e.g. a brand-new wallet moving large amounts is a red flag. Send a GET to https://api.strale.io/x402/wallet-age-check with the required query param address (0x...) and optional chain_id (1=Ethereum default, 8453=Base, or any EVM chain id). No request body. It is an x402 paid endpoint at $0.0216 USDC on Base; no API key. Response is synchronous JSON — read body.has_activity, body.first_tx_date, body.first_tx_hash, and body.age_days; body._meta carries provenance (etherscan.io) and settlement info. Verified 2026-08-07 with {address:'0xd8dA6BF26964aF9D7eEd9e03E53415D37aA96045', chain_id:'1'} -> HTTP 200 (has_activity true, first tx 2015-09-28, age_days 3966), $0.0216 charged (tx 0x3a6b227c69cf39c8a9236770ac4a70dd07c75beba68bebbc085245c844af7130).

name: Strale Wallet Balance Lookup
description: Get the native token balance (wei + ETH) for any EVM wallet address plus a list of recently interacted ERC-20 tokens — Ethereum and other EVM chains via Etherscan V2 — through Strale's x402 endpoint.

address.description: Wallet address (0x...). Required.

outputSchema.description: body.address, body.chain_id, body.native_balance_wei (string), body.native_balance_eth (number), body.recent_tokens[] each {name, symbol, address}, body.token_transfer_count (int), body.note; provenance/payment under body._meta.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.strale.io/x402/wallet-balance-lookup?address=0xd8dA6BF26964aF9D7eEd9e03E53415D37aA96045&chain_id=1 . Params are query-string: address (required, 0x... wallet), chain_id (optional, default 1=Ethereum). First call returns HTTP 402 with x402 requirements, then HTTP 200 with the data once an EIP-3009 USDC authorization is signed. Pays ~$0.0216 USDC via x402 on Base.
usage.outputShape: JSON object: body.address, body.chain_id, body.native_balance_wei (string, wei), body.native_balance_eth (number, ETH), body.recent_tokens[] each {name, symbol, address}, body.token_transfer_count (int), body.note (string). Provenance/payment at body._meta {capability, latency_ms, provenance{source:"etherscan.io", fetched_at}, payment{method:"x402", settlement_id, price_usd}}. Verified live for 0xd8dA6BF...96045: native_balance_eth 6.633338, native_balance_wei 6633338316767822584, token_transfer_count 100, recent_tokens included RELICS/CMD/ETH/MONEY/stkWALLET/CATE/CATE404.
quirks: address is required; chain_id defaults to 1 (Ethereum) — both are query-string params, not a JSON body.

recent_tokens is DERIVED from the last 100 token transfers, NOT actual token balances (the provider states this in body.note); it lists tokens the wallet recently interacted with, not current holdings or amounts.
Only the NATIVE token balance (native_balance_wei/eth) is a true balance; there are no per-ERC-20 balance amounts in the response.
Data sourced from Etherscan V2 (body._meta.provenance.source = etherscan.io); supports Ethereum and other EVM chains by chain_id.
Synchronous: balance is inline in the 200 body; no polling.
For transaction history use the sibling wallet-transactions-lookup; for wallet age use wallet-age-check.
usage.guide: Look up the native-token balance for an EVM wallet via Strale. Call GET https://api.strale.io/x402/wallet-balance-lookup with query params: address (required, the 0x... wallet) and optional chain_id (default 1 = Ethereum). It is an x402 paid endpoint at ~$0.0216 USDC on Base (asset USDC 0x8335...2913, payTo 0x66D7...83bC): the first request returns 402 with payment requirements, and after signing an EIP-3009 USDC authorization it returns 200. Read the native balance from body.native_balance_eth (ETH) or body.native_balance_wei (wei). body.recent_tokens[] lists ERC-20 tokens the wallet recently interacted with (name/symbol/address) — this is derived from the last 100 token transfers per body.note, NOT current balances, and carries no amounts. Data is Etherscan-V2-sourced. For transaction history use wallet-transactions-lookup; for wallet age use wallet-age-check.

name: Strale Wallet Transactions Lookup
description: Get recent transactions for any EVM wallet address (up to 50) with hash, from/to, ETH value, timestamp, block number, gas used, and sent/received direction — Ethereum and other EVM chains via Etherscan V2 — through Strale's x402 endpoint.

address.description: Wallet address (0x...). Required.

limit.description: Number of transactions (1-50). Default: 20.

outputSchema.description: body.address, body.chain_id, body.total_returned, body.sent_count, body.received_count, body.transactions[] each {hash, from, to, value_eth, timestamp, block_number, gas_used, is_error, direction}; provenance/payment under body._meta.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.strale.io/x402/wallet-transactions-lookup?address=0xd8dA6BF26964aF9D7eEd9e03E53415D37aA96045&chain_id=1 . Params are query-string: address (required, 0x... wallet), chain_id (optional, default 1=Ethereum), limit (optional, 1-50, default 20). First call returns HTTP 402 with x402 requirements, then HTTP 200 with the data once an EIP-3009 USDC authorization is signed. Pays ~$0.0216 USDC via x402 on Base.
usage.outputShape: JSON object: body.address, body.chain_id, body.total_returned (int), body.sent_count, body.received_count, body.transactions[] each {hash, from, to, value_eth (number, ETH), timestamp (ISO), block_number, gas_used, is_error (bool), direction: "sent"|"received"}. Provenance/payment at body._meta {capability, latency_ms, provenance{source:"etherscan.io", fetched_at}, payment{method:"x402", settlement_id, price_usd}}. Verified live for 0xd8dA6BF...96045: total_returned 20, sent_count 2, received_count 18; first tx hash 0x3711e90ac3014fff2bd0dc39a94c3cd717700ec5768a1eec8ed5813fbf6be3fb, value_eth 0.00005, direction received.
quirks: address is required; chain_id defaults to 1 (Ethereum) and limit defaults to 20 (max 50) — all are query-string params, not a JSON body.
Data sourced from Etherscan V2 (body._meta.provenance.source = etherscan.io); supports Ethereum and other EVM chains by chain_id.
value_eth is the native-token amount in ETH; token/ERC-20 transfers show value_eth 0 (this endpoint reports native value + gas, not token amounts).
Synchronous: transactions are inline in the 200 body; no polling.
For balances use the sibling wallet-balance-lookup; for wallet age use wallet-age-check.
usage.guide: Fetch recent transactions for an EVM wallet from Strale. Call GET https://api.strale.io/x402/wallet-transactions-lookup with query params: address (required, the 0x... wallet), optional chain_id (default 1 = Ethereum), and optional limit (1-50, default 20). It is an x402 paid endpoint at ~$0.0216 USDC on Base (asset USDC 0x8335...2913, payTo 0x66D7...83bC): the first request returns 402 with payment requirements, and after signing an EIP-3009 USDC authorization it returns 200. Read the transactions from body.transactions[] (each has hash, from, to, value_eth, timestamp, block_number, gas_used, is_error, direction), with counts at body.total_returned/sent_count/received_count. Data is Etherscan-V2-sourced. value_eth is native ETH value only. For balances use wallet-balance-lookup; for wallet age use wallet-age-check.
